# Warrantor Native AI Platform OS — Implementation Plan (spine)

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Turn the master blueprint's Wave 1 spine into capabilities a user can reach from the `warrantor` command line, in dependency order, with every promoted claim backed by a live-run receipt rather than a test fixture.

**Architecture:** One product crate (`rust/warrant`, tokio-free, 7 path deps) consumes the spine crates; 71 of 80 workspace crates are orphaned from it. The plan wires the four unwired planes into the warrant path first (Rule 1), promotes bound labels only where a refusal is observed (Rule 2), composes isolation from mature projects rather than building it (Rule 3), ships the buyer-facing coverage and approval surfaces (Rule 4), and publishes the conformance profile inside the supervisory window (Rule 5).

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.94 workspace (`rust/`), `ed25519-dalek` 3, `sha2` 0.11, `serde_json`, `ureq` 2; Python 3.11 (`python/`, ruff); Electron desktop; GitHub Actions; `git commit -s` (DCO).

**Spec:** `aumos/docs/html/warrantor-native-ai-platform-os-master-2026-09-01.html` — Part 06 (kernel, effect syscalls, failure semantics), Part 07 (catalog items by L-id), Part 11 (rules, blockers, horizons, wave lists). Survey of the code this plan binds to: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-02-codebase-survey.md`.

## Global Constraints

- Repository: `M:/Project AumOS - Open Secure AI Alliance/aumos` is its own git repo (nested; the parent ignores it). Branch from `origin/main`, never from the dirty `docs/content-program-p9-fold` checkout. One git worktree per task (`git -C aumos worktree add M:/wt-<task> -b feat/<task> origin/main`). Merge one branch at a time after rebasing on main (PR CI tests against old main).
- Every commit: `git commit -s` (DCO trailer required by CI). Conventional commit prefixes.
- Rust gate before any commit: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`, all with `-j 2`, never piped through `head`; `protoc` must be installed; `cargo metadata --locked` must pass (never hand-edit `Cargo.lock` conflicts).
- Windows hazards: fork exhaustion corrupts the cache (full `cargo clean` only); use a separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree to avoid the registry lock race.
- `rust/warrant` stays tokio-free and dependency-minimal: no `tokio`, no `async fn`, no `clap`; any crate it consumes must be sync. `warrantor-kill-switch` cannot be linked as-is (it declares tokio unconditionally).
- Bound tiers are the honest core (`rust/warrant/src/lib.rs:635 bound_strengths()`): `Enforced` (OS/crypto), `Mediated` (MCP proxy), `Observed`. A label is promoted only after a refusal at the moment of action is observed in a test on every kernel the label claims. No rendering may collapse the three.
- The notary's `Verdict::Deny { gate }` carries only the gate, never the missing capability. Preserve.
- No new trust root: keys are pinned out of band; nothing fetches keys over a network.
- Formats are versioned strings (`warrantor.<name>/1`); a new format gets a new name, never a silent change; `warrantor verify` must dispatch on it.
- Python: type hints on every signature, ruff clean (`E,F,I,B,UP,SIM,RUF`, line 100); `aumos/ml/` launchers ≤ 60 lines.
- US English in all prose, docs and messages. Never cite SR 11-7 as current.
- Nothing in this plan is claimed built until a live run (not a fixture) produced the receipt; the delivery-gaps ledger (`docs/W1-delivery-gaps.md`) is updated in the same PR as the capability.

## Phase 0 — Repair the measuring instruments

### Task 0.1: Put `rust/reputation` under the workspace

Anchor (plan-brief.md, Part 11 blocker table and Rule 1): *"Progress was measured in items completed, which counts inventory rather than capability a user can reach"* — and L8-22 makes the count itself the product ("the share of effects in the estate that provably traverse the boundary, and the named remainder that do not"), so a crate the build cannot see is a crate the census cannot count.

**What the code actually shows (read 2026-09-02, all paths under `M:/Project AumOS - Open Secure AI Alliance/aumos`).** The survey's finding is true and understated. `rust/reputation/` (`Cargo.toml`, 17 lines; `src/lib.rs`, 318 lines) is not in `[workspace] members` of `rust/Cargo.toml` — and it is also **untracked**: `git status --porcelain rust/reputation` prints `?? rust/reputation/`, `git ls-files rust/reputation` prints nothing, and `git ls-tree origin/main rust/` has no `reputation` entry. It lives only on the disk of the dirty `docs/content-program-p9-fold` checkout, alongside ~45 other untracked crates (`agent-channel`, `agent-identity-graph`, `agent-registry`, ...) and an uncommitted `rust/Cargo.toml` (+45 member lines, 0 deletions — `git diff -U0 rust/Cargo.toml | grep -c '^+    "'` → `45`) and `rust/Cargo.lock` (+454 lines, 0 deletions). (`git status --porcelain rust/ | grep '^??'` prints 56 entries, 46 of them directories; the uncommitted manifest claims 45 of those directories as members, one of which is `reputation` itself.) `origin/main` (`26d16df`, 2026-08-31) has **38** members, not the 80 the survey counted from the working tree. Because every task branches from `origin/main` (Global Constraints), this task must *carry the crate in*, not merely list it. Reproduced in a scratch copy of `origin/main`'s `rust/` tree with the crate copied in: (a) before the member line, `cargo build -p warrantor-reputation` fails with `error: package ID specification \`warrantor-reputation\` did not match any packages`; (b) after the member line, `cargo metadata --locked` fails (`error: cannot update the lock file ... because --locked was passed to prevent this`) and a regeneration adds exactly one `[[package]]` block — no new third-party versions, because `hex 0.4.3`, `serde_json 1.0.151`, `sha2 0.11.0` and `digest 0.11.3` are already in `origin/main`'s lock; (c) **`cargo fmt --check` fails on the crate** with three reflows (`reputation_score` body, the `aggregate` signature, one `assert_eq!` in tests) — so "add the member line and push" would have gone red at the "Check formatting" step of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (lines 116-117); (d) after formatting, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean and the 14 unit tests pass.

**Decision: keep, do not remove.** The crate is the H-4 scorer that H-1 (`rust/agent-identity-graph/src/lib.rs`, itself untracked, line 26: *"does not compute reputation (that is H-4) — it links the events"*) defers to; it has no internal dependencies, reads no clock, and its tests are deterministic. Removing it deletes the only implementation of a documented contract. It stays a leaf: nothing in Phase 0 wires it, and it will correctly show as *orphaned* in Task 0.3's census.

**Non-goals, stated so nobody widens this task.** Do not reconcile the two `ReputationEvent` types (`warrantor_agent_identity_graph::ReputationEvent { kind, at_ms, digest }` vs `warrantor_reputation::ReputationEvent { kind, weight, at_ms, issuer_id, digest }`); H-1 is not on `origin/main` yet. Do not touch `rust/README.md`'s six-row crate table (it is a stale Wave-1 list, not a member registry). Do not fix the crate's doc links that point at file paths (`[\`ReputationEvent\`](rust/reputation/src/lib.rs)`); `cargo doc` is not in the gate.

- [ ] **Step 6 — Write the consumer-path test that could not have existed before, and watch it fail to build without the member line.**
  Create `rust/reputation/tests/public_api.rs`:
  ```rust
  //! A stranger recomputes an agent's standing from the serialized event record alone.
  //!
  //! The unit tests in `src/lib.rs` cover each function. This file exercises the crate the way a
  //! consumer would — through `warrantor_reputation::*` only — which is the path that did not exist
  //! while the crate sat outside the workspace: an integration target is compiled only by
  //! `cargo test --all-targets`, and only for workspace members.

  use warrantor_reputation::{
      aggregate, verify_event, ReputationEvent, ReputationPolicy, ReputationReport, TrustTier,
  };

  const ONE_DAY_MS: u64 = 86_400_000;

  fn policy() -> ReputationPolicy {
      ReputationPolicy {
          half_life_ms: ONE_DAY_MS,
          floor: -100,
          ceil: 100,
          high_at: 50,
          medium_at: 20,
          low_at: 1,
      }
  }

  #[test]
  fn a_stranger_recomputes_the_same_standing_from_the_serialized_record() {
      let issued = vec![
          ReputationEvent::new("clean_audit", 40, 0, "auditor-a"),
          ReputationEvent::new("clean_audit", 30, ONE_DAY_MS, "auditor-b"),
          ReputationEvent::new("violation", -5, 2 * ONE_DAY_MS, "auditor-a"),
      ];
      let now_ms = 2 * ONE_DAY_MS;
      let report_at_issuer = aggregate(&issued, &policy(), now_ms);

      let record = serde_json::to_string(&issued).expect("events serialize");
      let received: Vec<ReputationEvent> = serde_json::from_str(&record).expect("events deserialize");
      assert!(received.iter().all(verify_event));
      let report_at_stranger = aggregate(&received, &policy(), now_ms);

      assert_eq!(report_at_stranger, report_at_issuer);
      // 40 two half-lives old -> 10; 30 one half-life old -> 15; -5 fresh -> -5; sum 20 -> Medium.
      assert_eq!(
          report_at_stranger,
          ReputationReport {
              score: 20,
              tier: TrustTier::Medium,
              contributing: 3,
              decayed_away: 0,
              total: 3,
          }
      );
  }

  #[test]
  fn a_tampered_record_fails_verification_before_it_is_scored() {
      let issued = vec![ReputationEvent::new("violation", -60, 0, "auditor-a")];
      let record = serde_json::to_string(&issued).expect("events serialize");
      // An agent laundering its own record: flip the sign of a violation in transit.
      let laundered = record.replace("\"weight\":-60", "\"weight\":60");
      assert_ne!(laundered, record, "the fixture must change the wire form");
      let received: Vec<ReputationEvent> =
          serde_json::from_str(&laundered).expect("a laundered record still parses");
      assert!(!verify_event(&received[0]));
      assert_eq!(
          received[0].weight, 60,
          "the digest, not the parser, is what catches it"
      );
  }
  ```
  To see it fail for the right reason, run it against the pre-fix state once: `git stash push rust/Cargo.toml rust/Cargo.lock` is not available (they are committed now), so instead temporarily comment out the `"reputation",` line, run `cargo test -p warrantor-reputation --test public_api -j 2`, expect `error: package ID specification \`warrantor-reputation\` did not match any packages`, and restore the line — then:
  ```bash
  git checkout -- rust/Cargo.lock
  cargo metadata --format-version 1 --locked > /dev/null && git status --porcelain rust/Cargo.lock   # expected: empty
  ```
  The `git checkout` is not optional bookkeeping. No `--locked` is passed on that deliberate-failure run, so cargo rewrites `Cargo.lock` — dropping the `warrantor-reputation` package block Step 5 just committed — *before* it fails on the `-p` package spec. Without the restore you are left holding a modified committed file whose one purpose was the block that was just deleted. (This is the same failure as Step 2, now observed through the target that CI's `--all-targets` will build.)

**Merge note (concurrent-session hazard).** The dirty checkout's uncommitted `rust/Cargo.toml` adds 45 member lines after the same `"misinformation-defense",` anchor (working-tree lines 42-86, `]` at 87), **and one of them is `"reputation",` itself, at line 84** — between `"agent-registry",` (83) and `"conformance",` (85). So when that batch lands, `rust/Cargo.toml` will conflict textually and the resolution is: **take THEIR side of the member block whole and drop ours.** Never "keep both sides" — that yields a `members` array containing `"reputation",` twice. (Cargo tolerates the duplicate — `cargo metadata --format-version 1` still exits 0 — so this is a tidiness defect that will pass the gate silently rather than a build break, which is exactly why it has to be caught at the merge.) `rust/Cargo.lock` will conflict too: resolve the lock by taking either side and running `cargo metadata --format-version 1`, then `--locked` to prove it — never by hand-merging hunks.

**Acceptance.** `cargo test -p warrantor-reputation --all-targets` runs 16 tests (14 unit + 2 integration) inside a worktree cut from `origin/main`; `cargo metadata --locked` passes; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes with the crate in the workspace; `docs/W1-delivery-gaps.md` §0.3 exists in the same PR; Task 0.3's first census counts the crate as *orphaned* (present, unreachable), which is the honest label until something consumes it.

Its **line 3** — one line, not two — reads `` # `rust-version = "1.85"` in rust/Cargo.toml declares the floor and cargo enforces it. This file is ``, while `rust/Cargo.toml:112` says `rust-version = "1.94"`. The `#[cfg(windows)]` surface this leg gates: `rust/warrant/src/supervise.rs` (job object at `:316-444`, `terminate_group` via `taskkill /T /F` at `:221-241`, `spawn_detached` creation flags at `:272-281`), `rust/warrant/src/daemon.rs:416-440` (`process_is_alive` via `tasklist.exe`), `rust/warrant/src/serve.rs:4414` (`SetConsoleCtrlHandler`), `rust/warrant/src/lock.rs` (no cfg gates, but its whole mechanism is `create_new` at `:150-153` and `remove_file` in `Drop` at `:85`, whose semantics differ on NTFS and have never run in CI), and `rust/kill-switch/src/execution.rs` (`reserved_pid_reason` `:283-306`, `critical_image_cached` `:442-460`, `process_exists` `:505-541`, `system32_tool` `:648-652`, `force_terminate` `:654-700`). Verified on the Windows box while writing this section — **two filtered subsets only, not the leg**: `cargo test --locked -p warrantor-kill-switch --lib ax05 -j 2` (fresh `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`) gave `test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed ... finished in 5.53s`, including `local_process_engine_actually_kills_a_real_process_ax05` and `the_critical_image_rail_is_consulted_once_per_kill_ax05`; and `cargo test --locked -p warrantor-warrant --test store_lock -j 2` gave `5 passed; 0 failed ... finished in 0.10s`, so the `create_new`/`remove_file` lock mechanism holds on NTFS. That is 18 tests. The Windows leg this task adds runs `cargo test -p warrantor-warrant -p warrantor-kill-switch --all-targets -j 2 -- --test-threads=2`, which is the 35 integration-test files under `rust/warrant/tests/` (`daemon.rs`, `stop.rs`, `serve_socket.rs`, `proxy.rs`, `worktree_commit.rs`, ...), the 150 `#[test]` attributes under `rust/warrant/src/` (by `grep -rc '#\[test\]' rust/warrant/src/`), and the whole kill-switch lib plus its bin build — **none of which has been run on Windows yet**. So the memory note's precondition ("verify the full workspace passes on Windows first — adding a leg that fails turns `main` red, which is worse than the gap") is *not* yet established; Step 5 establishes it with a full `--all-targets` run of both crates on this box, with the pass counts recorded in the log, before the leg is pushed. `fail-fast: false` plus `required` would catch a red leg on the PR, but the PR is not the place to discover it.

**Why the Windows leg tests two crates, not `--workspace`.** `cargo tree -p warrantor-warrant -p warrantor-kill-switch` contains no `wasmtime`/`cranelift` crate; the full workspace does, and `cranelift-codegen 0.134.3` overflows rustc's default thread stack on Windows (`STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN`, needs `RUST_MIN_STACK=33554432`). Widening the Windows leg to the whole workspace is this task's recorded residual, not its scope. `protoc` is still required on the Windows leg: `cargo tree -p warrantor-warrant -i warrantor-api` shows `warrantor-api` (whose `build.rs` runs `tonic-build`) reached through both `warrantor-authority-spec` and `warrantor-trust-core`.

**Why the Windows leg caps two different kinds of concurrency.** `cargo`'s `-j` caps *build* jobs only — it is passed to the compilation graph and has no effect on what a test binary does once it starts. Under `-j 2` alone, libtest still runs each binary's tests on as many threads as there are logical CPUs, and these are exactly the tests that spawn `cmd.exe`, `ping.exe`, `tasklist.exe`, `taskkill.exe` and `powershell.exe` — the process-table pressure that this platform has failed under before is a *test-time* property, so `-j` does not address it. The leg therefore carries both: `-j 2` bounds compilation (cranelift and the tonic build script are the memory-hungry ones), and `-- --test-threads=2` bounds the spawning tests. Every local reproduction in Steps 3 and 5 uses the same pair, so the box runs what the runner runs.

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the three tests.** Append to `rust/warrant/src/supervise.rs` after line 444 (the crate carries `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` and `#![deny(missing_docs)]` at `lib.rs:32-33`; this module uses neither `unsafe` nor public items):
  ```rust
  #[cfg(test)]
  mod tests {
      use super::*;

      /// `describe_linkage` and the `cfg` gates in this module must agree about the platform this
      /// binary was compiled for; a mismatch would report a link that is not the one in force.
      #[test]
      fn describe_linkage_names_the_mechanism_this_binary_was_compiled_for() {
          let linkage = describe_linkage();
          if cfg!(windows) {
              assert_eq!(linkage.mechanism, "job-object");
              assert!(linkage.survives_supervisor_death);
          } else if cfg!(target_os = "linux") {
              assert_eq!(linkage.mechanism, "setsid+pdeathsig");
              assert!(linkage.survives_supervisor_death);
          } else {
              assert_eq!(linkage.mechanism, "setsid");
              assert!(!linkage.survives_supervisor_death);
          }
      }

      /// A two-level tree: `cmd.exe /C ping -n 60 127.0.0.1 >NUL` -- cmd is the child, ping the
      /// grandchild. Only the tree shape matters; the redirect keeps ping's output out of the log.
      #[cfg(windows)]
      const TREE_ARGS: [&str; 6] = ["/C", "ping", "-n", "60", "127.0.0.1", ">NUL"];

      #[cfg(windows)]
      fn tree_args() -> Vec<String> {
          TREE_ARGS.iter().map(|arg| (*arg).to_string()).collect()
      }

      /// Poll `process_is_alive` for up to `budget`; true when the pid went away in time.
      #[cfg(windows)]
      fn gone_within(pid: u32, budget: std::time::Duration) -> bool {
          let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + budget;
          while std::time::Instant::now() < deadline {
              if !crate::daemon::process_is_alive(pid) {
                  return true;
              }
              std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));
          }
          !crate::daemon::process_is_alive(pid)
      }

      /// The `ping.exe` children of `parent`, via CIM. `wmic` is gone from current Windows images;
      /// `powershell.exe` is on every supported one. The image-name filter matters: when the test
      /// process has no attached console (a CI runner leg is one such case) `cmd.exe` allocates one
      /// and a `conhost.exe` appears with cmd's pid as `ParentProcessId`; without the filter the
      /// "grandchild" under test could be conhost, which dies with its client and would prove
      /// nothing about `/T`. WQL string comparison is case-insensitive; the doubled `''` is
      /// PowerShell's escape for a single quote inside a single-quoted string, so no double quote
      /// has to survive `Command`'s argument quoting.
      #[cfg(windows)]
      fn ping_pids_under(parent: u32) -> Vec<u32> {
          let query = format!(
              "(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter 'ParentProcessId={parent} AND Name=''PING.EXE''').ProcessId"
          );
          let output = Command::new("powershell")
              .args(["-NoProfile", "-Command", &query])
              .stdin(Stdio::null())
              .output()
              .expect("powershell.exe is present on every supported Windows");
          String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout)
              .lines()
              .filter_map(|line| line.trim().parse::<u32>().ok())
              .collect()
      }

      /// `cmd.exe` needs a moment to start `ping`; wait for the ping grandchild specifically.
      #[cfg(windows)]
      fn grandchild_of(parent: u32) -> u32 {
          for _ in 0..50 {
              if let Some(pid) = ping_pids_under(parent).first().copied() {
                  return pid;
              }
              std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));
          }
          panic!("cmd.exe {parent} never started ping.exe");
      }

      /// The kill-on-close link is the whole promise of this module on Windows: closing the job
      /// handle -- which `Drop` does on a tidy exit, a panic and a crash alike -- must take the
      /// grandchild with it, not only the process that was assigned to the job.
      #[cfg(windows)]
      #[test]
      fn job_object_kills_the_child_tree_when_the_supervisor_drops() {
          let mut supervisor = Supervisor::new().expect("job object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE");
          let pid = supervisor
              .spawn("cmd.exe", &tree_args(), None)
              .expect("spawn cmd.exe inside the job");
          let grandchild = grandchild_of(pid);
          assert!(crate::daemon::process_is_alive(pid));
          assert!(crate::daemon::process_is_alive(grandchild));

          // `Job` is dropped before `child` (field order), and its `CloseHandle` is the kill.
          drop(supervisor);

          let budget = std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);
          assert!(
              gone_within(pid, budget),
              "cmd.exe {pid} survived the job handle closing"
          );
          assert!(
              gone_within(grandchild, budget),
              "ping {grandchild} (grandchild) survived the job handle closing"
          );
      }

      /// `terminate_group` is what `stop` reaches for; on Windows it is `taskkill /T /F`, and the
      /// `/T` is the claim under test.
      #[cfg(windows)]
      #[test]
      fn terminate_group_kills_the_grandchild_too() {
          let mut child = Command::new("cmd.exe")
              .args(TREE_ARGS)
              .stdin(Stdio::null())
              .spawn()
              .expect("spawn cmd.exe");
          let pid = child.id();
          let grandchild = grandchild_of(pid);

          terminate_group(pid);

          let budget = std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);
          assert!(gone_within(pid, budget), "cmd.exe {pid} survived taskkill /T");
          assert!(
              gone_within(grandchild, budget),
              "ping {grandchild} (grandchild) survived taskkill /T"
          );
          let _ = child.wait();
      }
  }
  ```

### Task 0.3: Orphan census as a ratcheting CI number (seed of L8-22)

**Anchor (plan-brief.md, Part 11 "Wire before widen" and L8-22):** "The correct progress metric is capabilities a user can reach, not items completed" — and L8-22 wants that metric published as "the share of effects in the estate that provably traverse the boundary, and the named remainder that do not," with the verification gate "adding an unmediated harness lowers the number visibly." This task builds the crate-level seed of that number: how many workspace crates the `warrantor` binary actually links, recorded in a versioned file, gated so it can only rise, and rendered in the README where a buyer reads it.

**What the code says today (verified 2026-09-02 against `origin/main` = 26d16df, the ref Step 1 branches from; identical in HEAD 834db38).** `rust/Cargo.toml` lines 3–42 declare 38 `[workspace] members` (the list closes at line 42; `exclude = [` follows at 43). Exactly 17 `path = "../…"` dependency edges exist across 10 dependents, every one of them under a plain `[dependencies]` table (no dev-, build- or target-conditional path deps anywhere): `warrant` → 7 (`rust/warrant/Cargo.toml` lines 26–56), `archive` → 2, and eight crates with one edge each (`authority-spec`, `trust-core`, `nvtrust-bridge`, `eval-guard`, `flight-recorder` → `warrantor-api`; `gguf-ext`, `sandbox-runtime`, `secure-workspace` → `trust-core`). Reachable from `warrantor-warrant`: `warrantor-warrant`, `warrantor-trust-core`, `warrantor-authority-spec`, `warrantor-evidence`, `warrantor-notary`, `warrantor-egress`, `warrantor-containment-conformance`, `warrantor-spend`, `warrantor-api` — 9 of 38; the other 29 are orphans, and sorted by package name the list begins `defstack-cli`, `warrantor-agent-manifest`. **Why the survey says something else:** survey §2.5 ("13 path-dependency edges", "71 of 80") was measured in the dirty `docs/content-program-p9-fold` checkout, where 42 extra members (`task-validity` … `agent-registry`), their directories and `rust/reputation` exist only as uncommitted, untracked edits — 54 untracked `rust/*` directories; `git ls-tree origin/main rust/task-validity/` is empty. The Global Constraints say never to branch from that checkout, so this task states the `origin/main` numbers and the tests below pin them. If those 42 crates are committed to `main` before this branch merges, rebase, rerun `python tools/ci/wiring_census.py --write`, and carry the new `total`/`orphaned`/`edges` into the README row and the ledger entry — the reachable set itself (9 crates) does not change, because none of the uncommitted crates are linked by `warrant`. Every package is named `warrantor-<dir>` except `defstack-cli` (dir `defstack-cli`) and `warrantor-api` (dir `warrantor-api`), so the census keys on `[package].name` resolved through the `path` value, never on directory names. One blocker found in the tree: `.gitignore` line 92 is `/evidence/`, a directory ignore, and git cannot re-include a file whose parent directory is excluded — so the record cannot be committed at the stub's path until that line becomes `/evidence/*` with a negation (verified with a scratch repository: `git add -A` then stages `evidence/wiring-coverage.json` and nothing else under `evidence/`). The workflow runs with `permissions: contents: read` (ci.yml line 10–11) and no workflow in `.github/workflows/` commits or pushes, so "rewrites the file on push-to-main" is implemented the way every other `evidence/*.json` in ci.yml is: written in the runner and uploaded as an artifact (lines 166–172 pattern), while the committed copy is the floor a pull request must not drop below.

```python
RECORD_FORMAT = "warrantor.wiring-coverage/1"
BINARY_CRATE = "warrantor-warrant"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WiringCensus:
    total: int
    reachable: int
    orphaned: list[str]
    edges: int

def workspace_members(workspace_root: Path) -> list[Path]
def package_name(crate_dir: Path) -> str
def shipping_path_dependencies(crate_dir: Path) -> list[Path]
def dependency_graph(workspace_root: Path) -> dict[str, set[str]]
def reachable_crates(workspace_root: Path, binary_crate: str = BINARY_CRATE) -> set[str]
def census(workspace_root: Path, binary_crate: str = BINARY_CRATE) -> WiringCensus
def render_record(result: WiringCensus, binary_crate: str) -> dict[str, object]
def load_floor(path: Path) -> int
def readme_renders(readme: Path, result: WiringCensus) -> bool
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int
```
CLI: `python tools/ci/wiring_census.py [--workspace P] [--binary-crate NAME] [--floor P] [--readme P] [--write]`. Without `--write` it is the gate: exit 1 if `reachable < floor` or the README does not render `reachable from the CLI | **<reachable> of <total>**`; a `::notice::` (exit 0) if `reachable > floor`. With `--write` it rewrites the record.

**Design decisions this section fixes:**
- *Manifests, not `cargo metadata`.* The gate must run on a checkout with no cargo, no protoc and no network, in seconds, and the question is "what does the manifest link", which the manifest answers directly. `cargo metadata --locked` already runs at ci.yml line 115 and will keep catching lock drift; this script deliberately does not depend on it.
- *Only `[dependencies]` (and `[target.*.dependencies]`) count.* A crate reachable only through `[dev-dependencies]` is precisely "tested in isolation, called by nothing"; counting it would let a test import masquerade as a wiring. `[build-dependencies]` run on the build host and ship nothing.
- *Ratchet is `>=`, not `==`.* A pull request that wires a crate passes with a notice and is expected to commit the raised record in the same PR (the same-PR rule the Global Constraints already impose on the delivery-gaps ledger); a pull request that unwires one fails. Push-to-main regenerates and uploads the record so the artifact never lags the tree even if a PR forgot the bump.
- *The README is gated too.* The acceptance criterion is a rendered number; a number that can drift from the file it cites is the exact failure Task 0.4 fixes for the bounds table. `readme_renders` makes the row part of the test surface.
- *The record is versioned* (`warrantor.wiring-coverage/1`); a record in any other format is refused, never coerced.

  ```python
  #!/usr/bin/env python3
  """Count the workspace crates the `warrantor` binary can reach, and refuse to let it fall.

  The progress metric this repository has learned to distrust is "crates completed". The one it
  trusts is "crates a user can reach from the command line", because a crate that nothing links is
  a test suite, not a capability. This script measures the second number from the manifests alone
  (no cargo, no protoc, no network), records it in a versioned JSON file, and fails CI when a change
  would lower it. It can only go up: that is the ratchet.
  """

  from __future__ import annotations

  import argparse
  import json
  import sys
  import tomllib
  from collections import deque
  from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
  from pathlib import Path

  REPOSITORY_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
  WORKSPACE_ROOT = REPOSITORY_ROOT / "rust"
  FLOOR_PATH = REPOSITORY_ROOT / "evidence" / "wiring-coverage.json"
  README_PATH = REPOSITORY_ROOT / "README.md"
  BINARY_CRATE = "warrantor-warrant"
  RECORD_FORMAT = "warrantor.wiring-coverage/1"

  # Only `[dependencies]` (and its per-target form) puts code into the binary a user runs.
  # `[dev-dependencies]` compile for tests and `[build-dependencies]` run on the build host; a crate
  # reachable only through those is exactly the "tested in isolation, called by nothing" case this
  # census exists to count as orphaned.
  SHIPPING_TABLE = "dependencies"


  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  class WiringCensus:
      """One measurement of the workspace."""

      total: int
      reachable: int
      orphaned: list[str]
      edges: int


  def read_manifest(path: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
      """Parse one Cargo.toml."""

      with path.open("rb") as handle:
          return tomllib.load(handle)


  def workspace_members(workspace_root: Path) -> list[Path]:
      """Every member directory the workspace manifest declares, resolved."""

      manifest = read_manifest(workspace_root / "Cargo.toml")
      workspace = manifest.get("workspace")
      if not isinstance(workspace, dict) or not isinstance(workspace.get("members"), list):
          raise ValueError(f"{workspace_root / 'Cargo.toml'} declares no [workspace] members")
      return [(workspace_root / member).resolve() for member in workspace["members"]]


  def package_name(crate_dir: Path) -> str:
      """The `[package].name` of a crate, which is what dependency edges are keyed on."""

      manifest = read_manifest(crate_dir / "Cargo.toml")
      package = manifest.get("package")
      if not isinstance(package, dict) or not isinstance(package.get("name"), str):
          raise ValueError(f"{crate_dir / 'Cargo.toml'} has no [package].name")
      return package["name"]


  def shipping_path_dependencies(crate_dir: Path) -> list[Path]:
      """Resolved directories of every `path = ...` entry in the crate's shipping tables."""

      manifest = read_manifest(crate_dir / "Cargo.toml")
      tables: list[object] = [manifest.get(SHIPPING_TABLE, {})]
      targets = manifest.get("target", {})
      if isinstance(targets, dict):
          for target_table in targets.values():
              if isinstance(target_table, dict):
                  tables.append(target_table.get(SHIPPING_TABLE, {}))
      found: list[Path] = []
      for table in tables:
          if not isinstance(table, dict):
              continue
          for spec in table.values():
              if isinstance(spec, dict) and isinstance(spec.get("path"), str):
                  found.append((crate_dir / spec["path"]).resolve())
      return found


  def dependency_graph(workspace_root: Path) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
      """Package name -> the workspace package names it links into its shipping build."""

      names = {crate_dir: package_name(crate_dir) for crate_dir in workspace_members(workspace_root)}
      graph: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
      for crate_dir, name in names.items():
          graph[name] = {
              names[dependency]
              for dependency in shipping_path_dependencies(crate_dir)
              if dependency in names
          }
      return graph


  def reachable_crates(workspace_root: Path, binary_crate: str = BINARY_CRATE) -> set[str]:
      """Package names reachable from `binary_crate` over shipping path edges, itself included."""

      graph = dependency_graph(workspace_root)
      if binary_crate not in graph:
          raise KeyError(f"{binary_crate!r} is not a member of the workspace at {workspace_root}")
      seen = {binary_crate}
      queue: deque[str] = deque([binary_crate])
      while queue:
          for dependency in graph[queue.popleft()]:
              if dependency not in seen:
                  seen.add(dependency)
                  queue.append(dependency)
      return seen
  ```

  Run pytest. Expected: `5 failed, 4 passed`, each failure `NotImplementedError`. Replace the three remaining stubs and add the record/argument helpers:
  ```python
  def render_record(result: WiringCensus, binary_crate: str) -> dict[str, object]:
      """The committed record: a versioned format, the number, and the named remainder."""

      return {"format": RECORD_FORMAT, "binary_crate": binary_crate, **asdict(result)}


  def load_floor(path: Path) -> int:
      """Read the recorded `reachable` count, refusing any record in an unknown format."""

      record = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
      if record.get("format") != RECORD_FORMAT:
          raise ValueError(f"{path}: format {record.get('format')!r} is not {RECORD_FORMAT}")
      return int(record["reachable"])


  def readme_renders(readme: Path, result: WiringCensus) -> bool:
      """True when the README status table shows the current number."""

      expected = f"reachable from the CLI | **{result.reachable} of {result.total}**"
      return expected in readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


  def parse_arguments(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
      """Parse command-line arguments."""

      parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
      parser.add_argument("--workspace", type=Path, default=WORKSPACE_ROOT)
      parser.add_argument("--binary-crate", default=BINARY_CRATE)
      parser.add_argument("--floor", type=Path, default=FLOOR_PATH)
      parser.add_argument("--readme", type=Path, default=README_PATH)
      parser.add_argument("--write", action="store_true", help="rewrite the floor record")
      return parser.parse_args(argv)


  def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
      """Measure, then either record or gate."""

      arguments = parse_arguments(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
      result = census(arguments.workspace, arguments.binary_crate)
      print(
          f"wiring census: {result.reachable} of {result.total} crates reachable from "
          f"{arguments.binary_crate} over {result.edges} path edges"
      )
      if arguments.write:
          arguments.floor.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
          record = render_record(result, arguments.binary_crate)
          arguments.floor.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
          print(f"evidence: {arguments.floor}")
          return 0
      floor = load_floor(arguments.floor)
      if result.reachable < floor:
          print(
              f"::error::wiring ratchet: {result.reachable} reachable is below the recorded floor "
              f"of {floor} in {arguments.floor}; a crate was unwired from {arguments.binary_crate}"
          )
          return 1
      if result.reachable > floor:
          print(
              f"::notice::wiring ratchet: {result.reachable} reachable exceeds the floor of {floor}; "
              f"run `python tools/ci/wiring_census.py --write` and commit {arguments.floor}"
          )
      if not readme_renders(arguments.readme, result):
          print(
              "::error::README status table does not show "
              f"'reachable from the CLI | **{result.reachable} of {result.total}**'"
          )
          return 1
      return 0


  if __name__ == "__main__":
      raise SystemExit(main())
  ```

### Task 0.4: Tier disclosure lint across report, status and console (L8-13, partial → tested)

**Anchor (plan-brief.md, L8-13 Coverage disclosure surface):** "Every surface that renders a guarantee also renders what that guarantee does not cover, per harness and per bound strength … The bundle self-discloses tier per bound; a rendering that omits the tier fails the release gate … Blueprint proof gate (H-04): No rendering collapses observed, advisory, mediated and enforced into one status."

**What the code does today, and the three defects this task closes.** `bound_strengths()` (`rust/warrant/src/lib.rs:635`) is the single honest source. `report::render_cli` prints one lowercase word per bound and is pinned byte-for-byte by `the_prose_report_is_exactly_what_it_always_was` (`tests/report.rs:145`). The signed bundle copies the list verbatim (`tests/report.rs:706`).
```rust
//! Tier disclosure: every surface that renders a bound renders its tier, and no surface prints
//! "enforced" for a bound `bound_strengths()` calls Observed. L8-13.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
use serde_json::Value;
use warrantor_warrant::report::{build, render_cli, render_mcp};
use warrantor_warrant::serve::{no_adapter, route, status, HttpRequest, StoreApi};
use warrantor_warrant::staging::{EffectRegistry, StagingQueue};
use warrantor_warrant::store::{StoredWarrant, WarrantStore};
use warrantor_warrant::{
    bound_strengths, render_bound, render_bounds_table, render_tier_legend, BoundStrength,
    SideEffectClass, Warrant, WarrantBounds,
};

const NOW: u64 = 1_786_000_000;
fn now() -> u64 {
    NOW
}
const TOKEN: &str = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef";
const TIERS: [BoundStrength; 3] = [
    BoundStrength::Enforced,
    BoundStrength::Mediated,
    BoundStrength::Observed,
];

fn tempdir(tag: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
    let mut path = std::env::temp_dir();
    path.push(format!(
        "warrantor-tier-{tag}-{}",
        std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
            .unwrap_or(0)
    ));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&path).expect("tempdir");
    path
}

fn issuer() -> SigningKey {
    SigningKey::from_bytes(&[1; 32])
}

fn stored(id: &str, expires_at: u64) -> StoredWarrant {
    let bounds = WarrantBounds {
        tools: ["git".to_string()].into_iter().collect(),
        write_paths: ["src/**".to_string()].into_iter().collect(),
        egress_hosts: BTreeSet::new(),
        staged_classes: [SideEffectClass::Write].into_iter().collect(),
        expires_at,
        budget_cents_observed: Some(500),
        delegation_depth: 1,
    };
    let warrant = Warrant::grant(
        id,
        "fix the auth bug",
        "spiffe://muveraai.com/agent/a",
        bounds,
        NOW,
        &SigningKey::from_bytes(&[2; 32]).verifying_key(),
        &issuer(),
    )
    .expect("grant");
    StoredWarrant {
        warrant,
        worktree: None,
        repo: None,
        branch: None,
        base_commit: None,
        staged_chain: None,
    }
}

/// The word a surface prints is the word the wire carries. One vocabulary, checked by machine.
#[test]
fn the_tier_word_is_the_serde_name_for_every_variant() {
    for tier in TIERS {
        let wire = serde_json::to_value(tier).expect("serialize");
        assert_eq!(wire, Value::String(tier.word().to_string()), "{tier:?}");
    }
    assert_eq!(BoundStrength::Observed.word(), "observed");
    assert_eq!(BoundStrength::Mediated.word(), "mediated");
    assert_eq!(BoundStrength::Enforced.word(), "enforced");
}

/// The caveat is the half of L8-13 nothing rendered before: what the tier does NOT cover.
#[test]
fn every_tier_states_what_it_does_not_cover_and_the_weaker_two_never_say_enforced() {
    for tier in TIERS {
        assert!(tier.caveat().len() > 20, "{tier:?} has no caveat");
    }
    assert!(BoundStrength::Mediated.caveat().contains("traverse"));
    assert!(BoundStrength::Observed.caveat().contains("nothing refuses"));
    for tier in [BoundStrength::Mediated, BoundStrength::Observed] {
        assert!(
            !tier.caveat().contains("enforced"),
            "{tier:?} must not describe itself with the strongest word"
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
impl BoundStrength {
    /// The stable wire word for this tier. Equal to its serde name, and pinned equal by
    /// `tests/tier_disclosure.rs`, so a surface that prints the word and a client that reads the
    /// JSON are reading one vocabulary.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn word(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Enforced => "enforced",
            Self::Mediated => "mediated",
            Self::Observed => "observed",
        }
    }

    /// What this tier does NOT cover, in one clause. The half of a disclosure a reader skims past:
    /// a tier word alone is read as the strongest thing it could mean.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn caveat(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Enforced => {
                "held by cryptography or the operating system; holds against an agent that tries \
                 to route around it"
            }
            Self::Mediated => {
                "held only for calls that traverse the MCP proxy; a shell or a harness built-in \
                 reaches past it, and no netns, seccomp or firewall stands behind it"
            }
            Self::Observed => {
                "measured and reported after the fact; nothing refuses the action as it happens"
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
/// `render_bound` is the one formatter. Its output is what the CLI golden has always pinned:
/// the name padded to 24 columns, then the word.
#[test]
fn render_bound_pads_the_name_and_prints_exactly_the_tier_word() {
    assert_eq!(
        render_bound("write_paths", BoundStrength::Observed),
        "write_paths             observed"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        render_bound("expires_at", BoundStrength::Enforced),
        "expires_at              enforced"
    );
    for (name, strength) in bound_strengths() {
        let line = render_bound(name, strength);
        assert!(line.ends_with(strength.word()), "{line}");
        if strength != BoundStrength::Enforced {
            assert!(!line.contains("enforced"), "{line}");
        }
    }
}

/// The legend renders all three tiers, in strength order, each with its caveat.
#[test]
fn the_legend_names_all_three_tiers_and_never_collapses_them() {
    let legend = render_tier_legend();
    assert_eq!(legend.len(), 3);
    for (line, tier) in legend.iter().zip(TIERS) {
        assert!(line.starts_with(tier.word()), "{line}");
        assert!(line.contains(tier.caveat()), "{line}");
    }
    let distinct: BTreeSet<&String> = legend.iter().collect();
    assert_eq!(distinct.len(), 3, "three tiers, three different lines");
}
```

Then add to `lib.rs`, directly after `bound_strengths()` (after line 653):

```rust
/// One bound, one line, the way every surface prints it: the name padded to 24 columns and the
/// tier word. The CLI report, the MCP report, `warrantor status` and the README table all call
/// this, so the four cannot spell a tier four ways again.
#[must_use]
pub fn render_bound(name: &str, strength: BoundStrength) -> String {
    format!("{name:<24}{}", strength.word())
}

/// The three tiers, strongest first, each with what it does not cover.
///
/// Printed under every bounds block. A column of one-word marks is read by taking the first word
/// and moving on; the legend is what stops "mediated" being read as "enforced with extra steps".
#[must_use]
pub fn render_tier_legend() -> Vec<String> {
    [
        BoundStrength::Enforced,
        BoundStrength::Mediated,
        BoundStrength::Observed,
    ]
    .into_iter()
    .map(|tier| format!("{:<10}{}", tier.word(), tier.caveat()))
    .collect()
}

/// The README bounds table, generated from [`bound_strengths`] so the prose cannot drift from
/// the code again. `tests/tier_disclosure.rs` asserts both READMEs contain this string verbatim.
#[must_use]
pub fn render_bounds_table() -> String {
    let mut rows = vec![
        "| Bound | Tier | What the tier does not cover |".to_string(),
        "|---|---|---|".to_string(),
    ];
    rows.extend(bound_strengths().into_iter().map(|(name, strength)| {
        format!("| `{name}` | {} | {} |", strength.word(), strength.caveat())
    }));
    rows.join("\n")
}
```

```rust
/// `GET /v1/warrants/{id}` carries, per bound, the tier word `bound_strengths()` assigns and the
/// caveat for that tier, plus the legend. A client never has to infer a tier from a boolean.
#[test]
fn the_console_json_carries_the_tier_word_and_caveat_per_bound() {
    let dir = tempdir("json");
    WarrantStore::open(&dir)
        .expect("store")
        .save(&stored("wrt_json", NOW + 3600))
        .expect("save");
    let mut api = api(&dir);
    let request = HttpRequest::new("GET", &["v1", "warrants", "wrt_json"], BTreeMap::new())
        .with_bearer(TOKEN);
    let response = route(&mut api, &request);
    assert_eq!(response.status, status::OK);

    let expected: BTreeMap<&str, BoundStrength> = bound_strengths().into_iter().collect();
    let listed = response.body["data"]["bound_strengths"]
        .as_array()
        .expect("bound_strengths is an array");
    assert_eq!(listed.len(), expected.len());
    for entry in listed {
        let name = entry["name"].as_str().expect("name");
        let tier = expected[name];
        assert_eq!(entry["strength"], Value::String(tier.word().to_string()), "{name}");
        assert_eq!(entry["caveat"], Value::String(tier.caveat().to_string()), "{name}");
        if tier == BoundStrength::Observed {
            assert_ne!(entry["strength"], "enforced", "{name}");
        }
    }
    let legend = response.body["data"]["tier_legend"]
        .as_array()
        .expect("tier_legend");
    assert_eq!(legend.len(), 3);
}
```

```javascript
/** The three tier words the server may send. Anything else is "not stated", never rounded up. */
const TIER_WORDS = new Set(['enforced', 'mediated', 'observed']);

/**
 * One line per bound: name, tier word, and the server's caveat for that tier. Exported and pure so
 * `console.test.js` can pin the shape. An unknown or missing tier is rendered as "not stated" —
 * the console composes no tier of its own, and the one word it must never supply is "enforced".
 */
export function boundTierLines(data) {
  const list = data?.bound_strengths;
  if (!Array.isArray(list)) return [];
  return list.map((entry) => {
    const name = typeof entry?.name === 'string' ? entry.name : '(unnamed bound)';
    if (!TIER_WORDS.has(entry?.strength)) {
      return `${name} — tier not stated: do not read this as enforced`;
    }
    const caveat = typeof entry.caveat === 'string' ? entry.caveat : '';
    return `${name} — ${entry.strength}: ${caveat}`;
  });
}
```

Create `tools/ci/check_invariants.py`:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fail-closed checker for the invariant ledger at evidence/invariants.json.

The ledger is the honest label for I-01..I-12. Every entry names the tests that
observe a refusal; this checker refuses a ledger whose tests do not exist, whose
statements drift from docs/02-architecture.md, or whose status disagrees with
where its evidence lives.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import cast

REPOSITORY_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
LEDGER_RELATIVE_PATH = Path("evidence") / "invariants.json"
ARCHITECTURE_RELATIVE_PATH = Path("docs") / "02-architecture.md"
LEDGER_FORMAT = "warrantor.invariant-ledger/1"
ALLOWED_STATUSES = frozenset({"enforced", "partial", "orphaned", "unimplemented"})
EXPECTED_IDS = tuple(f"I-{number:02d}" for number in range(1, 13))
### The crate directories the `warrantor` binary links: rust/warrant/Cargo.toml path
### dependencies plus warrant itself. Task 0.3's census will replace this constant.
WARRANT_REACHABLE_CRATES = frozenset(
    {
        "warrant",
        "trust-core",
        "authority-spec",
        "evidence",
        "notary",
        "egress",
        "containment-conformance",
        "spend",
    }
)
TEST_REFERENCE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<file>rust/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.rs)::(?P<name>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)$"
)
DOC_ROW = re.compile(r"^\| \*\*(?P<id>I-\d{2})\*\* \| (?P<statement>.+?) \| [^|]+ \|$")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LedgerIssue:
    """One reason the ledger is refused."""

    invariant: str
    message: str


def doc_statements(architecture_doc: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Read the I-xx rows of the architecture table; bold markers are stripped."""

    statements: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in architecture_doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        match = DOC_ROW.match(line)
        if match:
            statements[match.group("id")] = match.group("statement").replace("**", "")
    return statements


def cited_test_exists(repository_root: Path, reference: str) -> bool:
    """True when `<file>::<name>` names a `fn` whose attribute block contains `#[test]`."""

    match = TEST_REFERENCE.match(reference)
    if match is None:
        return False
    source = repository_root / match.group("file")
    if not source.is_file():
        return False
    lines = source.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
    signature = re.compile(rf"^\s*(pub\s+)?fn\s+{re.escape(match.group('name'))}\s*[(<]")
    return any(
        signature.match(line) and has_test_attribute(lines, index)
        for index, line in enumerate(lines)
    )


def has_test_attribute(lines: list[str], index: int) -> bool:
    """Walk upward from the `fn` line through its attributes and comments only.

    Stopping at the first line that is neither an attribute, a comment nor blank is
    what keeps a `#[test]` on the previous function from leaking onto a helper.
    """

    cursor = index - 1
    while cursor >= 0:
        previous = lines[cursor].strip()
        if previous == "#[test]":
            return True
        if previous.startswith(("#[", "//")) or not previous:
            cursor -= 1
            continue
        return False
    return False


def symbol_exists(repository_root: Path, crate: str, symbol: str) -> bool:
    """True when the symbol's last path segment occurs as a token in rust/<crate>/**/*.rs."""

    crate_root = repository_root / "rust" / crate
    if not crate_root.is_dir():
        return False
    identifier = symbol.rsplit("::", 1)[-1]
    token = re.compile(rf"\b{re.escape(identifier)}\b")
    return any(
        token.search(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
        for path in crate_root.rglob("*.rs")
    )
```

```python
def check_entry(
    repository_root: Path, entry: dict[str, object], statements: dict[str, str]
) -> list[LedgerIssue]:
    """Validate one invariant entry against the tree and the architecture table."""

    invariant = str(entry.get("id", "<missing id>"))
    issues: list[LedgerIssue] = []
    status = entry.get("status")
    if status not in ALLOWED_STATUSES:
        issues.append(
            LedgerIssue(invariant, f"status {status!r} not in {sorted(ALLOWED_STATUSES)}")
        )
    expected = statements.get(invariant)
    if expected is None:
        issues.append(LedgerIssue(invariant, "no row in docs/02-architecture.md section 3"))
    elif entry.get("statement") != expected:
        issues.append(LedgerIssue(invariant, "statement drifted from docs/02-architecture.md"))
    enforced_by = entry.get("enforced_by")
    if not isinstance(enforced_by, list):
        return [*issues, LedgerIssue(invariant, "enforced_by must be a list")]
    if status == "unimplemented" and enforced_by:
        issues.append(LedgerIssue(invariant, "unimplemented must list no enforcement"))
    if status != "unimplemented" and not enforced_by:
        issues.append(LedgerIssue(invariant, f"{status} needs at least one enforced_by entry"))
    linked: list[bool] = []
    for record in cast(list[dict[str, object]], enforced_by):
        crate = str(record.get("crate", ""))
        symbol = str(record.get("symbol", ""))
        test = str(record.get("test", ""))
        if not symbol_exists(repository_root, crate, symbol):
            issues.append(LedgerIssue(invariant, f"symbol {symbol!r} not found under rust/{crate}"))
        if not cited_test_exists(repository_root, test):
            issues.append(LedgerIssue(invariant, f"test {test!r} does not exist"))
        linked.append(crate in WARRANT_REACHABLE_CRATES)
    if status == "orphaned" and any(linked):
        issues.append(
            LedgerIssue(invariant, "orphaned but cites a crate the warrantor binary links")
        )
    if status in {"enforced", "partial"} and linked and not any(linked):
        issues.append(LedgerIssue(invariant, f"{status} but no cited crate is linked by warrantor"))
    return issues


def check_ledger(repository_root: Path, ledger: dict[str, object]) -> list[LedgerIssue]:
    """Validate the whole ledger: format, the twelve ids in order, then each entry."""

    issues: list[LedgerIssue] = []
    if ledger.get("format") != LEDGER_FORMAT:
        issues.append(LedgerIssue("ledger", f"format must be {LEDGER_FORMAT!r}"))
    invariants = ledger.get("invariants")
    if not isinstance(invariants, list):
        return [*issues, LedgerIssue("ledger", "invariants must be a list")]
    entries = cast(list[dict[str, object]], invariants)
    identifiers = tuple(str(item.get("id")) for item in entries)
    if identifiers != EXPECTED_IDS:
        issues.append(LedgerIssue("ledger", f"ids must be exactly {list(EXPECTED_IDS)} in order"))
    statements = doc_statements(repository_root / ARCHITECTURE_RELATIVE_PATH)
    for item in entries:
        issues.extend(check_entry(repository_root, item, statements))
    return issues


def main() -> int:
    """Exit 1 with every issue printed, or 0 with the status census."""

    ledger_path = REPOSITORY_ROOT / LEDGER_RELATIVE_PATH
    ledger = cast(dict[str, object], json.loads(ledger_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    issues = check_ledger(REPOSITORY_ROOT, ledger)
    for issue in issues:
        print(f"{LEDGER_RELATIVE_PATH.as_posix()}: {issue.invariant}: {issue.message}")
    if issues:
        print(f"invariant ledger: {len(issues)} issue(s); refusing")
        return 1
    entries = cast(list[dict[str, object]], ledger["invariants"])
    census = Counter(str(item["status"]) for item in entries)
    summary = ", ".join(f"{status}={census[status]}" for status in sorted(ALLOWED_STATUSES))
    print(f"invariant ledger: {len(entries)} invariants; {summary}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

## Phase 1 — Wire before widen: the four wirings

### Task 1.1: Evidence and notary into the report path (keystone; L7-02 seed, L7-07)

> Anchor (plan-brief.md, L7-02 / L4-07 / Part 11 "Wire before widen"): *"Evidence emission must exist before decomposing an action into its effects means anything"*, and the effect's own rule, Invariant I-07 — *"a consequential effect cannot commit until the external recorder has sufficient identity, intent, policy, target, action, and staging proof"* (S61 IR-10) — is today true of nothing in the settle path: `warrantor_evidence::issue_pre_commit` and `issue_post_commit` have no caller anywhere in `rust/warrant`.

**What is already wired, so this task does not rebuild it.** `rust/warrant/src/report.rs` already takes one notary verdict over the whole warrant (`notary::verdict(&request, &context)` at line 778), signs one `Atomic` evidence receipt over the bundle digest (`issue_atomic_checked`, line 943), and `warrantor verify` dispatches on `REPORT_EXPORT_FORMAT` (bin line 1223) with `--issuer <hex | pinned name>`. What is missing is the per-effect half of L7-02: when `settle::settle` calls `performer.perform(effect, &resolved)` (settle.rs line 149) nothing decides *that effect*, nothing signs before it, nothing signs after it, and the exported report cannot say which effects committed under which receipt. This task adds exactly that: an `EvidencedPerformer` that wraps whatever performer the surface already builds, a durable `receipts/<id>.jsonl` log written before the side effect, the chain embedded in the export, and `verify` running `warrantor_evidence::verify_chain` over every pair.

**Enforcement-mode decision (Rule 2).** The per-effect receipts carry `evidence::EnforcementMode::Advisory` and `notary::EnforcementMode::Observed`, derived through the existing `report::notary_mode_for`, not `Mediated`. Settle does mediate the *staged* path — the agent never held the token — but it does not mediate the world: the same pull request can be opened by an agent with its own credential, and a receipt claiming `mediated` would assert non-bypassability the system does not have (see `report::report_modes`, report.rs lines 121–134). Promotion waits for L4-03 credential redemption, where the agent can be shown to have held no direct credential.

```rust
//! Task 1.1: every staged effect is decided by the notary, signed before it is performed and
//! signed again after, and the exported report carries the chain a stranger can verify offline.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
use warrantor_evidence as evidence;
use warrantor_warrant::receipts::{chains, ReceiptLog};
use warrantor_warrant::report::{build, verify_export, verify_export_signed_by, ReportError};
use warrantor_warrant::settle::{settle, EffectOutcome, EffectPerformer, EffectWitness, EvidencedPerformer};
use warrantor_warrant::staging::{EffectRegistry, StagedEffect, StagingQueue};
use warrantor_warrant::store::StoredWarrant;
use warrantor_warrant::{SideEffectClass, Warrant, WarrantBounds, WarrantState};

const NOW: u64 = 1_786_000_000;
const ID: &str = "wrt_chain";
const SUBJECT: &str = "spiffe://muveraai.com/agent/alpha";

fn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let mut path = std::env::temp_dir();
    path.push(format!(
        "warrantor-chain-{tag}-{}",
        std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
            .unwrap_or(0)
    ));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&path).expect("tempdir");
    path
}

fn issuer() -> SigningKey {
    SigningKey::from_bytes(&[1; 32])
}

fn settle_key() -> SigningKey {
    SigningKey::from_bytes(&[2; 32])
}

fn args(pairs: &[(&str, &str)]) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
    pairs.iter().map(|(k, v)| ((*k).to_string(), (*v).to_string())).collect()
}

/// A warrant whose tool allowlist names the effects it will stage. `tests/settle.rs` grants
/// `git` and stages `github.*`; that passes today only because nothing decides per effect.
fn warrant_with_tools(tools: &[&str]) -> Warrant {
    let bounds = WarrantBounds {
        tools: tools.iter().map(|t| (*t).to_string()).collect(),
        write_paths: ["src/**".to_string()].into_iter().collect(),
        egress_hosts: BTreeSet::new(),
        staged_classes: [SideEffectClass::Write].into_iter().collect(),
        expires_at: NOW + 3600,
        budget_cents_observed: None,
        delegation_depth: 2,
    };
    Warrant::grant(ID, "open the fix", SUBJECT, bounds, NOW, &settle_key().verifying_key(), &issuer())
        .expect("grant")
}

fn queue_with_pr_and_comment(dir: &Path) -> StagingQueue {
    let mut queue = StagingQueue::open(dir.join("q.jsonl"), ID, EffectRegistry::github()).expect("open");
    let pr = queue.stage("github.create_pr", args(&[("title", "Fix")]), NOW).expect("pr");
    queue
        .stage("github.comment", args(&[("target", &pr.handle), ("body", "why")]), NOW)
        .expect("comment");
    queue
}

/// Performs, and at the moment of performing counts what is already durable on disk.
struct Counting {
    log_path: PathBuf,
    fail_at: Option<usize>,
    performed: Vec<String>,
    lines_on_disk_when_performing: Vec<usize>,
}

impl EffectPerformer for Counting {
    fn perform(&mut self, effect: &StagedEffect, _resolved: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<String, String> {
        let lines = std::fs::read_to_string(&self.log_path)
            .map(|body| body.lines().filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty()).count())
            .unwrap_or(0);
        self.lines_on_disk_when_performing.push(lines);
        if self.fail_at == Some(self.performed.len()) {
            return Err("upstream returned 503".to_string());
        }
        self.performed.push(effect.handle.clone());
        Ok(format!("real-{}", effect.index))
    }
}

fn witness(warrant: &Warrant) -> EffectWitness {
    EffectWitness::for_warrant(warrant, &issuer().verifying_key(), &issuer(), "issuer", Vec::new(), NOW)
}

#[test]
fn the_receipt_log_is_append_only_fsynced_jsonl_that_replays() {
    let dir = tempdir("log");
    let path = dir.join("receipts.jsonl");
    let mut log = ReceiptLog::open(&path).expect("open empty");
    assert!(log.is_empty());
    let warrant = warrant_with_tools(&["github.create_pr"]);
    let mut queue = StagingQueue::open(dir.join("q.jsonl"), ID, EffectRegistry::github()).expect("q");
    let effect = queue.stage("github.create_pr", args(&[("title", "Fix")]), NOW).expect("pr");
    let digest = warrantor_warrant::staging::effect_digest(&effect).expect("digest");
    let predicate = witness(&warrant).pre_commit_predicate(&effect, &digest, "nonce-1");
    let pre = evidence::issue_pre_commit(predicate, &issuer(), "issuer");
    log.append(&pre).expect("append");
    let reopened = ReceiptLog::open(&path).expect("reopen");
    assert_eq!(reopened.receipts(), &[pre]);
    assert_eq!(chains(reopened.receipts()).len(), 1);
    assert!(chains(reopened.receipts())[0].post_commit.is_none());
}
```

```rust
//! The per-effect receipt log: a pre-commit receipt before every performed effect, a post-commit
//! after it (I-07), in an append-only, `fsync`'d JSONL file the settle process writes and the
//! report reads.
//!
//! It lives in `receipts/<id>.jsonl`, beside neither `staged/` nor `witness/`, for the same reason
//! `witness/` is not under `staged/`: one `rm` must not take the record of what was performed
//! along with the record of what was queued. This is not an external recorder — L7-02 wants the
//! log outside the agent's write authority, and this file is on the same disk as everything else.
//! What it is: the first consumer of the evidence crate on the settle path, and the bytes the
//! archive push and the export carry. The limitations on every report say the rest.

use std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use warrantor_evidence as evidence;

use crate::settle::ReceiptSink;
use crate::WarrantError;

/// Wire format of one line of the log.
pub const RECEIPT_LOG_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.effect-receipts/1";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct LogLine {
    format: String,
    receipt: evidence::WarReceipt,
}

/// The receipts one warrant's settles have issued, in issuance order.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ReceiptLog {
    path: PathBuf,
    receipts: Vec<evidence::WarReceipt>,
}

impl ReceiptLog {
    /// Open (or lazily create) the log at `path`, replaying and signature-checking every line.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`WarrantError::Invalid`] when a line is not this format or its signature does not verify —
    /// an edited receipt is refused at open, not discovered at export.
    pub fn open(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self, WarrantError> {
        let path = path.as_ref().to_path_buf();
        let mut receipts = Vec::new();
        if path.exists() {
            let body = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
                .map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("read receipt log: {e}")))?;
            for (number, line) in body.lines().enumerate() {
                if line.trim().is_empty() {
                    continue;
                }
                let parsed: LogLine = serde_json::from_str(line).map_err(|e| {
                    WarrantError::Invalid(format!("receipt log line {}: {e}", number + 1))
                })?;
                if parsed.format != RECEIPT_LOG_FORMAT {
                    return Err(WarrantError::Invalid(format!(
                        "receipt log line {} declares {:?}; this build writes {RECEIPT_LOG_FORMAT}",
                        number + 1,
                        parsed.format
                    )));
                }
                evidence::verify_receipt(&parsed.receipt).map_err(|e| {
                    WarrantError::Invalid(format!("receipt log line {} does not verify: {e}", number + 1))
                })?;
                receipts.push(parsed.receipt);
            }
        }
        Ok(Self { path, receipts })
    }

    /// Append one receipt and `fsync` before returning: the caller performs a side effect on the
    /// strength of this returning `Ok`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`WarrantError::Encode`] on any I/O failure. The caller must treat that as "do not perform".
    pub fn append(&mut self, receipt: &evidence::WarReceipt) -> Result<(), WarrantError> {
        if let Some(parent) = self.path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)
                .map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("create receipts dir: {e}")))?;
        }
        let line = serde_json::to_string(&LogLine {
            format: RECEIPT_LOG_FORMAT.to_string(),
            receipt: receipt.clone(),
        })
        .map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("encode receipt: {e}")))?;
        let mut file: File = OpenOptions::new()
            .create(true)
            .append(true)
            .open(&self.path)
            .map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("open receipt log: {e}")))?;
        file.write_all(line.as_bytes())
            .and_then(|()| file.write_all(b"\n"))
            .and_then(|()| file.flush())
            .and_then(|()| file.sync_all())
            .map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("append receipt log: {e}")))?;
        self.receipts.push(receipt.clone());
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Every receipt, in issuance order.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn receipts(&self) -> &[evidence::WarReceipt] {
        &self.receipts
    }

    /// How many receipts the log holds.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.receipts.len()
    }

    /// Whether the log holds nothing.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.receipts.is_empty()
    }
}

impl ReceiptSink for ReceiptLog {
    fn record(&mut self, receipt: &evidence::WarReceipt) -> Result<(), String> {
        self.append(receipt).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    }
}

/// One effect's chain: the pre-commit, and the post-commit if one was issued.
///
/// A pre-commit with no post-commit is a real state — the process died between the receipt and
/// the outcome — and it is reported as such, never dropped and never paired with a stranger.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct EffectChain {
    /// Signed before the effect was attempted.
    pub pre_commit: evidence::WarReceipt,
    /// Signed after, carrying the outcome. `None` if the log ends between the two.
    pub post_commit: Option<evidence::WarReceipt>,
}

/// Pair pre-commits with the post-commits that name them, in pre-commit order.
#[must_use]
pub fn chains(receipts: &[evidence::WarReceipt]) -> Vec<EffectChain> {
    receipts
        .iter()
        .filter(|r| r.predicate.binding.phase == evidence::Phase::PreCommit)
        .map(|pre| {
            let id = &pre.predicate.binding.receipt_id;
            let post = receipts.iter().find(|r| {
                r.predicate.binding.phase == evidence::Phase::PostCommit
                    && r.predicate.binding.parent_receipt.as_deref() == Some(id.as_str())
            });
            EffectChain {
                pre_commit: pre.clone(),
                post_commit: post.cloned(),
            }
        })
        .collect()
}
```

```rust
/// SHA-256 hex of one staged effect's serialized form — the `parameters_digest` a receipt over
/// that effect carries, recomputable by anyone holding the effect.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`WarrantError::Encode`] if the effect does not serialize.
pub fn effect_digest(effect: &StagedEffect) -> Result<String, WarrantError> {
    let body = serde_json::to_vec(effect)
        .map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("digest effect: {e}")))?;
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    hasher.update(&body);
    Ok(hex::encode(hasher.finalize()))
}
```
