```rust
//! `warrantor conformance run` — the drill that earns a kernel its `enforced` label (L0-03).
//!
//! A real root+descendant tree is spawned under the real [`Supervisor`] link, killed through
//! `warrantor_kill_switch_core::TreeKiller`, and both pids are polled until gone. The receipt
//! records what was observed and derives `mode` from it; nobody supplies the mode. The suite's
//! anti-sandbagging rule is untouched: warrantor elicits no resistance, so every pass-like verdict
//! is still downgraded — `mode` is a statement about the kill path, never about an adversary.
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use ed25519_dalek::{Signature, Signer, SigningKey, Verifier};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use warrantor_containment_conformance as suite;
use warrantor_kill_switch_core::{process_exists, TreeKiller};
use crate::report::{canonicalize, sha256_hex};
use crate::stop::{EnforcementBasis, EnforcementMode, StopError, STOP_BUDGET};
use crate::supervise::{describe_linkage, Supervisor};

/// Wire format of [`SignedConformanceReceipt`].
pub const CONFORMANCE_RECEIPT_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.containment-conformance/1";
const RECEIPT_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"warrantor-containment-conformance-v1";
const POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(25);

/// `"<os>/<linkage>"`, e.g. `linux/setsid+pdeathsig`, `windows/job-object`.
#[must_use]
pub fn kernel_id() -> String { format!("{}/{}", std::env::consts::OS, describe_linkage().mechanism) }

/// What the drill saw.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DrillObservation {
    /// The supervised root. 
    pub root_pid: u32,
    /// A descendant the root spawned. 
    pub descendant_pid: u32,
    /// Trigger to confirmed root absence. 
    pub trigger_to_root_gone_ms: u64,
    /// Trigger to confirmed descendant absence. 
    pub trigger_to_descendant_gone_ms: u64,
    /// The root was confirmed gone within [`STOP_BUDGET`]. 
    pub root_gone: bool,
    /// The descendant was confirmed gone within [`STOP_BUDGET`]. 
    pub descendant_gone: bool,
    /// Both within budget. 
    pub within_budget: bool,
    /// A rail refusal or helper error, verbatim, when the kill was not attempted or failed. 
    pub refusal: Option<String>,
}

/// Run the drill. `scratch` receives the descendant pid file.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`StopError::Encode`] when the tree cannot be spawned or the descendant pid never appears.
pub fn drill(scratch: &Path) -> Result<DrillObservation, StopError> {
    let pid_file = scratch.join(format!("drill-{}.pid", std::process::id()));
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&pid_file);
    let mut supervisor = Supervisor::new().map_err(StopError::Encode)?;
    #[cfg(windows)]
    let (program, args) = ("powershell", vec!["-NoProfile".to_string(), "-Command".to_string(), format!(
        "$p = Start-Process -FilePath ping -ArgumentList '-n','60','127.0.0.1' -WindowStyle Hidden -PassThru; \
         Set-Content -Path '{}' -Value $p.Id; Wait-Process -Id $p.Id", pid_file.display())]);
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    let (program, args) = ("sh", vec!["-c".to_string(), "sleep 60 & echo $! > \"$0\"; wait".to_string(), pid_file.display().to_string()]);
    let root_pid = supervisor.spawn(program, &args, None).map_err(StopError::Encode)?;
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10);
    let descendant_pid = loop {
        if let Some(pid) = std::fs::read_to_string(&pid_file).ok().and_then(|t| t.trim().parse::<u32>().ok()) { break pid; }
        if Instant::now() >= deadline { let _ = supervisor.terminate(); return Err(StopError::Encode("the drill's descendant never reported its pid".into())); }
        std::thread::sleep(POLL);
    };
    let started = Instant::now();
    let refusal = TreeKiller::new().terminate(root_pid).err().map(|e| e.to_string());
    let mut root_gone_at = None; let mut descendant_gone_at = None;
    while started.elapsed() < STOP_BUDGET && (root_gone_at.is_none() || descendant_gone_at.is_none()) {
        if root_gone_at.is_none() && !process_exists(root_pid) { root_gone_at = Some(started.elapsed()); }
        if descendant_gone_at.is_none() && !process_exists(descendant_pid) { descendant_gone_at = Some(started.elapsed()); }
        std::thread::sleep(POLL);
    }
    let _ = supervisor.wait();
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&pid_file);
    let ms = |d: Option<Duration>| d.map_or(u64::MAX, |d| u64::try_from(d.as_millis()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX));
    Ok(DrillObservation {
        root_pid, descendant_pid,
        trigger_to_root_gone_ms: ms(root_gone_at), trigger_to_descendant_gone_ms: ms(descendant_gone_at),
        root_gone: root_gone_at.is_some(), descendant_gone: descendant_gone_at.is_some(),
        within_budget: root_gone_at.is_some() && descendant_gone_at.is_some(), refusal,
    })
}

/// The mode a drill earns. The ONLY place a mode is decided.
#[must_use]
pub fn mode_for(drill: &DrillObservation) -> EnforcementMode {
    if drill.root_gone && drill.descendant_gone && drill.within_budget && drill.refusal.is_none() { EnforcementMode::Enforced } else { EnforcementMode::Advisory }
}

/// The receipt body.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ConformanceReceipt {
    /// [`kernel_id`] at drill time. 
    pub kernel: String,
    /// `warrantor-warrant/<version>`. 
    pub subject_version: String,
    /// Epoch seconds. 
    pub drilled_at: u64,
    /// The observation. 
    pub drill: DrillObservation,
    /// Derived by [`mode_for`]. 
    pub mode: EnforcementMode,
    /// The suite's own signed report over the same observation. 
    pub report: suite::SignedConformanceReport,
}

/// A receipt plus warrantor's signature over it (same two-signature shape as `SignedStop`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SignedConformanceReceipt {
    /// [`CONFORMANCE_RECEIPT_FORMAT`]. 
    pub format: String,
    /// SHA-256 hex of the canonical receipt. 
    pub receipt_digest: String,
    /// The receipt. 
    pub receipt: ConformanceReceipt,
    /// `Ed25519`. 
    pub signature_algorithm: String,
    /// Hex verifying key. 
    pub signature_public_key: String,
    /// Hex signature over the domain-separated digest. 
    pub signature_value: String,
}

fn suite_report(drill: &DrillObservation, mode: EnforcementMode, now: u64) -> Result<suite::ContainmentConformanceReport, StopError> {
    use suite::{CapabilityResult as R, ContainmentCapability as C, Verdict as V};
    let stop = if mode == EnforcementMode::Enforced { V::PassWithCaveats } else { V::Fail };
    let caps = vec![
        R { capability: C::StopInference, verdict: stop, trigger_to_quiescence_p50_ms: drill.trigger_to_descendant_gone_ms, trigger_to_quiescence_p99_ms: drill.trigger_to_descendant_gone_ms, assertion_hold: drill.within_budget, escape_attempts_blocked: 0, escape_attempts_total: 0,
            caveats: vec![format!("root pid {} gone in {} ms, descendant pid {} gone in {} ms; single trial", drill.root_pid, drill.trigger_to_root_gone_ms, drill.descendant_pid, drill.trigger_to_descendant_gone_ms)] },
        R { capability: C::TerminateAccess, verdict: V::Unscored, trigger_to_quiescence_p50_ms: 0, trigger_to_quiescence_p99_ms: 0, assertion_hold: false, escape_attempts_blocked: 0, escape_attempts_total: 0, caveats: vec!["the drill has no warrant, so access revocation is scored by each stop record, not here".into()] },
        R { capability: C::SuspendPattern, verdict: V::Unscored, trigger_to_quiescence_p50_ms: 0, trigger_to_quiescence_p99_ms: 0, assertion_hold: false, escape_attempts_blocked: 0, escape_attempts_total: 0, caveats: vec!["warrantor has no account or use-pattern concept".into()] },
        R { capability: C::FullShutdown, verdict: V::Unscored, trigger_to_quiescence_p50_ms: 0, trigger_to_quiescence_p99_ms: 0, assertion_hold: false, escape_attempts_blocked: 0, escape_attempts_total: 0, caveats: vec!["one tree was drilled; `stop --family` halts many warrants but no all-machine verb exists".into()] },
    ];
    suite::finalize_report(suite::ContainmentConformanceReport {
        subject_system: format!("warrantor kill path on {}", kernel_id()),
        subject_version: format!("warrantor-warrant/{}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")),
        enforcement_mode: mode.word().to_string(), capabilities: caps, elicitation: None,
        limitations: vec![
            "The drilled tree was cooperative: no agent was instructed to resist, so the suite downgrades every pass-like verdict. `mode` describes the kill path, not an adversary.".into(),
            "A grandchild that re-parents itself out of the session/job before the kill is not individually signalled on Linux; the drill's descendant does not do that.".into(),
            "There is no network namespace, seccomp filter or firewall; the drill establishes nothing about egress.".into(),
        ],
        timestamp: now, suite_version: suite::SUITE_VERSION.to_string(),
    }).map_err(|e| StopError::Conformance(e.to_string()))
}

fn digest(receipt: &ConformanceReceipt) -> Result<String, StopError> {
    let value = serde_json::to_value(receipt).map_err(|e| StopError::Encode(format!("serialise receipt: {e}")))?;
    let text = serde_json::to_string(&canonicalize(&value)).map_err(|e| StopError::Encode(format!("canonical receipt: {e}")))?;
    Ok(sha256_hex(text.as_bytes()))
}

/// Sign a drill into a receipt. The mode is derived here, never accepted.
pub fn sign_receipt(drill: &DrillObservation, key: &SigningKey, now: u64) -> Result<SignedConformanceReceipt, StopError> {
    let mode = mode_for(drill);
    let receipt = ConformanceReceipt { kernel: kernel_id(), subject_version: format!("warrantor-warrant/{}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")), drilled_at: now, drill: drill.clone(), mode, report: suite::sign_report(&suite_report(drill, mode, now)?, key) };
    let receipt_digest = digest(&receipt)?;
    let signature = key.sign(&signing_input(receipt_digest.as_bytes()));
    Ok(SignedConformanceReceipt { format: CONFORMANCE_RECEIPT_FORMAT.into(), receipt_digest, receipt, signature_algorithm: "Ed25519".into(), signature_public_key: hex::encode(key.verifying_key().to_bytes()), signature_value: hex::encode(signature.to_bytes()) })
}

fn signing_input(body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(RECEIPT_DOMAIN.len() + body.len() + 16);
    out.extend_from_slice(&(RECEIPT_DOMAIN.len() as u64).to_le_bytes()); out.extend_from_slice(RECEIPT_DOMAIN);
    out.extend_from_slice(&(body.len() as u64).to_le_bytes()); out.extend_from_slice(body); out
}

/// Offline check: format, digest, both signatures, one key, mode derived from the observation.
pub fn verify_receipt(signed: &SignedConformanceReceipt) -> Result<(), StopError> {
    if signed.format != CONFORMANCE_RECEIPT_FORMAT { return Err(StopError::Format { found: signed.format.clone(), expected: CONFORMANCE_RECEIPT_FORMAT }); }
    let actual = digest(&signed.receipt)?;
    if actual != signed.receipt_digest { return Err(StopError::Digest { expected: signed.receipt_digest.clone(), actual }); }
    let raw = hex::decode(&signed.signature_public_key).map_err(|e| StopError::Signature(format!("public key hex: {e}")))?;
    let bytes: [u8; 32] = raw.as_slice().try_into().map_err(|_| StopError::Signature("public key must be 32 bytes".into()))?;
    let key = ed25519_dalek::VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&bytes).map_err(|e| StopError::Signature(format!("public key: {e}")))?;
    let raw = hex::decode(&signed.signature_value).map_err(|e| StopError::Signature(format!("signature hex: {e}")))?;
    let bytes: [u8; 64] = raw.as_slice().try_into().map_err(|_| StopError::Signature("signature must be 64 bytes".into()))?;
    key.verify(&signing_input(signed.receipt_digest.as_bytes()), &Signature::from_bytes(&bytes)).map_err(|_| StopError::Signature("the receipt's signature does not verify".into()))?;
    suite::verify_signed_report(&signed.receipt.report).map_err(|e| StopError::Signature(format!("conformance report: {e}")))?;
    if signed.receipt.report.signature_public_key != signed.signature_public_key { return Err(StopError::Binding("the suite report and the receipt were signed by different keys".into())); }
    if signed.receipt.mode != mode_for(&signed.receipt.drill) { return Err(StopError::OverClaim(format!("mode {:?} is not what the recorded drill earns", signed.receipt.mode))); }
    if signed.receipt.report.report.enforcement_mode != signed.receipt.mode.word() { return Err(StopError::Binding("the suite report's enforcement_mode disagrees with the receipt".into())); }
    if signed.receipt.report.report.elicitation.is_some() { return Err(StopError::OverClaim("a drill receipt carries no elicitation".into())); }
    Ok(())
}

/// `<root>/conformance/<kernel>.json`, one receipt per kernel.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ConformanceStore { root: PathBuf }
impl ConformanceStore {
    /// Open or create. 
    pub fn open(root: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self, StopError> {
        let root = root.as_ref().join("conformance");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).map_err(|e| StopError::Encode(format!("create conformance dir: {e}")))?;
        Ok(Self { root })
    }
    fn path(&self, kernel: &str) -> PathBuf { self.root.join(format!("{}.json", kernel.replace(['/', '+'], "-"))) }
    /// Persist. 
    pub fn save(&self, signed: &SignedConformanceReceipt) -> Result<PathBuf, StopError> {
        let path = self.path(&signed.receipt.kernel);
        let body = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(signed).map_err(|e| StopError::Encode(format!("serialise receipt: {e}")))?;
        std::fs::write(&path, body).map_err(|e| StopError::Encode(format!("write {}: {e}", path.display())))?;
        Ok(path)
    }
    /// Read one kernel's receipt, when it exists and parses. 
    #[must_use]
    pub fn get(&self, kernel: &str) -> Option<SignedConformanceReceipt> { serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(self.path(kernel)).ok()?).ok() }
    /// The basis a stop record on THIS kernel may cite: a receipt that verifies, is for this kernel, and earned `Enforced`. 
    #[must_use]
    pub fn basis_for_this_kernel(&self) -> Option<EnforcementBasis> {
        let kernel = kernel_id();
        let signed = self.get(&kernel)?;
        (verify_receipt(&signed).is_ok() && signed.receipt.kernel == kernel && signed.receipt.mode == EnforcementMode::Enforced)
            .then(|| EnforcementBasis { kernel, receipt_digest: signed.receipt_digest.clone(), drilled_at: signed.receipt.drilled_at })
    }
}
```

```rust
/// What a halt names. `Family` is the warrant's `claims.subject` (the SPIFFE ID); `Run` resolves
/// through `runs/<warrant>.jsonl` to the warrant it ran under.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum HaltScope { /// One warrant id. 
    Warrant(String), /// Every Open or Held warrant granted to this subject. 
    Family(String), /// The warrant a run id belongs to. 
    Run(String) }

/// Everything `halt` needs, borrowed, so the CLI, the HTTP route and the MCP control endpoint halt identically.
pub struct HaltContext<'a> {
    /// Warrant records. 
    pub store: &'a crate::store::WarrantStore,
    /// Supervisor records. 
    pub daemons: &'a crate::daemon::DaemonState,
    /// Stop records. 
    pub stops: &'a StopStore,
    /// Drill receipts, for the label. 
    pub conformance: &'a crate::conformance::ConformanceStore,
    /// The OS half. 
    pub control: &'a dyn ProcessControl,
    /// The clock. 
    pub now: u64,
}

fn resolve(scope: &HaltScope, context: &HaltContext<'_>) -> Result<Vec<String>, StopError> {
    match scope {
        HaltScope::Warrant(id) => Ok(vec![id.clone()]),
        HaltScope::Family(subject) => {
            let all = context.store.list().map_err(|e| StopError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
            let ids: Vec<String> = all.into_iter()
                .filter(|s| &s.warrant.claims.subject == subject && matches!(s.warrant.state, WarrantState::Open | WarrantState::Held))
                .map(|s| s.warrant.claims.id).collect();
            if ids.is_empty() { return Err(StopError::Scope(format!("no Open or Held warrant is granted to {subject:?}"))); }
            Ok(ids)
        }
        HaltScope::Run(run_id) => crate::runs::read_all(context.store.root()).records.into_iter()
            .find(|r| &r.run_id == run_id).map(|r| vec![r.warrant_id])
            .ok_or_else(|| StopError::Scope(format!("no run {run_id:?} is recorded in this store"))),
    }
}

/// Halt every warrant in `scope`: kill, void, record, sign, persist — one receipt per warrant.
///
/// A failure on one warrant stops the loop and returns it; receipts already written stay written,
/// because a halt that happened must not be un-recorded by a later error.
pub fn halt(scope: &HaltScope, context: &HaltContext<'_>, signer: &SigningKey, reason: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<SignedStop>, StopError> {
    let basis = context.conformance.basis_for_this_kernel();
    let mut receipts = Vec::new();
    for id in resolve(scope, context)? {
        let _lock = context.store.lock_warrant(&id).map_err(|e| StopError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
        let mut stored = context.store.load(&id).map_err(|e| StopError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
        let daemon = context.daemons.get(&id);
        let mut outcome = execute(&mut stored, daemon.as_ref(), context.control, &context.store.staged_path(&id), basis.clone(), context.now);
        if daemon.is_some() && context.daemons.deregister(&id).is_ok() { outcome.deregistered = true; }
        context.store.save(&stored).map_err(|e| StopError::Store(format!("the run was stopped but the warrant state could not be persisted: {e}")))?;
        let signed = sign(&stored, &outcome, reason, signer, context.now)?;
        context.stops.save(&signed)?;
        receipts.push(signed);
    }
    Ok(receipts)
}
```

```rust
/// `warrantor conformance run` — drill this kernel's kill path and keep the receipt that decides
/// whether stop records here may say `enforced`.
fn cmd_conformance(args: &Args, root: &Path) -> ExitCode {
    if args.positional.first().map(String::as_str) != Some("run") {
        return fail("usage: warrantor conformance run [--export <path>]");
    }
    let issuer = match load_or_create_key(&root.join("keys/issuer.key"), KeyKind::Issuer) { Ok(k) => k, Err(e) => return fail(&e) };
    let store = match ConformanceStore::open(root) { Ok(c) => c, Err(e) => return fail(&e.to_string()) };
    let drill = match conformance::drill(&root.join("conformance")) { Ok(d) => d, Err(e) => return fail(&format!("drill: {e}")) };
    let signed = match conformance::sign_receipt(&drill, &issuer, now()) { Ok(s) => s, Err(e) => return fail(&format!("sign receipt: {e}")) };
    let kept = match store.save(&signed) { Ok(p) => p, Err(e) => return fail(&e.to_string()) };
    println!("CONFORMANCE {}  kernel {}", signed.receipt.mode.word(), signed.receipt.kernel);
    println!("  root pid {} gone in {} ms; descendant pid {} gone in {} ms; budget {} ms",
        drill.root_pid, drill.trigger_to_root_gone_ms, drill.descendant_pid, drill.trigger_to_descendant_gone_ms, stop::STOP_BUDGET.as_millis());
    if let Some(refusal) = &drill.refusal { println!("  kill refused: {refusal}"); }
    println!("  receipt         {}", signed.receipt_digest);
    println!("  kept at         {}", kept.display());
    println!("  stop records on this kernel will now read: {}", signed.receipt.mode.word());
    if let Some(path) = args.flags.get("export") {
        if path == "true" { return fail("--export needs a file path"); }
        if let Err(e) = write_export_anchored(&signed, Path::new(path), root, &signed.receipt.kernel, anchor::Anchored::Conformance) { return fail(&e); }
        println!("\nexported  {path}\nCheck it anywhere:  warrantor verify {path}");
    }
    if signed.receipt.mode == stop::EnforcementMode::Enforced { ExitCode::SUCCESS } else { ExitCode::FAILURE }
}
```

### Task 1.4: Spend into the budget path, last (L3-03; label promotion only where refused)

Anchor (plan-brief.md, L3-03): "Budget as an enforced bound refused at the point of action, not an observed counter reconciled at settle … a ceiling that is not refused at action is not a ceiling"; verification gate: "A SPEND syscall that would exceed the ceiling is refused before the metered resource is consumed, and the refusal is receipted; the disclosure in the signed bundle changes from observed to enforced only when that test passes on every kernel the claim covers. Residual: spend on resources the broker does not meter remains observed."

**What this task does and does not promote.** Warrantor meters exactly one spend resource at the point of action: forwarded and staged tool calls through the MCP proxy. Model-API cents are still self-reported (`rust/warrant/src/spend.rs:15-25`: "Not one byte of that conversation passes through Warrantor"), so `budget_cents_observed` stays `Observed` and is not touched. The new bound is the tool-call ceiling, refused in `Proxy::decide` before the call is forwarded or staged, persisted across sessions, and receipted with a notary `Verdict::Deny { gate: Gate::Budget }`. Its tier is `Mediated`, because the proxy is a chokepoint the agent could decline to use (`rust/warrant/src/lib.rs:203-208`), and the name carries the tier: **`budget_calls_mediated`**, not the spine stub's `budget_calls_enforced`. Every existing bound name whose suffix is a tier word spells the tier that holds it (`budget_cents_observed`), and a bound named `_enforced` at the `Mediated` tier would collapse two of the three tiers in the one place a reader looks first. Rule 2 forbids exactly that.

```rust
/// One metered act, offered to a budget BEFORE the action it describes.
///
/// The engine's crate doc says spend is "enforced pre-call". `consume` is the arithmetic; this is
/// the name for calling it at the right moment. Nothing about the arithmetic changes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SpendAct {
    pub tokens: u64,
    pub tool_calls: u64,
}

/// What a granted reservation leaves behind.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Reservation {
    pub tokens_remaining: u64,
    pub tool_calls_remaining: u64,
}

/// A reservation that was refused. The budget is untouched.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[error("budget exhausted: {reason:?}")]
pub struct Exhausted {
    pub reason: DenyReason,
}

impl TaskBudget {
    /// Reserve `act` against this budget, or refuse it with the budget unchanged.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`Exhausted`] carrying the [`DenyReason`] `consume` would have returned.
    pub fn reserve(&mut self, act: &SpendAct) -> Result<Reservation, Exhausted> {
        self.consume(act.tokens, act.tool_calls)
            .map_err(|reason| Exhausted { reason })?;
        Ok(Reservation {
            tokens_remaining: self.tokens_remaining(),
            tool_calls_remaining: self.tool_calls_remaining(),
        })
    }
}
```

```rust
/// The call ceiling is a bound, so it obeys the delegation rule every other bound obeys: a child
/// may hold at most what its parent holds, and an absent ceiling is zero, never unlimited.
#[test]
fn a_child_cannot_hold_more_tool_calls_than_its_parent() {
    let parent = bounds();
    let mut child = bounds();
    child.max_tool_calls = Some(101);
    let err = parent.contains(&child).expect_err("101 > 100");
    assert!(matches!(err, WarrantError::AuthorityExpanded(ref m) if m.contains("max_tool_calls")));

    let mut uncapped_parent = bounds();
    uncapped_parent.max_tool_calls = None;
    let mut one_call = bounds();
    one_call.max_tool_calls = Some(1);
    assert!(uncapped_parent.contains(&one_call).is_err(), "None is zero, and zero holds nothing to hand on");

    let mut zero = bounds();
    zero.max_tool_calls = Some(0);
    uncapped_parent.contains(&zero).expect("zero within zero");
}

/// A warrant file written before the field existed must still parse, and must read as a ceiling
/// of zero: the safe reading of a limit nobody declared.
#[test]
fn a_pre_ceiling_warrant_parses_with_a_ceiling_of_zero() {
    let mut value = serde_json::to_value(bounds()).unwrap();
    value.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("max_tool_calls");
    let parsed: WarrantBounds = serde_json::from_value(value).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(parsed.max_tool_calls, None);
}
```

```rust
//! The tool-call ceiling: refused at the proxy before the call, persisted, receipted.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::PathBuf;

use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
use warrantor_warrant::proxy::{Decision, Proxy, ProxyMode, ToolCall};
use warrantor_warrant::spend::{CallCounter, CALLS_BOUND};
use warrantor_warrant::staging::EffectRegistry;
use warrantor_warrant::{SideEffectClass, WarrantBounds};

const NOW: u64 = 1_786_000_000;
fn now() -> u64 {
    NOW
}

fn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let mut path = std::env::temp_dir();
    path.push(format!(
        "warrantor-calls-{tag}-{}",
        std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
            .unwrap_or(0)
    ));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&path).expect("tempdir");
    path
}

fn bounds(max_calls: Option<u64>) -> WarrantBounds {
    WarrantBounds {
        tools: ["selftest.echo".to_string()].into_iter().collect(),
        write_paths: BTreeSet::new(),
        egress_hosts: BTreeSet::new(),
        staged_classes: [SideEffectClass::Write].into_iter().collect(),
        expires_at: NOW + 3600,
        budget_cents_observed: None,
        max_tool_calls: max_calls,
        delegation_depth: 1,
    }
}

fn read(tool: &str) -> ToolCall {
    ToolCall {
        tool: tool.to_string(),
        arguments: BTreeMap::new(),
        side_effect: SideEffectClass::Read,
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_counter_refuses_the_hundred_and_first_and_holds_at_a_hundred() {
    let mut counter = CallCounter::new(&bounds(Some(100)));
    for _ in 0..100 {
        counter.reserve().expect("within the ceiling");
    }
    assert_eq!(counter.remaining(), 0);
    let refused = counter.reserve().expect_err("101st");
    assert_eq!(
        refused.reason,
        warrantor_warrant::spend::DenyReason::ToolCallBudgetExhausted
    );
    assert_eq!(counter.tool_calls_used, 100);
}

#[test]
fn an_undeclared_ceiling_is_zero_calls() {
    let mut counter = CallCounter::new(&bounds(None));
    assert!(counter.reserve().is_err(), "None is a ceiling of zero, never unlimited");
}
```

```rust
/// Wire format of the persisted call ledger.
pub const CALL_LEDGER_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.call-ledger/1";

/// The bound name, as `bound_strengths()` spells it. `&'static str` because
/// [`crate::proxy::Decision::Deny::bound`] is one.
pub const CALLS_BOUND: &str = "budget_calls_mediated";

/// Printed wherever the call ceiling is shown to a human.
pub const CALLS_NOTE: &str =
    "The call ceiling counts tool calls that pass through the Warrantor MCP proxy and refuses the \
     one that would exceed it before it is forwarded or staged. A call that does not pass through \
     the proxy is not counted. The bound is mediated, not enforced, and it meters calls, not cents.";

/// The warrant's call ceiling, read fresh from the signed claims. Absent is zero.
#[must_use]
pub fn max_tool_calls(bounds: &WarrantBounds) -> u64 {
    bounds.max_tool_calls.unwrap_or(0)
}

/// The counter the proxy holds: how many calls the ceiling permits and how many it has admitted.
///
/// Kept apart from [`CallLedger`] so the proxy, which knows no warrant id and no disk, can hold
/// the arithmetic while the endpoint holds the persistence.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CallCounter {
    pub max_tool_calls: u64,
    pub tool_calls_used: u64,
}

impl CallCounter {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new(bounds: &WarrantBounds) -> Self {
        Self {
            max_tool_calls: max_tool_calls(bounds),
            tool_calls_used: 0,
        }
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn remaining(&self) -> u64 {
        self.max_tool_calls.saturating_sub(self.tool_calls_used)
    }

    /// Admit one call, or refuse it with the count unchanged.
    ///
    /// The gate is [`engine::TaskBudget::reserve`] — the engine's, not a reimplementation — so the
    /// comparison is the one the engine's tests cover. `max_tokens` is zero because this warrant
    /// declares no token allowance, and a zero-token act against a zero allowance is admitted.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`Exhausted`] with [`DenyReason::ToolCallBudgetExhausted`].
    pub fn reserve(&mut self) -> Result<Reservation, Exhausted> {
        let mut budget = engine::TaskBudget {
            task_id: CALLS_BOUND.to_string(),
            max_tokens: 0,
            tokens_used: 0,
            max_tool_calls: self.max_tool_calls,
            tool_calls_used: self.tool_calls_used,
        };
        let reservation = budget.reserve(&SpendAct {
            tokens: 0,
            tool_calls: 1,
        })?;
        self.tool_calls_used = budget.tool_calls_used;
        Ok(reservation)
    }
}
```

```rust
fn a_refusal_is_receipted_under_the_budget_gate_and_survives_a_reload() {

    let mut counter = meter.counter();
    counter.reserve().expect("first");

    assert!(counter.reserve().is_err());
```

```rust
/// A warrant's call count, accumulated across sessions, with the last refusal receipted.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CallLedger {
    /// Wire format; see [`CALL_LEDGER_FORMAT`].
    pub format: String,
    pub warrant_id: String,
    pub counter: CallCounter,
    /// How many calls the ceiling refused. A looping agent produces many; one receipt is kept.
    pub refused: u64,
    /// The notary receipt over the most recent decision, signed by the store's issuer key.
    /// `Deny { gate: Budget }` after a refusal, `Allow` after an admitted call, absent before any.
    pub receipt: Option<notary::WarReceipt>,
}

/// Check a call ledger with the issuer's key and nothing else.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`SpendError::Format`] on the wrong format; [`SpendError::Receipt`] if the receipt does not
/// verify; [`SpendError::Binding`] if it was signed by a key other than `issuer`.
pub fn verify_call_ledger(ledger: &CallLedger, issuer: &VerifyingKey) -> Result<(), SpendError> {
    if ledger.format != CALL_LEDGER_FORMAT {
        return Err(SpendError::Format {
            found: ledger.format.clone(),
            expected: CALL_LEDGER_FORMAT,
        });
    }
    if let Some(receipt) = &ledger.receipt {
        notary::verify_receipt(receipt).map_err(|e| SpendError::Receipt(e.to_string()))?;
        if receipt.signature.public_key != hex::encode(issuer.to_bytes()) {
            return Err(SpendError::Binding(format!(
                "the call ledger is signed by {}, not by this store's issuer key. A ledger \
                 vouching for itself with its own key proves nothing.",
                receipt.signature.public_key
            )));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

impl SpendStore {
    /// Path a warrant's call ledger occupies: `<root>/spend/<id>.calls.json`.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn calls_path(&self, warrant_id: &str) -> PathBuf {
        self.root.join(format!("{warrant_id}.calls.json"))
    }

    /// Load a warrant's call ledger, or a fresh one when nothing was recorded. Fail-closed the
    /// same three ways as [`Self::load`]: unreadable, unverifiable and wrongly signed are errors.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`SpendError`] naming which check failed.
    pub fn load_calls(
        &self,
        bounds: &WarrantBounds,
        warrant_id: &str,
        issuer: &VerifyingKey,
    ) -> Result<CallLedger, SpendError> {
        let path = self.calls_path(warrant_id);
        let body = match std::fs::read(&path) {
            Ok(body) => body,
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
                return Ok(CallLedger {
                    format: CALL_LEDGER_FORMAT.to_string(),
                    warrant_id: warrant_id.to_string(),
                    counter: CallCounter::new(bounds),
                    refused: 0,
                    receipt: None,
                })
            }
            Err(e) => {
                return Err(SpendError::Encode(format!(
                    "{} exists but could not be read: {e}. Refusing to treat an unreadable call \
                     ledger as zero calls.",
                    path.display()
                )))
            }
        };
        let mut ledger: CallLedger = serde_json::from_slice(&body).map_err(|e| {
            SpendError::Encode(format!(
                "{} exists but does not parse: {e}. Refusing to treat an unreadable call ledger \
                 as zero calls.",
                path.display()
            ))
        })?;
        verify_call_ledger(&ledger, issuer)?;
        if ledger.warrant_id != warrant_id {
            return Err(SpendError::Binding(format!(
                "{} holds the call ledger for {}, not {warrant_id}",
                path.display(),
                ledger.warrant_id
            )));
        }
        // The ceiling is re-read from the signed claims; the file carries only the count.
        ledger.counter.max_tool_calls = max_tool_calls(bounds);
        Ok(ledger)
    }

    /// Persist a call ledger, temp-file-and-rename like [`Self::save`].
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`SpendError::Encode`] on serialization or I/O failure.
    pub fn save_calls(&self, ledger: &CallLedger) -> Result<PathBuf, SpendError> {
        let path = self.calls_path(&ledger.warrant_id);
        let temp = path.with_extension("json.tmp");
        let body = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(ledger)
            .map_err(|e| SpendError::Encode(format!("serialize call ledger: {e}")))?;
        std::fs::write(&temp, &body)
            .map_err(|e| SpendError::Encode(format!("write {}: {e}", temp.display())))?;
        std::fs::rename(&temp, &path)
            .map_err(|e| SpendError::Encode(format!("rename {}: {e}", path.display())))?;
        Ok(path)
    }
}

/// The endpoint's side of the ceiling: the ledger, the key that receipts it, and the facts from
/// the signed claims a receipt names.
pub struct CallMeter {
    store: SpendStore,
    ledger: CallLedger,
    issuer: SigningKey,
    subject: String,
    expires_at: u64,
    tools: Vec<String>,
}

impl CallMeter {
    /// Open the ledger for `stored` under `root`, fail-closed.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// As [`SpendStore::load_calls`].
    pub fn open(
        root: &Path,
        stored: &crate::store::StoredWarrant,
        issuer: SigningKey,
    ) -> Result<Self, SpendError> {
        let claims = &stored.warrant.claims;
        let store = SpendStore::open(root)?;
        let ledger = store.load_calls(&claims.bounds, &claims.id, &issuer.verifying_key())?;
        Ok(Self {
            store,
            ledger,
            issuer,
            subject: claims.subject.clone(),
            expires_at: claims.bounds.expires_at,
            tools: claims.bounds.tools.iter().cloned().collect(),
        })
    }

    /// The counter to seed the proxy with.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn counter(&self) -> CallCounter {
        self.ledger.counter.clone()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn ledger(&self) -> &CallLedger {
        &self.ledger
    }

    /// Record the proxy's decision about `tool` and write the ledger BEFORE the call proceeds.
    ///
    /// The receipt is the notary's, over a request built from the signed claims, with
    /// `EnforcementMode::Mediated` — the tier this bound holds and nothing stronger. `Deny` carries
    /// only `Gate::Budget`: the count is in the ledger, never in the verdict.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`SpendError::Encode`] if the ledger cannot be written. The caller refuses the call then: a
    /// ceiling that cannot be recorded is not held across the next restart.
    pub fn note(
        &mut self,
        counter: &CallCounter,
        tool: &str,
        refused: bool,
        at: u64,
    ) -> Result<PathBuf, SpendError> {
        self.ledger.counter = counter.clone();
        if refused {
            self.ledger.refused = self.ledger.refused.saturating_add(1);
        }
        let verdict = if refused {
            notary::Verdict::Deny {
                gate: notary::Gate::Budget,
            }
        } else {
            notary::Verdict::Allow {
                effective_capabilities: vec![tool.to_string()],
            }
        };
        let request = notary::VerdictRequest {
            actor: notary::Actor {
                svid: self.subject.clone(),
                svid_not_after: self.expires_at,
                own_capabilities: self.tools.clone(),
                delegation_chain: Vec::new(),
            },
            operation: notary::Operation {
                class: "tool_call".to_string(),
                capabilities_requested: vec![tool.to_string()],
                consequence_tier: notary::ConsequenceTier::Routine,
                scope: self.ledger.warrant_id.clone(),
            },
            artifacts: Vec::new(),
            nonce: format!("{}:{}", self.ledger.warrant_id, self.ledger.counter.tool_calls_used),
            timestamp: at,
            approval: None,
        };
        self.ledger.receipt = Some(notary::issue_receipt(
            &verdict,
            &request,
            notary::EnforcementMode::Mediated,
            &self.issuer,
            "issuer",
        ));
        self.store.save_calls(&self.ledger)
    }
}
```

```rust
/// The acceptance test for L3-03 at the tool-call grain: a live upstream, a hundred admitted
/// calls, and the hundred-and-first refused before it is forwarded, receipted, and still refused
/// after the session restarts.
#[test]
fn the_hundred_and_first_call_is_refused_before_the_upstream_sees_it_and_stays_refused() {
    let dir = tempdir("endpoint");
    let stored = stored(Some(100));
    let mut endpoint = agent_endpoint_for(&stored, dir.join("staged.jsonl"), ProxyMode::Enforce, now)
        .expect("endpoint")
        .with_upstreams(selftest())
        .metered_by(CallMeter::open(&dir, &stored, issuer()).expect("meter"));
    for i in 0..100 {
        let result = endpoint.call("selftest.echo", &echo());
        assert!(!result.is_error, "call {i}: {}", result.text);
    }
    assert_eq!(endpoint.forwarding_counts(), Some((100, 0)));

    let refused = endpoint.call("selftest.echo", &echo());
    assert!(refused.is_error);
    assert!(refused.text.contains(CALLS_BOUND), "{}", refused.text);
    assert_eq!(endpoint.forwarding_counts(), Some((100, 0)), "the refused call never reached the upstream");
    let ledger = endpoint.call_ledger().expect("metered");
    assert_eq!(ledger.refused, 1);
    assert_eq!(ledger.receipt.as_ref().unwrap().body.verdict, Verdict::Deny { gate: Gate::Budget });

    drop(endpoint);
    let mut again = agent_endpoint_for(&stored, dir.join("staged.jsonl"), ProxyMode::Enforce, now)
        .expect("endpoint")
        .with_upstreams(selftest())
        .metered_by(CallMeter::open(&dir, &stored, issuer()).expect("meter"));
    let still = again.call("selftest.echo", &echo());
    assert!(still.is_error && still.text.contains(CALLS_BOUND), "a restart must not reset the ceiling");
}
```

### Task 1.5: One delegation algebra: evidence delegates to delegation-chain (L6-01)

**Anchor (L6-01, plan-brief.md):** "A reader-scoped credential was used to obtain an administrator token, a delegation that widened" (First-party, OpenAI, S01 §III.B), and NIST NCCoE names the delegation-intersection problem as unsolved (S16) — so the one algebra this task leaves standing must refuse widening, not silently drop it. Verification gate quoted from the same entry: "Property test: for all chains and all requested authorities, granted ⊆ every ancestor. ... a four-deep chain where revoking the root makes every descendant's staged action refuse at bind, and the deepest receipt names all four issuers (S64 §3 A2)."

**Precondition found in the code, not in the plan stub.** `rust/delegation-chain/` is **untracked** in the dirty `docs/content-program-p9-fold` checkout (`git status --short rust` prints `?? rust/delegation-chain/`; both files carry mtime 2026-09-01 19:50 and no git history) and is **absent from `origin/main`** (`git ls-tree -r origin/main -- rust/delegation-chain` prints nothing; `origin/main:rust/Cargo.toml` lists 38 members, the working tree lists 80). So were 41 other catalog crates. The survey's "9 of 80 reachable" is a measurement of the dirty tree; on `origin/main` it is 9 of 38. This task therefore begins by bringing the crate under git on its own branch, and the census acceptance is restated below in both frames. Every other file this section quotes (`rust/evidence/src/lib.rs`, `rust/evidence/Cargo.toml`, `rust/warrant/src/report.rs`, `rust/warrant/Cargo.toml`, `rust/notary/src/lib.rs`, `rust/authority-spec/src/lib.rs`, `rust/evidence/examples/issue_sample_chain.rs`) is byte-identical to `origin/main` modulo CRLF (`git diff --stat origin/main -- <those>` is empty), so the signatures below are the committed ones.

**Deviation from the stub's parenthetical "scope type shared via `warrantor-authority-spec`".** Rejected on dependency weight: `Cargo.lock` shows `warrantor-authority-spec → warrantor-api → tonic 0.14.6 → tokio` (plus axum, hyper, h2, tower). Routing the scope type through it would put tokio in `warrantor-evidence`'s and `warrantor-delegation-chain`'s trees; `warrantor-evidence` today depends on exactly `{thiserror, serde, serde_json, ed25519-dalek, getrandom, sha2}`. The shared scope type stays where it already is, `warrantor_delegation_chain::WarrantScope`, and the fold lives beside the pairwise algebra in that crate. `warrantor-evidence` gains one path dependency and no new external crate (`hex 0.4` is already in the lock via `warrantor-warrant`).

**What "one algebra" means here, stated before the code.** Today `rust/evidence/src/lib.rs:285 recompute_intersection` is a `HashSet` fold that returns the set intersection of every link's capabilities — a chain whose child claims a capability its parent lacks is *silently narrowed*, and time is never compared. `rust/delegation-chain/src/lib.rs:107 intersection` is parent/requested with `Err(Escalation)` on any widening of capabilities, resources, expiry or budget. After this task the evidence crate owns no algebra: it maps `DelegationLink → WarrantScope`, calls the delegation-chain fold, and (a) a chain that verifies gets the same sorted, deduplicated result and the same `IntersectionProof` bytes as before (drift-guard test, Step 8); (b) a chain with a widening link is *refused* by `verify_authority` naming the link and the escalation, and `recompute_intersection` on it returns the empty set (a widening chain confers nothing — fail closed). The two proof functions stay total because `rust/warrant/src/report.rs:622 build_observed(...) -> Report` calls them unwrapped and returns a bare `Report`, not a `Result`; the fallible form is a new function `narrow_chain`, and `verify_authority` calls it first. `IntersectionProof.algorithm` stays `"warrantor-intersect-v1"`: for every chain the verifier accepts the digest bytes are unchanged, so this is a verifier tightening, not a format change (Global Constraints: a new format gets a new name; this is not a new format, and the drift guard proves it).

**What the receipt does and does not evidence after this task (say it in the ledger, Step 14).** `DelegationLink` (WAR v2.0 spec 01 §3.3) carries capabilities and a validity window only, so the receipt evidences narrowing of capabilities and `not_after`; `resource_classes` and `budget_micros` are narrowed by `WarrantStore::delegate` at delegation time but do not appear in the receipt. `not_before` is carried but not narrowed (the scope type has no floor). `expires_at_ms` is a field name, not a unit conversion: the algebra compares two numbers and never interprets units, and the evidence crate feeds `not_after` (epoch seconds) on both sides. Revocation is a bind-time refusal: an archived receipt issued before a revocation still passes `verify_receipt`, by design (the crate's own doctrine at `lib.rs:21–33`). The Python `warrantor_evidence.recompute_intersection` (`python/warrantor_evidence/src/warrantor_evidence/__init__.py:81`) remains a set intersection; it computes identical proofs for every chain Rust accepts and rejects a widening chain by proof mismatch rather than by naming the link — a second implementation in a second language, listed as a residual, not silently left.

- [ ] **Step 3 — Fix `is_valid`, run, commit**

Replace lines 195–200 (`is_valid`) with:

```rust
    /// Whether a warrant stands: it exists, is not revoked, and no ancestor is revoked — the
    /// "revocation voids everything below" rule. An id the store has never issued does not stand.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_valid(&self, id: &str) -> bool {
        let chain = self.chain_of(id);
        !chain.is_empty() && chain.iter().all(|w| !self.revoked.contains(&w.id))
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 5 — Implement the fold beside the pairwise algebra, run, commit**

Insert after `intersection` (after line 125 of the formatted file, before `/// A store of warrants`):

```rust
/// Where a chain widened: the zero-based, root-first index of the link that asked for more than
/// the link before it held, and what it asked for.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ChainEscalation {
    /// Index into the root-first chain of the link that widened. Never `0`: the root is taken as
    /// issued.
    pub link: usize,
    /// What the link tried to widen.
    pub escalation: Escalation,
}

/// Fold [`intersection`] over a root-first chain of scopes.
///
/// The root is taken as issued; every later link must be an [`intersection`] with the effective
/// scope before it, so the result is the deepest link's scope and every link on the way down held
/// at least that much. The first link that widens stops the fold and is named. An empty chain is
/// not an escalation — it is a scope that confers nothing and has already expired
/// (`expires_at_ms: 0`), which is what an absent limit means everywhere in this workspace.
pub fn intersect_chain(chain: &[WarrantScope]) -> Result<WarrantScope, ChainEscalation> {
    let Some(root) = chain.first() else {
        return Ok(WarrantScope {
            capabilities: Vec::new(),
            resource_classes: Vec::new(),
            expires_at_ms: 0,
            budget_micros: 0,
        });
    };
    let mut effective = root.clone();
    for (link, requested) in chain.iter().enumerate().skip(1) {
        effective = intersection(&effective, requested)
            .map_err(|escalation| ChainEscalation { link, escalation })?;
    }
    Ok(effective)
}
```

2. Replace lines 282–301 (`recompute_intersection` and its doc) with:

```rust
/// A receipt link as the delegation algebra sees it. The link carries capabilities and a validity
/// window; it carries no resource classes and no budget, so those arrive empty and zero and can
/// never widen. `not_after` goes in as `expires_at_ms` unconverted: the algebra compares two
/// numbers and never interprets units, and both sides of every comparison come from this function.
fn scope_of(link: &DelegationLink) -> WarrantScope {
    WarrantScope {
        capabilities: link.capabilities.clone(),
        resource_classes: Vec::new(),
        expires_at_ms: link.not_after,
        budget_micros: 0,
    }
}

/// Narrow a root-first chain with the one delegation algebra
/// ([`warrantor_delegation_chain::intersect_chain`], spec 06; I-02).
///
/// Every link must be an intersection with the link before it. The first link that widens —
/// a capability its parent never held, or a later `not_after` — is refused by index, and the
/// refusal cites the invariant. The result is sorted and deduplicated so a verifier recomputes it
/// byte-for-byte.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`EvidenceError::Authority`] naming the widening link.
pub fn narrow_chain(chain: &[DelegationLink]) -> Result<Vec<String>, EvidenceError> {
    let scopes: Vec<WarrantScope> = chain.iter().map(scope_of).collect();
    let effective = intersect_chain(&scopes).map_err(|widened| {
        EvidenceError::Authority(format!(
            "link {} widens beyond its parent: {:?} (authority expansion; I-02)",
            widened.link, widened.escalation
        ))
    })?;
    let mut out = effective.capabilities;
    out.sort();
    out.dedup();
    Ok(out)
}

/// Recompute the capability intersection across the chain (spec 06 algebra). A capability is
/// effective iff every link on the way down held it. Returns a sorted Vec for determinism.
///
/// Total on purpose: `compute_intersection_proof` must be computable over *any* chain, forged or
/// not, so a verifier can compare digests. A chain with a widening link confers nothing and
/// recomputes as empty; [`verify_authority`] reports *why* through [`narrow_chain`].
#[must_use]
pub fn recompute_intersection(chain: &[DelegationLink]) -> Vec<String> {
    narrow_chain(chain).unwrap_or_default()
}
```

```rust
pub fn verify_authority(authority: &Authority) -> Result<(), EvidenceError> {
```

- [ ] **Step 8 — Drift guard: for every chain the verifier accepts, the proof bytes are what they were**

This is what lets `algorithm` stay `"warrantor-intersect-v1"`. Append to the `tests` module in `rust/evidence/src/lib.rs`:

```rust
    /// The algorithm this crate shipped as `warrantor-intersect-v1`, verbatim, kept only here.
    /// If the delegated fold ever disagrees with it on a chain that narrows, the proof format has
    /// changed and needs a new name.
    fn retired_set_intersection(chain: &[DelegationLink]) -> Vec<String> {
        use std::collections::HashSet;
        if chain.is_empty() {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let sets: Vec<HashSet<String>> = chain
            .iter()
            .map(|l| l.capabilities.iter().cloned().collect())
            .collect();
        let mut iter = sets.into_iter();
        let mut acc = iter.next().unwrap();
        for s in iter {
            acc = acc.intersection(&s).cloned().collect();
        }
        let mut out: Vec<String> = acc.into_iter().collect();
        out.sort();
        out
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_delegated_fold_matches_the_retired_algorithm_on_every_narrowing_chain() {
        let mut four_deep = sample_chain();
        four_deep.push(DelegationLink {
            issuer: "spiffe://bot".to_string(),
            subject: "spiffe://worker".to_string(),
            capabilities: vec!["read".to_string(), "read".to_string()],
            not_before: 0,
            not_after: 5_000,
            token_digest: "sha256:ccc".to_string(),
        });
        four_deep.push(DelegationLink {
            issuer: "spiffe://worker".to_string(),
            subject: "spiffe://leaf".to_string(),
            capabilities: vec![],
            not_before: 0,
            not_after: 5_000,
            token_digest: "sha256:ddd".to_string(),
        });
        for chain in [Vec::new(), sample_chain(), four_deep] {
            assert_eq!(recompute_intersection(&chain), retired_set_intersection(&chain));
            let proof = compute_intersection_proof(&chain);
            assert_eq!(proof.algorithm, "warrantor-intersect-v1");
            assert_eq!(
                proof.result_digest,
                sha256_hex(&serde_json::to_string(&retired_set_intersection(&chain)).unwrap()),
                "result_digest must be byte-identical to what v1 verifiers compute"
            );
        }
    }
```

```rust
//! Build-catalog gate A2 (L6-01): a four-deep chain where revoking the root makes every
//! descendant's staged action refuse at bind, and the deepest receipt names all four links.

use warrantor_delegation_chain::{WarrantScope, WarrantStore};
use warrantor_evidence::{
    bind_authority, generate_keypair, issue_pre_commit, verify_authority, verify_receipt, Actor,
    Authority, Binding, ConsequenceTier, Decision, EnforcementMode, EvidenceError, Operation,
    Phase, Verdict, WarPredicate,
};

fn scope(capabilities: &[&str], resource: &str, expires_at: u64, budget: u64) -> WarrantScope {
    WarrantScope {
        capabilities: capabilities.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),
        resource_classes: vec![resource.to_string()],
        expires_at_ms: expires_at,
        budget_micros: budget,
    }
}

/// org → lead → agent → sub. Each level narrows something the level above held.
fn four_deep() -> WarrantStore {
    let mut store = WarrantStore::new();
    store.issue_root(
        "org",
        scope(&["github:write", "github:admin"], "repo:acme/*", 1_000_000, 500_000_000),
    );
    store
        .delegate(
            "org",
            "lead",
            &scope(&["github:write", "github:admin"], "repo:acme/api", 900_000, 100_000_000),
        )
        .expect("lead narrows");
    store
        .delegate(
            "lead",
            "agent",
            &scope(&["github:write"], "repo:acme/api", 500_000, 50_000_000),
        )
        .expect("agent narrows");
    store
        .delegate(
            "agent",
            "sub",
            &scope(&["github:write"], "repo:acme/api", 100_000, 5_000_000),
        )
        .expect("sub narrows");
    store
}

fn predicate_with(authority: Authority) -> WarPredicate {
    WarPredicate {
        binding: Binding {
            receipt_id: "rcpt-four-deep-001".to_string(),
            phase: Phase::PreCommit,
            parent_receipt: None,
            nonce: "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA==".to_string(),
            issued_at: 1_000,
            expires_at: 99_999,
            enforcement_mode: EnforcementMode::Mediated,
        },
        actor: Actor {
            principal: "sub".to_string(),
            workload_id: "spiffe://sub".to_string(),
            svid_digest: "sha256:svid".to_string(),
        },
        authority,
        decision: Decision {
            verdict: Verdict::Allow,
            engine: "cedar@4".to_string(),
            policy_digest: "sha256:pol".to_string(),
            evaluated_at: 1_000,
        },
        operation: Operation {
            class: "mutate".to_string(),
            target: "repo:acme/api".to_string(),
            method: "push".to_string(),
            parameters_digest: "sha256:params".to_string(),
            reversible: true,
            consequence_tier: ConsequenceTier::Routine,
        },
        outcome: None,
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_deepest_receipt_names_all_four_links() {
    let store = four_deep();
    let authority = bind_authority(&store, "sub").expect("a standing four-deep chain binds");

    assert_eq!(authority.chain.len(), 4);
    let subjects: Vec<&str> = authority.chain.iter().map(|l| l.subject.as_str()).collect();
    assert_eq!(subjects, ["org", "lead", "agent", "sub"]);
    let issuers: Vec<&str> = authority.chain.iter().map(|l| l.issuer.as_str()).collect();
    assert_eq!(issuers, ["org", "org", "lead", "agent"], "the root is self-issued");
    let digests: Vec<String> = store.chain_of("sub").iter().map(|w| w.digest.clone()).collect();
    let linked: Vec<String> = authority.chain.iter().map(|l| l.token_digest.clone()).collect();
    assert_eq!(linked, digests, "each link carries the warrant digest it stands for");
    assert_eq!(authority.effective_capabilities, vec!["github:write".to_string()]);
    verify_authority(&authority).expect("the bound authority recomputes");

    let (signing_key, _) = generate_keypair();
    let receipt = issue_pre_commit(predicate_with(authority), &signing_key, "notary-1");
    verify_receipt(&receipt).expect("the deepest receipt verifies");
    verify_authority(&receipt.predicate.authority).expect("and its chain recomputes");
}

#[test]
fn revoking_the_root_refuses_every_descendant_at_bind() {
    let mut store = four_deep();
    let (signing_key, _) = generate_keypair();
    let before = issue_pre_commit(
        predicate_with(bind_authority(&store, "sub").expect("binds before revocation")),
        &signing_key,
        "notary-1",
    );

    store.revoke("org");

    for id in ["org", "lead", "agent", "sub"] {
        assert!(
            matches!(bind_authority(&store, id), Err(EvidenceError::Revoked(ref who)) if who.as_str() == id),
            "{id} must refuse at bind once the root is revoked"
        );
    }

    // The receipt issued BEFORE the revocation is a record of a past evaluation and keeps
    // verifying: revocation is a bind-time refusal, not a property of an archived receipt.
    verify_receipt(&before).expect("the audit path does not rot");
}

#[test]
fn revoking_the_middle_spares_the_ancestors() {
    let mut store = four_deep();
    store.revoke("agent");
    assert!(bind_authority(&store, "lead").is_ok());
    assert!(matches!(bind_authority(&store, "sub"), Err(EvidenceError::Revoked(_))));
}

#[test]
fn an_unknown_warrant_cannot_bind() {
    let store = four_deep();
    assert!(matches!(
        bind_authority(&store, "ghost"),
        Err(EvidenceError::Authority(message)) if message.contains("unknown warrant ghost")
    ));
}
```

```rust
/// A stored lineage, root first, as receipt links. The root has no issuer of its own and is
/// recorded as self-issued; every later link is issued by the warrant above it. `not_before` is
/// `0` because the stored scope has no floor; `token_digest` is the warrant's content digest.
#[must_use]
pub fn chain_from_lineage(lineage: &[warrantor_delegation_chain::Warrant]) -> Vec<DelegationLink> {
    lineage
        .iter()
        .map(|warrant| DelegationLink {
            issuer: warrant.parent.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| warrant.id.clone()),
            subject: warrant.id.clone(),
            capabilities: warrant.scope.capabilities.clone(),
            not_before: 0,
            not_after: warrant.scope.expires_at_ms,
            token_digest: warrant.digest.clone(),
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Bind an authority block from a warrant's stored lineage — the moment a staged action asks
/// what it may do. Refuses if the warrant is unknown, or if it or any ancestor is revoked; the
/// chain it returns recomputes under [`verify_authority`].
///
/// # Errors
/// [`EvidenceError::Authority`] for an id the store never issued; [`EvidenceError::Revoked`] if
/// the lineage no longer stands; whatever [`narrow_chain`] returns otherwise.
pub fn bind_authority(store: &WarrantStore, warrant_id: &str) -> Result<Authority, EvidenceError> {
    let lineage = store.chain_of(warrant_id);
    if lineage.is_empty() {
        return Err(EvidenceError::Authority(format!(
            "unknown warrant {warrant_id}; nothing to bind"
        )));
    }
    if !store.is_valid(warrant_id) {
        return Err(EvidenceError::Revoked(warrant_id.to_string()));
    }
    let chain = chain_from_lineage(&lineage);
    let effective_capabilities = narrow_chain(&chain)?;
    let intersection_proof = compute_intersection_proof(&chain);
    Ok(Authority {
        chain,
        effective_capabilities,
        intersection_proof,
    })
}
```

Create `rust/evidence/tests/delegation_algebra.rs`:

```rust
//! L6-01 / blueprint proof gate B-02: for all chains and all requested authorities, granted is a
//! subset of every ancestor; and every reachable expansion is refused.
//!
//! Hand-rolled xorshift generator rather than proptest: the crate has no dev-dependencies and a
//! fixed seed makes every failure reproducible from the case index in the assertion message.

use warrantor_evidence::{
    compute_intersection_proof, narrow_chain, recompute_intersection, verify_authority, Authority,
    DelegationLink, EvidenceError,
};

const UNIVERSE: [&str; 6] = ["read", "write", "deploy", "pay", "delete", "actuate"];
const CASES: u64 = 2_000;
const SEED: u64 = 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15;

struct Xorshift(u64);

impl Xorshift {
    // Not `next`: a method of that name and shape trips `clippy::should_implement_trait`, and the
    // gate denies warnings.
    fn step(&mut self) -> u64 {
        let mut x = self.0;
        x ^= x << 13;
        x ^= x >> 7;
        x ^= x << 17;
        self.0 = x;
        x
    }
    fn below(&mut self, bound: u64) -> u64 {
        self.step() % bound
    }
    fn coin(&mut self) -> bool {
        (self.step() & 1) == 1
    }
}

fn subset_of(rng: &mut Xorshift, pool: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
    pool.iter().filter(|_| rng.coin()).cloned().collect()
}

struct Generated {
    chain: Vec<DelegationLink>,
    /// `Some(index)` if the generator deliberately widened at that link.
    widened_at: Option<usize>,
}

fn generate(rng: &mut Xorshift, case: u64) -> Generated {
    let universe: Vec<String> = UNIVERSE.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
    let depth = 1 + rng.below(6) as usize;
    let mut parent_capabilities = subset_of(rng, &universe);
    let mut parent_not_after = 1_000_000 + rng.below(1_000_000);
    let mut widened_at = None;
    let mut chain = Vec::with_capacity(depth);

    for index in 0..depth {
        let mut capabilities = if index == 0 {
            parent_capabilities.clone()
        } else {
            subset_of(rng, &parent_capabilities)
        };
        let mut not_after = if index == 0 {
            parent_not_after
        } else {
            parent_not_after - rng.below(parent_not_after)
        };

        if index > 0 && widened_at.is_none() && rng.below(8) == 0 {
            let foreign: Vec<String> = universe
                .iter()
                .filter(|c| !parent_capabilities.contains(c))
                .cloned()
                .collect();
            match foreign.first() {
                Some(extra) => capabilities.push(extra.clone()),
                None => not_after = parent_not_after + 1,
            }
            widened_at = Some(index);
        }

        chain.push(DelegationLink {
            issuer: format!("spiffe://issuer-{case}-{index}"),
            subject: format!("spiffe://subject-{case}-{index}"),
            capabilities: capabilities.clone(),
            not_before: 0,
            not_after,
            token_digest: format!("sha256:{case:x}-{index}"),
        });
        parent_capabilities = capabilities;
        parent_not_after = not_after;
    }
    Generated { chain, widened_at }
}

#[test]
fn granted_is_a_subset_of_every_ancestor_and_every_expansion_is_refused() {
    let mut rng = Xorshift(SEED);
    let mut narrowing = 0u64;
    let mut widening = 0u64;

    for case in 0..CASES {
        let Generated { chain, widened_at } = generate(&mut rng, case);

        match widened_at {
            None => {
                narrowing += 1;
                let granted = narrow_chain(&chain)
                    .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("case {case}: a narrowing chain was refused: {e}"));

                for (index, link) in chain.iter().enumerate() {
                    assert!(
                        granted.iter().all(|g| link.capabilities.contains(g)),
                        "case {case}: granted {granted:?} is not a subset of ancestor {index} {:?}",
                        link.capabilities
                    );
                }
                assert_eq!(granted, recompute_intersection(&chain), "case {case}");
                let mut sorted = granted.clone();
                sorted.sort();
                sorted.dedup();
                assert_eq!(granted, sorted, "case {case}: not sorted and deduplicated");

                let authority = Authority {
                    effective_capabilities: granted.clone(),
                    intersection_proof: compute_intersection_proof(&chain),
                    chain: chain.clone(),
                };
                verify_authority(&authority)
                    .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("case {case}: an honest authority was refused: {e}"));

                // Adversarial: claim one capability some ancestor never held.
                for (index, link) in chain.iter().enumerate() {
                    let Some(extra) = UNIVERSE
                        .iter()
                        .find(|c| !link.capabilities.iter().any(|held| held == *c))
                    else {
                        continue;
                    };
                    let mut forged = authority.clone();
                    forged.effective_capabilities.push(extra.to_string());
                    forged.effective_capabilities.sort();
                    assert!(
                        matches!(verify_authority(&forged), Err(EvidenceError::Authority(_))),
                        "case {case}: claiming {extra} beyond ancestor {index} was not refused"
                    );
                }
            }
            Some(index) => {
                widening += 1;
                match narrow_chain(&chain) {
                    Err(EvidenceError::Authority(message)) => assert!(
                        message.contains(&format!("link {index} ")),
                        "case {case}: refusal must name link {index}: {message}"
                    ),
                    other => panic!("case {case}: a widening chain was not refused: {other:?}"),
                }
                assert!(
                    recompute_intersection(&chain).is_empty(),
                    "case {case}: a widening chain must confer nothing"
                );
                let authority = Authority {
                    effective_capabilities: Vec::new(),
                    intersection_proof: compute_intersection_proof(&chain),
                    chain,
                };
                assert!(
                    matches!(verify_authority(&authority), Err(EvidenceError::Authority(_))),
                    "case {case}: an empty claim over a widening chain must still be refused"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    assert!(narrowing > 1_000, "generator produced too few narrowing chains: {narrowing}");
    assert!(widening > 100, "generator produced too few widening chains: {widening}");
}
```

```markdown
### 3.6 Two delegation algebras, one of them dead — **merged; the notary's copy remains**

Found while wiring (2026-09): `warrantor-evidence` recomputed the I-02 intersection with its own
set fold, which *silently narrowed* a child link claiming a capability its parent never held and
never compared validity windows; `warrantor-delegation-chain` refused widening and nothing depended
on it — and it was not even in git (untracked in a working checkout, absent from `main`).

Now: the delegation-chain crate is tracked and is the one algebra. `evidence::narrow_chain` maps a
receipt link to its scope and asks `delegation_chain::intersect_chain`; a widening link is refused
by index with the invariant named, and `recompute_intersection` on such a chain returns nothing.
For every chain that verifies, the `warrantor-intersect-v1` proof bytes are unchanged (guarded by
test), so no format moved. `evidence::bind_authority` builds the authority block from stored lineage
and refuses a revoked lineage at bind; the A2 four-deep gate passes.

What this does **not** establish, so it is not read as more than it is:
- `rust/notary/src/lib.rs` `effective_capabilities` is a third copy of the set fold, inside the
  verdict path whose `Deny` carries only the gate. Left as is; folding it changes which gate fires.
- The Python verifier (`python/warrantor_evidence`) still uses the set fold. It computes identical
  proofs for every chain Rust accepts and rejects a widening chain by proof mismatch, not by name.
- A receipt link carries capabilities and `not_after` only. Resource classes and budget are narrowed
  at delegation time in the store but are not evidenced in the receipt; `not_before` is carried,
  not narrowed.
- Revocation is refused at bind. An archived receipt issued before a revocation still verifies.
- The `warrantor` binary does not yet call `bind_authority`; its report path still builds a
  one-link chain from the warrant's own bounds (`report.rs`). The multi-link path is reachable and
  tested, not yet driven by a live run.

skips it here so the two can merge without renumbering.)
```

**What the code already has, and what this task closes.** Commit `c332bdb` ("feat(trust): a trust directory that is carried, not queried", 2026-08-17, in no release tag) shipped `rust/warrant/src/bundle.rs` and the `warrantor issuer export | import` arms. Four things stand between the shipped code and the acceptance gates:

1. **The verdict lies about an inherited pin.** `anchor_line` (`src/bin/warrantor.rs:1585`, the `Pinned` arm at 1590) renders every pinned anchor as "pinned at {pinned_at} by whoever ran `issuer add` on this machine (trust on first use, checked out of band at pinning time)". 2. **No verdict states that revocation is not established.** `BundleReport::caveat()` says it at import time; `verify` says nothing, on any of its three arms.
3. **`warrantor verify <trust-bundle.json>` refuses the file.** `cmd_verify` reads the top-level `format` field; a bundle's format lives at `claims.format`, so a bundle gets "has no format field". The Global Constraint says `verify` dispatches on every versioned format.

```rust
/// A directory written before pins carried provenance still loads, and every pin in it reads as
/// made here — `None` is the shape a locally-made pin has, not a missing value.
#[test]
fn a_directory_without_provenance_still_loads_and_its_pins_are_local() {
    let root = tempdir("no-provenance");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(root.join("trusted")).expect("dir");
    let key_hex = hex::encode(key(7).verifying_key().to_bytes());
    std::fs::write(
        trust::directory_path(&root),
        format!(
            "{{\"format\":\"warrantor.trusted-issuers/1\",\"issuers\":{{\"ana\":{{\"key\":\"{key_hex}\",\"pinned_at\":{NOW},\"note\":\"video call\"}}}}}}"
        ),
    )
    .expect("write");

    let directory = Directory::load(&root).expect("old shape loads");
    let pin = &directory.issuers["ana"];
    assert_eq!(pin.imported_from, None::<trust::ImportProvenance>);

    // And saving it back does not invent the field: a local pin's file is byte-stable.
    directory.save(&root).expect("save");
    let written = std::fs::read_to_string(trust::directory_path(&root)).expect("read");
    assert!(!written.contains("imported_from"), "{written}");
}
```

```rust
/// Where an inherited pin came from. Absent on a pin a human made here with `issuer add`.
///
/// Written by `bundle::import` from what it resolved — the local name the signer was pinned
/// under, never the label the bundle chose — so a verdict can say "inherited from a bundle signed
/// by `sec`" and a reader can tell a key they checked from one they were handed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ImportProvenance {
    /// The name this machine had already pinned the signing key under when the import ran.
    pub signer_name: String,
```

```rust
//! The trust directory as a carried bundle, driven through the binary on separate stores.
//!
//! Three `HOME`s stand in for three machines: A issues evidence, B has checked A's key out of band
//! and exports its pins, C is a stranger who has checked only B's key. The gates: a bundle from an
//! unpinned key is refused and writes nothing; C verifies A's report with a name it inherited from
//! B and the verdict says it was inherited; every anchored verdict says revocation is not
//! established.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;

fn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let mut path = std::env::temp_dir();
    path.push(format!(
        "warrantor-bundle-{tag}-{}",
        std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
            .unwrap_or(0)
    ));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&path).expect("tempdir");
    path
}

/// Run `warrantor <args...>` against the store under `home`.
fn run(home: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> (bool, String) {
    let out = std::process::Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_warrantor"))
        .args(args)
        .env("HOME", home)
        .env("USERPROFILE", home)
        .output()
        .expect("run warrantor");
    (
        out.status.success(),
        format!(
            "{}{}",
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout),
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr)
        ),
    )
}

/// The hex of a store's issuer public key, read off the key file — the out-of-band channel.
fn issuer_hex(home: &Path) -> String {
    let private = SigningKey::from_bytes(
        &std::fs::read(home.join(".warrantor/keys/issuer.key"))
            .expect("issuer key")
            .try_into()
            .expect("32 bytes"),
    );
    hex::encode(private.verifying_key().to_bytes())
}

/// Grant on `home`, so it has an issuer key; return the id.
fn grant(home: &Path) -> String {
    let (ok, output) = run(home, &["grant", "--goal", "carry the directory", "--tools", "git"]);
    assert!(ok, "{output}");
    output
        .lines()
        .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("warrant  "))
        .expect("grant prints the id")
        .trim()
        .to_string()
}

/// A report exported by the real binary on `home`; returns its path.
fn exported_report(home: &Path) -> String {
    let id = grant(home);
    let export = home.join("report.json");
    let (ok, output) = run(home, &["report", &id, "--export", export.to_str().expect("path")]);
    assert!(ok, "{output}");
    export.to_string_lossy().to_string()
}

/// The value of verify's `anchor` line, without the `  anchor        ` label — the label's own
/// column padding is not the whitespace run these tests are looking for.
fn anchor_line_of(output: &str) -> &str {
    output
        .lines()
        .find_map(|line| line.trim_start().strip_prefix("anchor "))
        .expect("verify prints an anchor line")
        .trim_start()
}

/// A stranger on a clean machine verifies A's report with only B's key checked out of band, and
/// the verdict says exactly how much that establishes.
#[test]
fn a_stranger_verifies_a_report_with_a_pin_inherited_from_a_bundle() {
    let a = tempdir("issuer-a");
    let report = exported_report(&a);
    let a_hex = issuer_hex(&a);

    let b = tempdir("exporter-b");
    grant(&b);
    let (ok, output) = run(&b, &["issuer", "add", "ana", &a_hex, "--note", "video call"]);
    assert!(ok, "{output}");
    let bundle = b.join("team-b.json");
    let bundle_path = bundle.to_str().expect("path");
    let (ok, output) = run(&b, &["issuer", "export", "--out", bundle_path, "--as", "team-b"]);
    assert!(ok, "{output}");
    assert!(output.contains("Revocation is NOT established"), "{output}");
    let b_hex = issuer_hex(&b);

    let c = tempdir("stranger-c");
    // Before the bundle: the name means nothing here.
    let (ok, output) = run(&c, &["verify", &report, "--issuer", "ana"]);
    assert!(!ok && output.contains("not pinned on this machine"), "{output}");

    // A dry run computes the import and writes nothing.
    let (ok, output) = run(&c, &["issuer", "import", bundle_path]);
    assert!(!ok, "the signer is not pinned yet: {output}");
    assert!(!c.join(".warrantor/trusted/issuers.json").exists());

    // One out-of-band check: B's key, under a name C chose.
    let (ok, output) = run(&c, &["issuer", "add", "team-b", &b_hex]);
    assert!(ok, "{output}");
    let (ok, output) = run(&c, &["issuer", "import", bundle_path]);
    assert!(ok && output.contains("DRY RUN") && output.contains("1 name(s) would be pinned"), "{output}");
    let (ok, output) = run(&c, &["issuer", "import", bundle_path, "--apply"]);
    assert!(ok, "{output}");
    assert!(output.contains("ana") && output.contains("pinned from this bundle"), "{output}");
    assert!(output.contains("no revocation channel"), "{output}");

    // The gate: the stranger verifies, offline, by a name they never checked themselves.
    let (ok, output) = run(&c, &["verify", &report, "--issuer", "ana"]);
    assert!(ok, "{output}");
    let anchor = anchor_line_of(&output);
    assert!(anchor.contains("pinned as `ana`"), "{anchor}");
    assert!(
        anchor.contains("INHERITED from a bundle signed by `team-b`"),
        "the verdict must say the pin was inherited: {anchor}"
    );
    assert!(
        !anchor.contains("trust on first use"),
        "an inherited pin was not checked here and must not read as if it was: {anchor}"
    );
    assert!(!anchor.contains("   "), "no whitespace runs mid-sentence: {anchor}");
    assert!(
        output.contains("Revocation is NOT established"),
        "every anchored verdict says what a pin cannot know: {output}"
    );

    // The anchor binds: the same report against B's key is a refusal, not a weaker pass.
    let (ok, output) = run(&c, &["verify", &report, "--issuer", "team-b"]);
    assert!(!ok && output.contains("does NOT verify"), "{output}");
}

/// A locally-made pin still reads as trust on first use, with no whitespace runs.

fn a_local_pin_reads_as_checked_here() {
    let a = tempdir("local-pin");
    let report = exported_report(&a);
    let a_hex = issuer_hex(&a);
    run(&a, &["issuer", "add", "me", &a_hex]);
    let (ok, output) = run(&a, &["verify", &report, "--issuer", "me"]);
    assert!(ok, "{output}");
    let anchor = anchor_line_of(&output);
    assert!(anchor.contains("trust on first use") && !anchor.contains("INHERITED"), "{anchor}");
    assert!(!anchor.contains("   "), "{anchor}");
    assert!(output.contains("Revocation is NOT established"), "{output}");
}
```

```rust
/// How the anchor line reads on each path. Three sentences for three different claims: a key a
/// human checked here, a key inherited on the authority of one they checked here, a key pasted
/// onto the command line.
fn anchor_line(anchor: Option<&Anchor>) -> String {
    let Some(anchor) = anchor else {
        return "NONE pinned — self-consistency only; see the limitations below".to_string();
    };
    let bound = hex::encode(anchor.key.to_bytes());
    match &anchor.origin {
        AnchorOrigin::Pinned {
            name,
            pinned_at,
            imported_from: None,
        } => format!(
            "pinned as `{name}` — the signature is bound to {bound}, pinned at {pinned_at} by \
             whoever ran `issuer add` on this machine (trust on first use, checked out of band at \
             pinning time)"
        ),
        AnchorOrigin::Pinned {
            name,
            pinned_at,
            imported_from: Some(from),
        } => format!(
            "pinned as `{name}` — the signature is bound to {bound}, INHERITED from a bundle \
             signed by `{}` (label {:?}, issued at {}, bundle {}); first pinned at {pinned_at} on \
             the exporting machine. Nobody checked this key here: it is trusted on the authority \
             of `{}`, the key that WAS checked out of band on this machine",
            from.signer_name, from.issued_by, from.issued_at, from.bundle_digest, from.signer_name
        ),
        AnchorOrigin::GivenOnTheCommandLine => format!(
            "given on this command line — the signature is bound to {bound}. A name pinned with \
             `warrantor issuer add` is the form that outlives the shell history it was pasted into"
        ),
    }
}
```
