```rust
/// Run the real binary against `root`, with the binary's own directory on PATH so an
/// `--upstream 'x=warrantor selftest-upstream'` value never has to carry a path with spaces.
fn warrantor(root: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> std::process::Output {
    let bin = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_warrantor"));
    let mut paths = vec![bin.parent().expect("a directory").to_path_buf()];
    if let Some(existing) = std::env::var_os("PATH") {
        paths.extend(std::env::split_paths(&existing));
    }
    let mut all: Vec<String> = args.iter().map(|a| (*a).to_string()).collect();
    all.push("--root".to_string());
    all.push(root.to_string_lossy().to_string());
    std::process::Command::new(&bin)
        .args(&all)
        .env("PATH", std::env::join_paths(paths).expect("joinable"))
        .output()
        .expect("run warrantor")
}

fn shown_hex(root: &Path) -> String {
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&warrantor(root, &["issuer", "show-hex"]).stdout)
        .lines()
        .find_map(|l| l.strip_prefix("issuer public key  ").map(str::trim).map(str::to_string))
        .expect("a key line")
}

fn machine_key(root: &Path) -> SigningKey {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(root.join("keys/issuer.key")).expect("the store's issuer key");
    SigningKey::from_bytes(&bytes.as_slice().try_into().expect("32 bytes"))
}

#[test]
fn the_cli_signs_admits_exports_verifies_offline_and_refuses_an_unadmitted_server() {
    let root = tempdir("cli");
    let vendor_root = tempdir("cli-vendor");
    // The vendor signs with its own store's issuer key; this machine pins that key by name.
    let claims_path = vendor_root.join("selftest.claims.json");
    std::fs::write(
        &claims_path,
        serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&selftest_manifest(&[Syscall::Attest])).expect("json"),
    )
    .expect("write claims");
    let manifest_path = vendor_root.join("selftest.manifest.json");
    let signed = warrantor(
        &vendor_root,
        &["tools", "sign", claims_path.to_str().expect("utf-8"), "--out", manifest_path.to_str().expect("utf-8")],
    );
    assert!(signed.status.success(), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&signed.stderr));
    let vendor_hex = shown_hex(&vendor_root);

    // Unpinned: refused, and the refusal is in the ledger.
    let refused = warrantor(&root, &["tools", "admit", manifest_path.to_str().expect("utf-8")]);
    assert!(!refused.status.success());
    assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&refused.stderr).contains("issuer add vendor"));
    assert_eq!(AdmittedSet::open(&root).receipts().expect("ledger").len(), 1);

    assert!(warrantor(&root, &["issuer", "add", "vendor", &vendor_hex]).status.success());
    let admitted = warrantor(&root, &["tools", "admit", manifest_path.to_str().expect("utf-8")]);
    assert!(admitted.status.success(), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&admitted.stderr));
    let listed = String::from_utf8_lossy(&warrantor(&root, &["tools", "list"]).stdout).to_string();
    assert!(listed.contains("admitted") && listed.contains("selftest"), "{listed}");

    // Export, then verify on a store that has pinned nothing, against the admitting key.
    let export = root.join("selftest.admission.json");
    assert!(warrantor(&root, &["tools", "export", "selftest", "--out", export.to_str().expect("utf-8")]).status.success());
    let machine_hex = shown_hex(&root);
    let clean = tempdir("cli-clean");
    let verdict = warrantor(&clean, &["verify", export.to_str().expect("utf-8"), "--issuer", &machine_hex]);
    assert!(verdict.status.success(), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&verdict.stderr));
    let out = String::from_utf8_lossy(&verdict.stdout);
    assert!(out.contains("VERIFIED") && out.contains("not checked against a pin on this machine"), "{out}");
    let no_anchor = warrantor(&clean, &["verify", export.to_str().expect("utf-8")]);
    assert!(!no_anchor.status.success(), "an export without an anchor verifies nothing");

    // A session under --require-admission refuses a server with no admitted manifest.
    let stored = stored_open("w-cli", &["other.echo"], &[]);
    warrantor_warrant::store::WarrantStore::open(&root).expect("store").create(&stored).expect("create");
    let refused = warrantor(
        &root,
        &["mcp", "--agent", "w-cli", "--require-admission", "--upstream", "other=warrantor selftest-upstream"],
    );
    assert!(!refused.status.success());
    let err = String::from_utf8_lossy(&refused.stderr);
    assert!(err.contains("no admitted manifest") && err.contains("tools admit"), "{err}");
}

fn a_server_publishing_beyond_its_manifest_is_revoked_at_attach_and_the_revocation_is_receipted() {
    let root = tempdir("attach");
    let vendor = key(7);
    // Names `echo` only; the selftest server also publishes `now`.
    let mut only_echo = selftest_manifest(&[Syscall::Attest]);
    only_echo.tools.remove("now");
    let signed = sign_manifest(only_echo, &vendor);
    let manifest_path = root.join("selftest.manifest.json");
    std::fs::write(&manifest_path, serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&signed).expect("json")).expect("write");
    let vendor_hex = hex::encode(vendor.verifying_key().to_bytes());
    assert!(warrantor(&root, &["issuer", "add", "vendor", &vendor_hex]).status.success());
    assert!(warrantor(&root, &["tools", "admit", manifest_path.to_str().expect("utf-8")]).status.success());

    let stored = stored_open("w-attach", &["selftest.echo"], &[]);
    warrantor_warrant::store::WarrantStore::open(&root).expect("store").create(&stored).expect("create");
    let session = warrantor(
        &root,
        &["mcp", "--agent", "w-attach", "--upstream", "selftest=warrantor selftest-upstream"],
    );
    assert!(!session.status.success(), "the session must not start");
    let err = String::from_utf8_lossy(&session.stderr);
    assert!(err.contains("revoked") && err.contains("\"now\""), "{err}");

    let set = AdmittedSet::open(&root);
    assert!(set.is_revoked("selftest").expect("read").is_some());
    let receipts = set.receipts().expect("ledger");
    let last = receipts.last().expect("the revocation");
    assert_eq!(last.claims.decision, AdmissionDecision::Revoked);
    assert!(last.claims.reason.contains("now"), "{}", last.claims.reason);
    verify_receipt(last, &machine_key(&root).verifying_key()).expect("the revocation verifies");

    // Revoked servers are refused at the next attach too, with or without --require-admission.
    let again = warrantor(
        &root,
        &["mcp", "--agent", "w-attach", "--upstream", "selftest=warrantor selftest-upstream"],
    );
    assert!(!again.status.success());
    assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&again.stderr).contains("was revoked at"));
}
```

```rust
/// `warrantor tools <sign|admit|list|revoke|export|check-skill>`: signed admission manifests (L4-09).
fn cmd_tools(args: &Args, root: &Path) -> ExitCode {
    match args.positional.first().map(String::as_str) {
        Some("sign") => cmd_tools_sign(args, root),
        Some("admit") => cmd_tools_admit(args, root),
        Some("list") => cmd_tools_list(root),
        Some("revoke") => cmd_tools_revoke(args, root),
        Some("export") => cmd_tools_export(args, root),
        Some("check-skill") => cmd_tools_check_skill(args, root),
        Some(other) => fail(&format!(
            "unknown tools verb {other:?}. warrantor tools has six: sign, admit, list, revoke, \
             export, check-skill."
        )),
        None => fail(
            "usage: warrantor tools sign <claims.json> [--key <path>] --out <file>\n       \
             warrantor tools admit <manifest.json>\n       warrantor tools list\n       \
             warrantor tools revoke <server> --reason \"...\"\n       warrantor tools export \
             <server> --out <file>\n       warrantor tools check-skill <server> <file>",
        ),
    }
}

fn read_manifest(path: &str) -> Result<admission::SignedManifest, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("read {path}: {e}"))?;
    serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)
        .map_err(|e| format!("{path} is not a {}: {e}", admission::MANIFEST_FORMAT))
}

fn cmd_tools_sign(args: &Args, root: &Path) -> ExitCode {
    let (Some(claims_path), Some(out)) = (args.positional.get(1), args.flags.get("out")) else {
        return fail("usage: warrantor tools sign <claims.json> [--key <path>] --out <file>");
    };
    let key_path = args
        .flags
        .get("key")
        .map_or_else(|| root.join("keys/issuer.key"), PathBuf::from);
    let key = match load_or_create_key(&key_path, KeyKind::Issuer) {
        Ok(k) => k,
        Err(e) => return fail(&e),
    };
    let bytes = match std::fs::read(claims_path) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(e) => return fail(&format!("read {claims_path}: {e}")),
    };
    let claims: admission::ManifestClaims = match serde_json::from_slice(&bytes) {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(e) => {
            return fail(&format!(
                "{claims_path} is not a {} claims file: {e}",
                admission::MANIFEST_FORMAT
            ))
        }
    };
    let signed = admission::sign_manifest(claims, &key);
    if let Err(e) = admission::verify_manifest(&signed, &key.verifying_key(), now()) {
        return fail(&format!("{claims_path} would not verify even freshly signed: {e}"));
    }
    let body = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&signed).expect("a manifest serializes");
    if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(out, body) {
        return fail(&format!("write {out}: {e}"));
    }
    println!("signed   {} v{} -> {out}", signed.claims.server, signed.claims.version);
    println!(
        "issuer   {}. The admitting machine must pin this key under that name, checked out of \
         band:\n         warrantor issuer add {} {}",
        signed.claims.issuer,
        signed.claims.issuer,
        hex::encode(key.verifying_key().to_bytes())
    );
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

fn cmd_tools_admit(args: &Args, root: &Path) -> ExitCode {
    let Some(path) = args.positional.get(1) else {
        return fail("usage: warrantor tools admit <manifest.json>");
    };
    let manifest = match read_manifest(path) {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(e) => return fail(&e),
    };
    let directory = match trust::Directory::load(root) {
        Ok(d) => d,
        Err(e) => return fail(&e),
    };
    let signer = match load_or_create_key(&root.join("keys/issuer.key"), KeyKind::Issuer) {
        Ok(k) => k,
        Err(e) => return fail(&e),
    };
    match admission::AdmittedSet::open(root).admit(&manifest, &directory, &signer, now()) {
        Ok(receipt) => {
            println!(
                "admitted {} v{} (issuer {}, manifest {})",
                manifest.claims.server,
                manifest.claims.version,
                manifest.claims.issuer,
                &receipt.claims.manifest_digest[..16]
            );
            for (tool, entry) in &manifest.claims.tools {
                let verbs: Vec<&str> = entry.effects.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
                println!(
                    "  {}.{tool}: {}  data {:?}",
                    manifest.claims.server,
                    verbs.join("+"),
                    entry.data_classes
                );
            }
            println!(
                "record   {}",
                admission::admitted_path(root, &manifest.claims.server).display()
            );
            println!("receipt  {}", admission::ledger_path(root).display());
            ExitCode::SUCCESS
        }
        Err(e) => fail(&format!(
            "{e}\nThe refusal is receipted in {}.",
            admission::ledger_path(root).display()
        )),
    }
}

fn cmd_tools_list(root: &Path) -> ExitCode {
    let set = admission::AdmittedSet::open(root);
    let receipts = match set.receipts() {
        Ok(r) => r,
        Err(e) => return fail(&e.to_string()),
    };
    let servers: BTreeSet<String> = receipts
        .iter()
        .map(|r| r.claims.server.clone())
        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
        .collect();
    if servers.is_empty() {
        println!("no manifests have been admitted on this machine. warrantor tools admit <manifest.json>");
        return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
    }
    for server in servers {
        match (set.load(&server), set.is_revoked(&server)) {
            (Ok(Some(m)), _) => println!(
                "admitted   {server:<20} v{} issuer {} expires {} ({:?})",
                m.claims.version, m.claims.issuer, m.claims.expires_at, m.claims.kind
            ),
            (Ok(None), Ok(Some((at, reason)))) => println!("revoked    {server:<20} at {at}: {reason}"),
            (Ok(None), Ok(None)) => println!("refused    {server:<20} (never admitted; see the ledger)"),
            (Err(e), _) | (_, Err(e)) => println!("unreadable {server:<20} {e}"),
        }
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

fn cmd_tools_revoke(args: &Args, root: &Path) -> ExitCode {
    let (Some(server), Some(reason)) = (args.positional.get(1), args.flags.get("reason")) else {
        return fail("usage: warrantor tools revoke <server> --reason \"...\"");
    };
    let signer = match load_or_create_key(&root.join("keys/issuer.key"), KeyKind::Issuer) {
        Ok(k) => k,
        Err(e) => return fail(&e),
    };
    match admission::AdmittedSet::open(root).revoke(server, reason, &signer, now()) {
        Ok(receipt) => {
            println!("revoked  {server} at {}: {reason}", receipt.claims.at);
            println!(
                "Every session started from now refuses to attach {server} until a manifest is \
                 admitted again by name."
            );
            ExitCode::SUCCESS
        }
        Err(e) => fail(&e.to_string()),
    }
}

/// The export: the admitted manifest (absent once revoked) plus every receipt naming its server.
#[derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
struct AdmissionExport {
    format: String,
    server: String,
    manifest: Option<admission::SignedManifest>,
    receipts: Vec<admission::Receipt>,
}

fn cmd_tools_export(args: &Args, root: &Path) -> ExitCode {
    let (Some(server), Some(out)) = (args.positional.get(1), args.flags.get("out")) else {
        return fail("usage: warrantor tools export <server> --out <file>");
    };
    let set = admission::AdmittedSet::open(root);
    let manifest = match set.load(server) {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(e) => return fail(&e.to_string()),
    };
    let receipts: Vec<admission::Receipt> = match set.receipts() {
        Ok(r) => r.into_iter().filter(|r| &r.claims.server == server).collect(),
        Err(e) => return fail(&e.to_string()),
    };
    if receipts.is_empty() {
        return fail(&format!(
            "nothing has been decided about {server:?} on this machine; there is nothing to export"
        ));
    }
    let export = AdmissionExport {
        format: admission::EXPORT_FORMAT.to_string(),
        server: server.clone(),
        manifest,
        receipts,
    };
    let body = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&export).expect("an export serializes");
    match std::fs::write(out, body) {
        Ok(()) => {
            println!("exported {server} -> {out}");
            ExitCode::SUCCESS
        }
        Err(e) => fail(&format!("write {out}: {e}")),
    }
}

/// Compare a skill file's SHA-256 with the admitted skill manifest's `subject_digest`.
///
/// OBSERVED, and said so: a skill is loaded by the harness, never through the proxy, so this
/// checks a file an operator points at and refuses nothing at load time.
fn cmd_tools_check_skill(args: &Args, root: &Path) -> ExitCode {
    let (Some(server), Some(file)) = (args.positional.get(1), args.positional.get(2)) else {
        return fail("usage: warrantor tools check-skill <server> <file>");
    };
    let manifest = match admission::AdmittedSet::open(root).load(server) {
        Ok(Some(m)) if m.claims.kind == admission::AdmissionKind::Skill => m,
        Ok(Some(_)) => return fail(&format!("{server:?} is admitted as a tool server, not a skill")),
        Ok(None) => return fail(&format!("{server:?} has no admitted manifest on this machine")),
        Err(e) => return fail(&e.to_string()),
    };
    let bytes = match std::fs::read(file) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(e) => return fail(&format!("read {file}: {e}")),
    };
    let actual = report::sha256_hex(&bytes);
    let expected = manifest.claims.subject_digest.clone().unwrap_or_default();
    if actual == expected {
        println!(
            "MATCHES   {file} is byte-identical to the skill {server:?} admitted (sha256 {actual}).\n\
             This is an OBSERVED check of a file you named: nothing stops a harness loading a \
             different one."
        );
        ExitCode::SUCCESS
    } else {
        fail(&format!(
            "MISMATCH  {file} has sha256 {actual}; the admitted skill {server:?} is {expected}. \
             Do not load it."
        ))
    }
}

/// `warrantor verify` arm for [`admission::EXPORT_FORMAT`].
fn verify_admission_export(path: &str, body: &[u8], anchor: Option<&Anchor>) -> ExitCode {
    let Some(anchor) = anchor else {
        return fail(
            "an admission export verifies against the ADMITTING machine's issuer key, and the \
             export carries no key this command will take on its own word: pass --issuer \
             <name|hex>",
        );
    };
    let export: AdmissionExport = match serde_json::from_slice(body) {
        Ok(e) => e,
        Err(e) => return fail(&format!("{path} is not a {}: {e}", admission::EXPORT_FORMAT)),
    };
    for (i, receipt) in export.receipts.iter().enumerate() {
        if let Err(e) = admission::verify_receipt(receipt, &anchor.key) {
            return fail(&format!("{path}: receipt {} does not verify: {e}", i + 1));
        }
    }
    let origin = match &anchor.origin {
        AnchorOrigin::Pinned { name, pinned_at } => format!("pinned as {name} at {pinned_at}"),
        AnchorOrigin::GivenOnTheCommandLine => "given on the command line".to_string(),
    };
    println!(
        "VERIFIED  {} receipt(s) about {:?}, signed by the admitting machine's key ({origin})",
        export.receipts.len(),
        export.server
    );
    for receipt in &export.receipts {
        let digest = &receipt.claims.manifest_digest;
        println!(
            "  {:<9} at {}  manifest {}  {}",
            format!("{:?}", receipt.claims.decision).to_lowercase(),
            receipt.claims.at,
            &digest[..digest.len().min(16)],
            receipt.claims.reason
        );
    }
    if let Some(manifest) = &export.manifest {
        let recorded = export.receipts.iter().rev().find(|r| {
            r.claims.decision == admission::AdmissionDecision::Admitted
                && !r.claims.issuer_key.is_empty()
        });
        match recorded.and_then(|r| trust::parse_key(&r.claims.issuer_key).ok()) {
            Some(vendor_key) => match admission::verify_manifest(manifest, &vendor_key, 0) {
                Ok(()) => println!(
                    "manifest  signed by the vendor key the admitting machine recorded as {:?}. \
                     That key is taken from the receipt and is not checked against a pin on \
                     this machine; what is established is that the admitting machine's decision \
                     has not changed since it was made.",
                    manifest.claims.issuer
                ),
                Err(e) => {
                    return fail(&format!(
                        "{path}: the manifest does not verify against the vendor key the receipt \
                         recorded: {e}"
                    ))
                }
            },
            None => println!(
                "manifest  present, but no admission receipt records a vendor key, so its \
                 signature is not checked here."
            ),
        }
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}
```

**Acceptance (the L4-09 gate, mapped):** an unsigned manifest is `AdmissionError::Unsigned`, receipted (Step 5); a pinned, signed server that publishes a tool or schema its manifest does not name is revoked at attach, receipted, and the session refused, including on the next attach (Step 7); a call naming a destination to a no-`net` tool is refused at the `admission` bound and receipted with the manifest's standing unchanged, within that one invocation (Step 6); `warrantor verify <export> --issuer <hex>` on a store that pinned nothing prints `VERIFIED` and states that the vendor key came from the receipt and not from a pin (Step 7); a skill file that differs by one byte from its admitted digest is reported `MISMATCH` and the match output names its tier as `OBSERVED` (Step 8). No rendering in this task labels anything `Enforced`, and the first live run's revocation is expected, recorded, and is what makes the second run's receipt worth citing.

### Task 2.3: Two-phase staged effects for every syscall with idempotency keys (L4-07)

> Anchor (plan-brief.md, L4-07): *"Every external effect is staged, evidenced, then performed, never performed then logged. Two-phase commit for consequences: phase one writes identity, intent, policy verdict, target and staged payload to the external recorder; phase two performs only when the recorder acknowledges"* — Invariant I-07, blueprint P2 (S61 IR-10), proof gate E-06: pre-commit receipt and post-commit outcome link for every effect class.

**What exists and what is missing.** `rust/warrant/src/staging.rs` already stages instead of performing, and `rust/warrant/src/settle.rs` already releases in topological order and stops at the first failure. What it does not do is *evidence* an effect before performing it: `settle` calls `performer.perform(effect, &resolved)` directly (settle.rs:149), and nothing signed exists for that effect until the morning report. The evidence crate has had the primitive for this the whole time — `warrantor_evidence::issue_pre_commit` / `issue_post_commit` / `verify_chain` enforce the commit gate with the error text `"commit-gate violation (I-07)"` — and `rust/warrant` imports the crate only to sign reports (`report.rs:73`). This task puts the pre-commit receipt between the release loop and the performer, keys every staged effect so a retried settle cannot repeat it, and defines the `Recorder` seam that Task 3.4 later fills with the external flight recorder. The local file recorder shipped here lives on the same disk as the store; the section says so in the ledger rather than calling it external.

**Bound tier.** The gate is `Mediated`: the performer is the chokepoint (it holds the credential; the agent never does — `adapters/mod.rs:3-5`), and an effect that does not pass `settle` does not happen. It is not `Enforced`: nothing in this crate stops a human with the GitHub token from opening the pull request by hand. The ledger entry states that tier; no label is promoted by this task.

```rust
    fn record(&mut self, idempotency_key: &str, receipt: &warrantor_evidence::WarReceipt) -> Result<RecorderAck, String>;
    fn performed(&self, idempotency_key: &str) -> Option<String>;   // real_id of a recorded performance
    fn unresolved(&self, idempotency_key: &str) -> bool;            // pre-commit recorded, no post-commit
}
pub struct RecordedReceipt { pub format: String, pub sequence: u64, pub idempotency_key: String, pub receipt: warrantor_evidence::WarReceipt }
pub struct FileRecorder { /* path, next sequence, index */ }
impl FileRecorder { pub fn open(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self, WarrantError>; pub fn records(&self) -> &[RecordedReceipt]; }
impl Recorder for FileRecorder { ... }
pub fn verify_receipt_log(path: &Path) -> Result<usize, WarrantError>;       // pairs verified
pub struct EffectKind { pub tool: String, pub syscall: String, pub mints: String, pub targets: BTreeSet<String> }
impl EffectRegistry { pub fn register_as(&mut self, tool: &str, syscall: &str, mints: &str, targets: &[&str]); }

// settle.rs
pub const STAGED_RECEIPT_TTL_SECONDS: u64 = 600;
pub struct CommitGate<'a> { pub recorder: &'a mut dyn Recorder, pub signer: &'a ed25519_dalek::SigningKey, pub key_id: &'a str, pub now: u64 }
pub fn staged_predicate(warrant: &Warrant, effect: &StagedEffect, syscall: &str, idempotency_key: &str, now: u64) -> Result<warrantor_evidence::WarPredicate, WarrantError>;
pub fn settle(warrant: &mut Warrant, queue: &StagingQueue, worktree: Option<&Worktree>, presented: &ed25519_dalek::VerifyingKey, performer: &mut dyn EffectPerformer, gate: &mut CommitGate<'_>) -> Result<SettleReport, WarrantError>;

// store.rs
impl WarrantStore { pub fn receipts_path(&self, id: &str) -> PathBuf; }   // <root>/receipts/<id>.jsonl
```

  ```rust
  /// Wire format of one line in `receipts/<id>.jsonl`.
  pub const STAGED_RECEIPT_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.staged-receipt/1";

  /// The key under which a staged effect is performed at most once.
  ///
  /// Derived, not stored: `StagedEffect` is serialized into the queue's hash chain, so a new field
  /// on it would invalidate every existing log. The key is a digest over the warrant id and the
  /// effect's own position, tool and verbatim arguments — the same bytes the chain already
  /// commits to — so two processes replaying the same log compute the same key without talking.
  #[must_use]
  pub fn idempotency_key(warrant_id: &str, effect: &StagedEffect) -> String {
      let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
      for part in [
          warrant_id.as_bytes(),
          effect.index.to_string().as_bytes(),
          effect.tool.as_bytes(),
      ] {
          hasher.update((part.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
          hasher.update(part);
      }
      for (name, value) in &effect.arguments {
          hasher.update((name.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
          hasher.update(name.as_bytes());
          hasher.update((value.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
          hasher.update(value.as_bytes());
      }
      hex::encode(hasher.finalize())
  }
  ```

  In `staging.rs`, add `use warrantor_evidence::{Phase, WarReceipt};` to the imports, and after `idempotency_key`:
  ```rust
  /// The recorder's acknowledgment: the position it assigned in its own clock.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub struct RecorderAck {
      /// 1-based, strictly increasing across every receipt this recorder ever wrote.
      pub sequence: u64,
  }

  /// Phase one of every consequential effect.
  ///
  /// `settle` performs nothing until [`Recorder::record`] has returned `Ok` for the pre-commit
  /// receipt of that effect. An `Err` here is a refusal to perform, never a warning: a recorder
  /// that cannot acknowledge is a recorder that cannot testify, and an effect it cannot testify to
  /// is an effect that must not happen (I-07).
  pub trait Recorder {
      /// Durably record `receipt` under `idempotency_key` and acknowledge with its sequence.
      ///
      /// # Errors
      /// Why the record could not be made durable. The caller treats any error as "not recorded".
      fn record(&mut self, idempotency_key: &str, receipt: &WarReceipt) -> Result<RecorderAck, String>;

      /// The real id of a performance already recorded under this key, if any.
      fn performed(&self, idempotency_key: &str) -> Option<String>;

      /// True when a pre-commit was recorded for this key and no post-commit followed: the effect
      /// may or may not have happened, and only a human can say which.
      fn unresolved(&self, idempotency_key: &str) -> bool;
  }

  /// One line of `receipts/<id>.jsonl`.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  pub struct RecordedReceipt {
      /// Always [`STAGED_RECEIPT_FORMAT`].
      pub format: String,
      /// The recorder's clock.
      pub sequence: u64,
      /// The staged effect this receipt is about.
      pub idempotency_key: String,
      /// Pre-commit or post-commit, signed by the settling process.
      pub receipt: WarReceipt,
  }

  /// A recorder that appends to one `fsync`'d JSONL file.
  ///
  /// **Local, not external.** This file sits beside the staged log on the same disk as the store,
  /// so it proves the protocol, not custody: a host that can rewrite the store can rewrite this.
  /// Task 3.4 puts the flight recorder behind the same trait. The seam is what this delivers.
  #[derive(Debug)]
  pub struct FileRecorder {
      path: PathBuf,
      records: Vec<RecordedReceipt>,
      performed: BTreeMap<String, String>,
      in_flight: BTreeSet<String>,
  }

  impl FileRecorder {
      /// Open (or create) the log at `path`, replaying it.
      ///
      /// # Errors
      /// [`WarrantError::Invalid`] if a line does not parse, declares another format, or breaks the
      /// sequence — a gap or a repeat means the log was edited, and a recorder that was edited
      /// cannot answer `performed` truthfully.
      pub fn open(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self, WarrantError> {
          let path = path.as_ref().to_path_buf();
          let mut recorder = Self {
              path,
              records: Vec::new(),
              performed: BTreeMap::new(),
              in_flight: BTreeSet::new(),
          };
          if recorder.path.exists() {
              let body = std::fs::read_to_string(&recorder.path)
                  .map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("read receipts: {e}")))?;
              for (line_number, line) in body.lines().enumerate() {
                  if line.trim().is_empty() {
                      continue;
                  }
                  let record: RecordedReceipt = serde_json::from_str(line).map_err(|e| {
                      WarrantError::Invalid(format!("receipts line {}: {e}", line_number + 1))
                  })?;
                  if record.format != STAGED_RECEIPT_FORMAT {
                      return Err(WarrantError::Invalid(format!(
                          "receipts line {} declares {:?}; this build reads {STAGED_RECEIPT_FORMAT}",
                          line_number + 1,
                          record.format
                      )));
                  }
                  let expected = recorder.records.len() as u64 + 1;
                  if record.sequence != expected {
                      return Err(WarrantError::Invalid(format!(
                          "receipts line {} carries sequence {} where {expected} was expected; \
                           the log was edited and cannot say what was performed",
                          line_number + 1,
                          record.sequence
                      )));
                  }
                  recorder.index(&record);
                  recorder.records.push(record);
              }
          }
          Ok(recorder)
      }

      /// Every receipt, in the recorder's clock order.
      #[must_use]
      pub fn records(&self) -> &[RecordedReceipt] {
          &self.records
      }

      fn index(&mut self, record: &RecordedReceipt) {
          match record.receipt.predicate.binding.phase {
              Phase::PreCommit => {
                  self.in_flight.insert(record.idempotency_key.clone());
              }
              Phase::PostCommit => {
                  self.in_flight.remove(&record.idempotency_key);
                  let real_id = record
                      .receipt
                      .predicate
                      .outcome
                      .as_ref()
                      .filter(|outcome| outcome.status == "performed")
                      .and_then(|outcome| outcome.effects.first());
                  if let Some(real_id) = real_id {
                      self.performed
                          .insert(record.idempotency_key.clone(), real_id.clone());
                  }
              }
              Phase::Atomic => {}
          }
      }
  }

  impl Recorder for FileRecorder {
      fn record(&mut self, idempotency_key: &str, receipt: &WarReceipt) -> Result<RecorderAck, String> {
          let record = RecordedReceipt {
              format: STAGED_RECEIPT_FORMAT.to_string(),
              sequence: self.records.len() as u64 + 1,
              idempotency_key: idempotency_key.to_string(),
              receipt: receipt.clone(),
          };
          if let Some(parent) = self.path.parent() {
              std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| format!("create receipts dir: {e}"))?;
          }
          let mut file: File = OpenOptions::new()
              .create(true)
              .append(true)
              .open(&self.path)
              .map_err(|e| format!("open receipts: {e}"))?;
          let line = serde_json::to_string(&record).map_err(|e| format!("encode receipt: {e}"))?;
          file.write_all(line.as_bytes())
              .and_then(|()| file.write_all(b"\n"))
              .and_then(|()| file.flush())
              // The acknowledgment means "on stable storage". Anything less and a crash between
              // the ack and the effect leaves an effect with no record, which is the thing I-07
              // forbids.
              .and_then(|()| file.sync_all())
              .map_err(|e| format!("append receipt: {e}"))?;
          let ack = RecorderAck { sequence: record.sequence };
          self.index(&record);
          self.records.push(record);
          Ok(ack)
      }

      fn performed(&self, idempotency_key: &str) -> Option<String> {
          self.performed.get(idempotency_key).cloned()
      }

      fn unresolved(&self, idempotency_key: &str) -> bool {
          self.in_flight.contains(idempotency_key)
      }
  }
  ```

  After the `EffectPerformer` trait (line 56):
  ```rust
  /// How long a pre-commit receipt authorizes its effect. A settle is a moment, not a session.
  pub const STAGED_RECEIPT_TTL_SECONDS: u64 = 600;

  /// Everything phase one needs: where the record goes, who signs it, and what time it is.
  pub struct CommitGate<'a> {
      /// Phase one writes here; phase two waits for its `Ok`.
      pub recorder: &'a mut dyn Recorder,
      /// The key that signs both receipts. The settling process's key, never the agent's.
      pub signer: &'a SigningKey,
      /// Named in the signature envelope so a verifier knows which pinned key to check.
      pub key_id: &'a str,
      /// Epoch seconds, injected so tests own the clock.
      pub now: u64,
  }

  /// The pre-commit predicate for one staged effect: identity, intent, verdict, target and the
  /// staged payload's digest — the five things IR-10 says the recorder must hold before commit.
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// [`WarrantError::Encode`] if the arguments or bounds cannot be serialized, or the nonce cannot
  /// be drawn.
  pub fn staged_predicate(
      warrant: &Warrant,
      effect: &StagedEffect,
      syscall: &str,
      idempotency_key: &str,
      now: u64,
  ) -> Result<evidence::WarPredicate, WarrantError> {
      let claims = &warrant.claims;
      let mut nonce = [0u8; 16];
      getrandom::fill(&mut nonce).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("nonce: {e}")))?;
      let nonce = hex::encode(nonce);
      let parameters = serde_json::to_vec(&effect.arguments)
          .map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("encode arguments: {e}")))?;
      let bounds = serde_json::to_vec(&claims.bounds)
          .map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("encode bounds: {e}")))?;
      // One true link, built the way report.rs builds it: the issuer delegated exactly these tools
      // to this subject for this window, and the proof is recomputed by every verifier.
      let chain = vec![evidence::DelegationLink {
          issuer: warrant.issuer_key.clone(),
          subject: claims.subject.clone(),
          capabilities: claims.bounds.tools.iter().cloned().collect(),
          not_before: claims.issued_at,
          not_after: claims.bounds.expires_at,
          token_digest: format!("sha256:{}", sha256_hex(warrant.signature.as_bytes())),
      }];
      Ok(evidence::WarPredicate {
          binding: evidence::Binding {
              receipt_id: sha256_hex(format!("{idempotency_key}:{nonce}").as_bytes()),
              phase: evidence::Phase::PreCommit,
              parent_receipt: None,
              nonce,
              issued_at: now,
              expires_at: now + STAGED_RECEIPT_TTL_SECONDS,
              // The performer is a chokepoint the agent cannot reach around, and not an OS bound.
              enforcement_mode: evidence::EnforcementMode::Mediated,
          },
          actor: evidence::Actor {
              principal: claims.subject.clone(),
              workload_id: claims.id.clone(),
              // Same caveat as report.rs: a digest of the subject string, not of an SVID document.
              svid_digest: format!("sha256:{}", sha256_hex(claims.subject.as_bytes())),
          },
          authority: evidence::Authority {
              effective_capabilities: evidence::recompute_intersection(&chain),
              intersection_proof: evidence::compute_intersection_proof(&chain),
              chain,
          },
          decision: evidence::Decision {
              verdict: evidence::Verdict::Allow,
              engine: "warrantor-settle".to_string(),
              policy_digest: format!("sha256:{}", sha256_hex(&bounds)),
              evaluated_at: now,
          },
          operation: evidence::Operation {
              class: syscall.to_string(),
              target: effect.handle.clone(),
              method: effect.tool.clone(),
              parameters_digest: format!("sha256:{}", sha256_hex(&parameters)),
              reversible: false,
              consequence_tier: evidence::ConsequenceTier::Elevated,
          },
          outcome: None,
      })
  }

  fn performed_outcome(real_id: &str) -> evidence::Outcome {
      evidence::Outcome {
          status: "performed".to_string(),
          outcome_digest: format!("sha256:{}", sha256_hex(real_id.as_bytes())),
          effects: vec![real_id.to_string()],
          error: None,
          rollback_pointer: None,
      }
  }

  fn failed_outcome(reason: &str) -> evidence::Outcome {
      evidence::Outcome {
  ```

  ```rust
  /// Records events from the recorder and the performer into one log, so ordering is testable.
  struct Witnessed {
      inner: FileRecorder,
      fail_pre_commit_at: Option<usize>,
      fail_post_commits: bool,
      pre_commits: usize,
      events: Rc<RefCell<Vec<String>>>,
  }

  impl Recorder for Witnessed {
      fn record(&mut self, key: &str, receipt: &WarReceipt) -> Result<RecorderAck, String> {
          let phase = receipt.predicate.binding.phase;
          if phase == Phase::PreCommit {
              if self.fail_pre_commit_at == Some(self.pre_commits) {
                  return Err("recorder unreachable".to_string());
              }
              self.pre_commits += 1;
          } else if self.fail_post_commits {
              return Err("recorder unreachable".to_string());
          }
          let ack = self.inner.record(key, receipt)?;
          self.events.borrow_mut().push(format!("recorded:{phase:?}:{}", &key[..8]));
          Ok(ack)
      }
      fn performed(&self, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
          self.inner.performed(key)
      }
      fn unresolved(&self, key: &str) -> bool {

              .borrow_mut()
              .push(format!("performed:{}", &idempotency_key("wrt_2pc", effect)[..8]));
          Ok(format!("{}-{}", self.prefix, effect.index))
      }
  }

  fn harness(dir: &std::path::Path) -> (Witnessed, Performer, Rc<RefCell<Vec<String>>>) {

          inner: FileRecorder::open(dir.join("receipts.jsonl")).expect("open"),
          fail_pre_commit_at: None,
          fail_post_commits: false,
          pre_commits: 0,

  fn every_performed_effect_has_a_pre_commit_before_it_and_a_post_commit_after() {
      let dir = tempdir("order");
      let (mut w, settle_key) = warrant();
      let q = queue_with_three(&dir);
      let (mut recorder, mut performer, events) = harness(&dir);

          &mut w, &q, None, &settle_key.verifying_key(), &mut performer,
          &mut CommitGate { recorder: &mut recorder, signer: &settle_key, key_id: "settle", now: NOW },

          let pre = events.iter().position(|e| *e == format!("recorded:PreCommit:{key}")).expect("pre");
          let did = events.iter().position(|e| *e == format!("performed:{key}")).expect("performed");
          let post = events.iter().position(|e| *e == format!("recorded:PostCommit:{key}")).expect("post");
          assert!(pre < did && did < post, "{key}: pre={pre} performed={did} post={post}");

          assert!(pair[0].sequence < pair[1].sequence, "receipt precedes outcome in the recorder's clock");
      }
      assert_eq!(records[0].receipt.predicate.operation.class, "mutate");
      assert_eq!(records[2].receipt.predicate.operation.class, "msg");
  ```

- [ ] **Step 7 — The two-phase release loop.**
  Replace `settle` (settle.rs:120-196) with:
  ```rust
  /// Settle a warrant: evidence, release and record each staged effect in order, then merge.
  ///
  /// For every effect, in release order: if the recorder already holds a performance under the
  /// effect's idempotency key, reuse its real id and perform nothing; if it holds a pre-commit
  /// with no post-commit, stop — the effect may have happened and nobody can say; otherwise sign
  /// a pre-commit receipt, wait for the recorder's acknowledgment, perform, and sign the
  /// post-commit. An effect is never attempted before its pre-commit is acknowledged (I-07).
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// [`WarrantError::NotSettleAuthority`] if `presented` is not the warrant's settle authority,
  /// [`WarrantError::WrongState`] if it is not open or held, [`WarrantError::Invalid`] if the
  /// release order cannot be computed or a staged tool is absent from the queue's registry, or
  /// [`WarrantError::Encode`] if a receipt cannot be built.
  pub fn settle(
      warrant: &mut Warrant,
      queue: &StagingQueue,
      worktree: Option<&Worktree>,
      presented: &ed25519_dalek::VerifyingKey,
      performer: &mut dyn EffectPerformer,
      gate: &mut CommitGate<'_>,
  ) -> Result<SettleReport, WarrantError> {
      warrant.verify_settle(presented)?;
      if !matches!(warrant.state, WarrantState::Open | WarrantState::Held) {
          return Err(WarrantError::WrongState {
              state: warrant.state,
              operation: "settle",
          });
      }

      let order = queue.release_order()?;
      let mut resolved: BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::new();
      let mut outcomes: Vec<EffectOutcome> = Vec::new();
      let mut boundary = None;
      let mut stopped = false;

      for effect in order {
          if stopped {
              outcomes.push(EffectOutcome::Unreleased {
                  handle: effect.handle.clone(),
              });
              continue;
          }
          let key = idempotency_key(&warrant.claims.id, effect);

          // A retried settle re-walks the whole order. Anything already performed is reused,
          // never repeated: this is what makes a retry storm safe against an irreversible effect.
          if let Some(real_id) = gate.recorder.performed(&key) {
              resolved.insert(effect.handle.clone(), real_id.clone());
              outcomes.push(EffectOutcome::Released {
                  handle: effect.handle.clone(),
                  real_id,
              });
              continue;
          }
          if gate.recorder.unresolved(&key) {
              let reason = format!(
                  "the recorder holds a pre-commit for {} with no post-commit: it may have been \
                   performed. It is not re-performed automatically; check the target and settle \
                   again once the record is resolved.",
                  effect.handle
              );
              boundary = Some(format!("stopped at {} ({}): {reason}", effect.handle, effect.tool));
              outcomes.push(EffectOutcome::Failed {
                  handle: effect.handle.clone(),
                  reason,
              });
              stopped = true;
              continue;
          }

          let syscall = queue
              .kind_of(&effect.tool)
              .map(|kind| kind.syscall.clone())
              .ok_or_else(|| {
                  WarrantError::Invalid(format!(
                      "{} was staged by a registry this settle does not know",
                      effect.tool
                  ))
              })?;
          let predicate = staged_predicate(warrant, effect, &syscall, &key, gate.now)?;
          let pre = evidence::issue_pre_commit(predicate, gate.signer, gate.key_id);

          // Phase one. Nothing below runs until this returns Ok.
          if let Err(reason) = gate.recorder.record(&key, &pre) {
              let reason = format!("recorder did not acknowledge the pre-commit: {reason}");
              boundary = Some(format!(
                  "stopped at {} ({}): {reason}. It was not attempted; effects before it are \
                   real; effects after it were not attempted.",
                  effect.handle, effect.tool
              ));
              outcomes.push(EffectOutcome::Failed {
                  handle: effect.handle.clone(),
                  reason,
              });
              stopped = true;
              continue;
          }

          // Phase two.
          match performer.perform(effect, &resolved) {
              Ok(real_id) => {
                  let post =
                      evidence::issue_post_commit(&pre, performed_outcome(&real_id), gate.signer, gate.key_id);
                  resolved.insert(effect.handle.clone(), real_id.clone());
                  outcomes.push(EffectOutcome::Released {
                      handle: effect.handle.clone(),
                      real_id,
                  });
                  if let Err(reason) = gate.recorder.record(&key, &post) {
                      // The effect is real and its outcome is not on record. Say exactly that and
                      // stop: the next settle sees the open pre-commit and refuses to repeat it.
                      boundary = Some(format!(
                          "stopped after {} ({}): it was performed, but the recorder did not \
                           acknowledge the post-commit ({reason}). Effects after it were not \
                           attempted.",
                          effect.handle, effect.tool
                      ));
                      stopped = true;
                  }
              }
              Err(reason) => {
                  let post =
                      evidence::issue_post_commit(&pre, failed_outcome(&reason), gate.signer, gate.key_id);
                  // Best effort: the failure is already the boundary, and a recorder error here
                  // leaves an open pre-commit, which the next settle reports rather than repeats.
                  let _ = gate.recorder.record(&key, &post);
                  boundary = Some(format!(
                      "stopped at {} ({}): {reason}. Effects before it are real; effects after it \
                       were not attempted.",
                      effect.handle, effect.tool
                  ));
                  outcomes.push(EffectOutcome::Failed {
                      handle: effect.handle.clone(),
                      reason,
                  });
                  stopped = true;
              }
          }
      }

      let complete = !stopped;
      let mut worktree_merged = false;
      if complete {
          if let Some(tree) = worktree {
              tree.merge_into_base(&format!(
                  "warrant {}: {}",
                  warrant.claims.id, warrant.claims.goal
              ))?;
              worktree_merged = true;
          }
          warrant.transition(WarrantState::Settled)?;
      } else {
          warrant.transition(WarrantState::Held)?;
      }

      Ok(SettleReport {
          warrant_id: warrant.claims.id.clone(),
          effects: outcomes,
          complete,
          worktree_merged,
          boundary,
      })
  }
  ```

  In `staging.rs`, after `impl Recorder for FileRecorder`:
  ```rust
  /// Verify a receipt log offline: every line parses under [`STAGED_RECEIPT_FORMAT`], sequences are
  /// gapless, and every post-commit chains to the pre-commit before it under the same key
  /// (`warrantor_evidence::verify_chain`, which checks both signatures and the I-07 gate).
  ///
  /// Returns the number of verified pre/post pairs. A trailing pre-commit with no post-commit is
  /// not an error — it is the open-effect state `settle` refuses to repeat — and is left uncounted.
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// [`WarrantError::Invalid`] naming the first line that fails, with the evidence crate's reason.
  pub fn verify_receipt_log(path: &Path) -> Result<usize, WarrantError> {
      let recorder = FileRecorder::open(path)?;
      let mut open: BTreeMap<&str, &RecordedReceipt> = BTreeMap::new();
      let mut pairs = 0;
      for record in recorder.records() {
          match record.receipt.predicate.binding.phase {
              Phase::PreCommit => {
                  warrantor_evidence::verify_receipt(&record.receipt).map_err(|e| {
                      WarrantError::Invalid(format!("receipt {}: {e}", record.sequence))
                  })?;
                  open.insert(record.idempotency_key.as_str(), record);
              }
              Phase::PostCommit => {
                  let pre = open.remove(record.idempotency_key.as_str()).ok_or_else(|| {
                      WarrantError::Invalid(format!(
                          "receipt {} is a post-commit with no pre-commit before it",
                          record.sequence
                      ))
                  })?;
                  warrantor_evidence::verify_chain(&pre.receipt, &record.receipt).map_err(|e| {
                      WarrantError::Invalid(format!("receipts {}/{}: {e}", pre.sequence, record.sequence))
                  })?;
                  pairs += 1;
              }
              Phase::Atomic => {
                  return Err(WarrantError::Invalid(format!(
                      "receipt {} is atomic; a staged effect is never routine and reversible",
                      record.sequence
                  )))
              }
          }
      }
      Ok(pairs)
  }
  ```

### Task 2.4: EXEC admission by content digest and declared execution surface (L4-05)

**Anchor (plan-brief.md, L4-05):** *"From 26 June to 4 July agents installed Groovy plugins, user-supplied scripts, into Artifactory S01 §III.B; later a crafted RubyGems API call reached a JRuby deserialization path S01 §IV.B"* (First-party · OpenAI), and the proof gate is E-04: *"Unpinned or undeclared execution surfaces are refused under strict mode"*, verified by *"Execute a renamed but byte-identical artifact and assert the same verdict; execute a same-named but modified artifact and assert refusal; assert every EXEC receipt carries the digest."*

**What this task binds to, and what it does not claim.** Warrantor itself executes code in exactly two places: the agent process spawned by `warrantor run` → `warrantor supervise` (`rust/warrant/src/daemon.rs:329 supervise_run` → `rust/warrant/src/supervise.rs:120 Supervisor::spawn`), and the upstream MCP servers spawned by `rust/warrant/src/upstream.rs:287 Upstream::start_with`. This task puts the digest gate on the first, because it is the one the warrant already governs (`SuperviseRequest` is built from `stored.warrant.claims.bounds` at `bin/warrantor.rs:4535-4547`). The bound is a **chokepoint at the moment Warrantor spawns**: once the agent is running, its own shell can exec anything, and nothing here sees it (the mediation ceiling; `sandbox.rs:349-356` says the same about `tools`). The label therefore starts `Observed` and is promoted to `Mediated` only in the last commit, after the refusal test has been seen to run on both CI runners (Rule 2). It never claims `Enforced`. The `Upstream` surface is *named* in the enum so a warrant can declare it, but no refusal is wired for it here — Task 2.2's manifest admission owns the upstream spawn, and this section says so rather than pretending to cover it.

`exec: None` = the warrant declares no execution surface (every warrant granted before this task, and every grant without `--exec`): the spawn is digested and receipted (`Unpinned`), nothing is refused. `exec: Some(set)` = strict mode: a spawn whose `(surface, sha256)` is not in the set is refused **before the process exists**, and `Some(empty)` refuses every spawn. Declaring at least one `--exec` is the strict switch; there is no separate flag. The field is skipped when `None`, so the canonical bytes of every existing `warrantor.warrant/1` are unchanged and their signatures still verify; a warrant that declares a surface is still `warrantor.warrant/1` because an older binary re-canonicalizes it without the field and **fails signature verification** — fail-closed, which is the right direction for a bound it does not understand (Global Constraints: no silent format change; the encoding of every already-issued warrant is byte-identical).

  ```rust
  //! EXEC admission by content digest (L4-05).
  //!
  //! Anything this process executes on a warrant's behalf is identified by the SHA-256 of its
  //! bytes, never by its name or path, and the surface it may run on is declared in the warrant.
  //! A renamed artifact gets the same verdict; a modified one with the same name is refused. The
  //! refusal happens before the process exists, and every attempt -- admitted, unpinned or
  //! refused -- is receipted with the digest before anything is spawned.
  //!
  //! # What this holds and what it does not
  //!
  //! The gate sits where Warrantor itself spawns: [`crate::daemon::supervise_run`]. It cannot see
  //! what the agent then executes from its own shell; that is the mediation ceiling, and the bound
  //! is labeled accordingly in [`crate::bound_strengths`]. Digest pinning does not make the pinned
  //! artifact safe (blueprint E-04 residual); it makes "which code, exactly" a policy question.

  use std::collections::BTreeSet;
  use std::io::Read;
  use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

  use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

  /// Wire format of an EXEC receipt.
  pub const EXEC_RECEIPT_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.exec-receipt/1";

  /// Where admitted code runs. Only surfaces this build has a chokepoint for are nameable.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
  pub enum ExecSurface {
      /// The agent process spawned by `warrantor run` / `warrantor supervise`. Gated here.
      Process,
      /// An MCP server spawned by `--upstream`. Declarable; its gate is tool admission (manifests).
      Upstream,
  }

  impl ExecSurface {
      /// The word it is written as.
      #[must_use]
      pub const fn word(self) -> &'static str {
          match self {
              Self::Process => "process",
              Self::Upstream => "upstream",
          }
      }

      /// Parse one.
      ///
      /// # Errors
      /// A sentence naming the two surfaces this build gates. `shell`, `plugin` and `deserializer`
      /// are real surfaces the blueprint names; refusing them here is the point -- a surface with
      /// no chokepoint must not be declarable as though it had one.
      pub fn parse(word: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
          match word.trim() {
              "process" => Ok(Self::Process),
              "upstream" => Ok(Self::Upstream),
              other => Err(format!(
                  "{other:?} is not an execution surface this build has a chokepoint for. The two \
                   are: process, upstream."
              )),
          }
      }
  }

  /// One admitted artifact: a surface and the SHA-256 of the bytes that may run on it.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  pub struct ExecAdmission {
      /// Where it may run.
      pub surface: ExecSurface,
      /// Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the whole file. Never a name, never a path.
      pub sha256: String,
  }

  impl ExecAdmission {
      /// Parse `surface=<64 lowercase hex>`.
      ///
      /// # Errors
      /// A sentence. Uppercase hex is refused rather than lowered: two spellings of one digest
      /// would let the same artifact be admitted twice and revoked once.
      pub fn parse(raw: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
          let Some((surface, digest)) = raw.split_once('=') else {
              return Err(format!(
                  "{raw:?}: an admission is written surface=<sha256>, e.g. process=<64 hex chars>. \
                   Get the digest with `warrantor exec digest <path>`."
              ));
          };
          let surface = ExecSurface::parse(surface)?;
          let digest = digest.trim();
          let is_lower_hex = digest.len() == 64
              && digest.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(&b));
          if !is_lower_hex {
              return Err(format!(
                  "{digest:?} is not a 64-character lowercase hex SHA-256. An admission names \
                   bytes, not a file: run `warrantor exec digest <path>` and paste the digest."
              ));
          }
          Ok(Self { surface, sha256: digest.to_string() })
      }
  }
  ```

  ```rust
  /// Resolve a command on `PATH`, the way a shell would.
  ///
  /// Moved from the binary's `agents` verb. Written rather than shelled out to `which`/`where`,
  /// which differ between platforms, are absent in minimal containers, and on Windows answer about
  /// a different search order than the one a spawned process actually gets.
  #[must_use]
  pub fn resolve_on_path(command: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
      let path = std::env::var_os("PATH")?;
      let extensions: Vec<String> = if cfg!(windows) {
          std::env::var("PATHEXT")
              .unwrap_or_else(|_| ".COM;.EXE;.BAT;.CMD".to_string())
              .split(';')
              .filter(|e| !e.is_empty())
              .map(str::to_string)
              .collect()
      } else {
          vec![String::new()]
      };
      for directory in std::env::split_paths(&path) {
          for extension in &extensions {
              let candidate = directory.join(format!("{command}{extension}"));
              if candidate.is_file() {
                  return Some(candidate);
              }
          }
      }
      None
  }

  /// The file a program name denotes, before anything is hashed or spawned.
  ///
  /// A bare name is resolved on `PATH` and **never** in `cwd`: a file the agent wrote into its
  /// worktree must not shadow a tool of the same name. A name containing a separator is a path;
  /// relative paths are joined to `cwd`.
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// A sentence when nothing is found. Nothing that cannot be found can be hashed, and nothing
  /// that cannot be hashed can be admitted.
  pub fn resolve_program(program: &str, cwd: Option<&Path>) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
      let has_separator = program.contains('/') || program.contains(char::from(92));
      let candidate = if has_separator {
          let as_path = Path::new(program);
          match (as_path.is_absolute(), cwd) {
              (true, _) | (false, None) => as_path.to_path_buf(),
              (false, Some(dir)) => dir.join(as_path),
          }
      } else {
          return resolve_on_path(program).ok_or_else(|| {
              format!(
                  "{program:?} is not on PATH. A bare name is looked up on PATH only, never in the \
                   worktree; give a path if you mean a file there."
              )
          });
      };
      if candidate.is_file() {
          Ok(candidate)
      } else {
          Err(format!("{} is not a file", candidate.display()))
      }
  }

  /// SHA-256 of a whole file, streamed, with its length.
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// A sentence on I/O failure.
  pub fn sha256_file(path: &Path) -> Result<(String, u64), String> {
      let mut file = std::fs::File::open(path)
          .map_err(|e| format!("cannot open {} to digest it: {e}", path.display()))?;
      let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
      let mut buffer = [0u8; 64 * 1024];
      let mut total: u64 = 0;
      loop {
          let n = file
              .read(&mut buffer)
              .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
          if n == 0 {
              break;
          }
          hasher.update(&buffer[..n]);
          total += n as u64;
      }
      Ok((hex::encode(hasher.finalize()), total))
  }
  ```

  ```rust
  /// When in a run the admission was checked.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
  pub enum ExecPhase {
      /// `warrantor run`, before the detached supervisor is started. Advisory to the terminal.
      Preflight,
      /// `supervise_run`, immediately before `Supervisor::spawn`. The one that gates.
      Spawn,
  }

  /// What the gate decided.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
  pub enum ExecVerdict {
      /// The `(surface, sha256)` pair is in the warrant's declared set.
      Admitted,
      /// The warrant declares no execution surface. Digested and receipted; nothing refused.
      Unpinned,
      /// Strict mode and the pair is not declared. Nothing was spawned.
      Refused,
  }

  /// One EXEC attempt, written before anything is spawned.
  ///
  /// `path` is carried, unlike [`crate::runs::RunRecord`], because a digest with no statement of
  /// what was digested is not replayable evidence. It is the one field here that can name a
  /// location; the store class is listed in `docs/W1-delivery-gaps.md` §3.5 for that reason.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  pub struct ExecReceipt {
      /// Wire format: [`EXEC_RECEIPT_FORMAT`].
      pub format: String,
      /// The warrant under which execution was attempted.
      pub warrant_id: String,
      /// Epoch seconds.
      pub at: u64,
      /// Preflight or spawn.
      pub phase: ExecPhase,
      /// The surface asked for.
      pub surface: ExecSurface,
      /// SHA-256 of the file that would have run. Present on every verdict.
      pub sha256: String,
      /// Length of that file in bytes.
      pub bytes: u64,
      /// The resolved file.
      pub path: String,
      /// The decision.
      pub verdict: ExecVerdict,
      /// The notary gate a refusal is attributed to; `None` unless refused. Only the gate --
      /// never the declared set -- the same rule as `warrantor_notary::Verdict::Deny`.
      pub gate: Option<warrantor_notary::Gate>,
  }

  /// Decide whether `program` may run on `surface` under a warrant's declared execution surface.
  ///
  /// Resolves, hashes, and compares. Performs nothing.
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// A sentence when the program cannot be resolved or read. That is not a verdict: an artifact
  /// that cannot be hashed has no digest to admit, and the caller must treat it as a refusal.
  pub fn admit(
      declared: Option<&BTreeSet<ExecAdmission>>,
      surface: ExecSurface,
      program: &str,
      cwd: Option<&Path>,
      warrant_id: &str,
      phase: ExecPhase,
      at: u64,
  ) -> Result<ExecReceipt, String> {
      let path = resolve_program(program, cwd)?;
      let (sha256, bytes) = sha256_file(&path)?;
      let (verdict, gate) = match declared {
          None => (ExecVerdict::Unpinned, None),
          Some(set) => {
              let wanted = ExecAdmission { surface, sha256: sha256.clone() };
              if set.contains(&wanted) {
                  (ExecVerdict::Admitted, None)
              } else {
                  (ExecVerdict::Refused, Some(warrantor_notary::Gate::Artifacts))
              }
          }
      };
      Ok(ExecReceipt {
          format: EXEC_RECEIPT_FORMAT.to_string(),
          warrant_id: warrant_id.to_string(),
          at,
          phase,
          surface,
          sha256,
          bytes,
          path: path.to_string_lossy().to_string(),
          verdict,
          gate,
      })
  }

  /// The sentence printed when a spawn is refused. Names the gate, the surface and the digest of
  /// what was attempted; never the admitted set.
  #[must_use]
  pub fn refusal_sentence(receipt: &ExecReceipt) -> String {
      format!(
          "exec refused at gate artifacts: the {} artifact at {} (sha256 {}) is not admitted by \
           {}. Nothing was spawned. Pin exactly the bytes you mean on a NEW warrant with \
           `warrantor grant ... --exec {}=<sha256>` (get it with `warrantor exec digest <path>`), \
           or grant without --exec to record digests without refusing.",
          receipt.surface.word(),
          receipt.path,
          receipt.sha256,
          receipt.warrant_id,
          receipt.surface.word()
      )
  }

  /// Where a warrant's EXEC receipts live: `root/exec/<warrant-id>.jsonl`.
  #[must_use]
  pub fn log_path(root: &Path, warrant_id: &str) -> PathBuf {
      root.join("exec").join(format!("{warrant_id}.jsonl"))
  }

  /// Append one receipt, `fsync`-free but flushed, before the spawn it describes.
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// A sentence on I/O failure. The caller refuses to spawn on it: a spawn with no receipt is
  /// exactly the unreceipted execution this module exists to end.
  pub fn record(root: &Path, receipt: &ExecReceipt) -> Result<(), String> {
      let path = log_path(root, &receipt.warrant_id);
      if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
          std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)
              .map_err(|e| format!("cannot create {}: {e}", parent.display()))?;
      }
      let line = serde_json::to_string(receipt)
          .map_err(|e| format!("cannot serialize an exec receipt: {e}"))?;
      use std::io::Write as _;
      let mut file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
          .create(true)
          .append(true)
          .open(&path)
          .map_err(|e| format!("cannot open {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
      writeln!(file, "{line}").map_err(|e| format!("cannot append to {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
      file.flush().map_err(|e| format!("cannot flush {}: {e}", path.display()))
  }

  /// A warrant's receipts, with the count of lines that would not parse (never skipped silently).
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub struct ExecLog {
      /// The receipts, in the order written.
      pub receipts: Vec<ExecReceipt>,
      /// Lines that exist and would not parse.
      pub unreadable_lines: usize,
  }

  /// Read one warrant's receipts. An absent log is an empty log.
  #[must_use]
  pub fn read_for(root: &Path, warrant_id: &str) -> ExecLog {
      let Ok(raw) = std::fs::read_to_string(log_path(root, warrant_id)) else {
          return ExecLog::default();
      };
      let mut log = ExecLog::default();
      for line in raw.lines().filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty()) {
          match serde_json::from_str::<ExecReceipt>(line) {
              Ok(r) if r.format == EXEC_RECEIPT_FORMAT => log.receipts.push(r),
              _ => log.unreadable_lines += 1,
          }
      }
      log
  }
  ```

  ```rust
          [ExecAdmission { surface: ExecSurface::Process, sha256: digest.clone() }].into_iter().collect();

      let modified = dir.join(if cfg!(windows) { "warrantor.exe" } else { "warrantor" });
      let mut bytes = std::fs::read(agent()).expect("read");
      bytes.push(0x00);
      std::fs::write(&modified, &bytes).expect("write");

      let err = supervise_run(&state, &request(&dir, "wrt_exec_refuse", &modified.to_string_lossy(), Some(pinned.clone())))
          .expect_err("a modified artifact is refused");
      assert!(err.contains("gate artifacts"), "{err}");
      assert!(!err.contains(&digest), "the admitted digest is not disclosed: {err}");
      assert_eq!(state.get("wrt_exec_refuse"), None, "nothing was registered, because nothing ran");
      assert_eq!(state.completion("wrt_exec_refuse"), None);
      let log = exec::read_for(&dir, "wrt_exec_refuse");
      assert_eq!(log.receipts.len(), 1);
      assert_eq!(log.receipts[0].verdict, ExecVerdict::Refused);
      assert_eq!(log.receipts[0].phase, ExecPhase::Spawn);
      assert_ne!(log.receipts[0].sha256, digest);

      // The renamed, byte-identical copy gets the opposite verdict and actually runs.
      let renamed = dir.join(if cfg!(windows) { "renamed.exe" } else { "renamed" });
      std::fs::copy(agent(), &renamed).expect("copy");
      let code = supervise_run(&state, &request(&dir, "wrt_exec_ok", &renamed.to_string_lossy(), Some(pinned)))
          .expect("a byte-identical artifact runs");
      assert_eq!(code, 0);
      let log = exec::read_for(&dir, "wrt_exec_ok");
      assert_eq!(log.receipts[0].verdict, ExecVerdict::Admitted);
      assert_eq!(log.receipts[0].sha256, digest, "every EXEC receipt carries the digest");
      assert_eq!(state.completion("wrt_exec_ok").map(|c| c.exit_code), Some(0));
  }
  ```

  ```rust
  #[test]
  fn grant_with_exec_pins_and_run_refuses_or_admits_by_bytes_through_the_real_binary() {
      let root = tempdir("cli").join(".warrantor");
      let digest_out = warrantor(&root, &["exec", "digest", &artifact().to_string_lossy()]);
      assert!(digest_out.status.success(), "{}", stderr(&digest_out));
      let digest = stdout(&digest_out).split_whitespace().next().expect("digest").to_string();
      assert_eq!(digest.len(), 64);

      let grant = warrantor(&root, &["grant", "--goal", "exec gate", "--tools", "git",
          "--exec", &format!("process={digest}")]);
      assert!(grant.status.success(), "{}", stderr(&grant));
      let id = stdout(&grant).lines().next().and_then(|l| l.split_whitespace().nth(1))
          .expect("warrant id").to_string();

      // Same name, different bytes: refused at preflight, no supervisor log, receipt written.
      let dir = tempdir("cli-artifacts");
      let modified = dir.join(if cfg!(windows) { "warrantor.exe" } else { "warrantor" });
      let mut bytes = std::fs::read(artifact()).expect("read");
      bytes.push(0x00);
      std::fs::write(&modified, &bytes).expect("write");
      let refused = warrantor(&root, &["run", &id, "--", &modified.to_string_lossy(), "--help"]);
      assert!(!refused.status.success());
      assert!(stderr(&refused).contains("gate artifacts"), "{}", stderr(&refused));
      assert!(!root.join("logs").join(format!("{id}.log")).exists(), "no supervisor was started");
      let log = exec::read_for(&root, &id);
      assert_eq!(log.receipts.len(), 1);
      assert_eq!((log.receipts[0].phase, log.receipts[0].verdict), (ExecPhase::Preflight, ExecVerdict::Refused));

      // Renamed, byte-identical: admitted at preflight AND at spawn, and it runs to completion.
      let renamed = dir.join(if cfg!(windows) { "renamed.exe" } else { "renamed" });
      std::fs::copy(artifact(), &renamed).expect("copy");
      let admitted = warrantor(&root, &["run", &id, "--", &renamed.to_string_lossy(), "--help"]);
      assert!(admitted.status.success(), "{}", stderr(&admitted));
      let done = wait_for_completion(&root, &id);
      assert_eq!(done.exit_code, 0);
      let log = exec::read_for(&root, &id);
      let phases: Vec<(ExecPhase, ExecVerdict)> = log.receipts.iter().map(|r| (r.phase, r.verdict)).collect();
      assert_eq!(phases, vec![
          (ExecPhase::Preflight, ExecVerdict::Refused),
          (ExecPhase::Preflight, ExecVerdict::Admitted),
          (ExecPhase::Spawn, ExecVerdict::Admitted),
      ]);
      assert!(log.receipts.iter().all(|r| r.sha256.len() == 64), "every EXEC receipt carries the digest");

      let shown = warrantor(&root, &["exec", "log", &id]);
      assert!(shown.status.success());
      assert!(stdout(&shown).contains("spawn") && stdout(&shown).contains(&digest), "{}", stdout(&shown));
  }
  ```

**Acceptance (L4-05 verification gate, mapped):** renamed byte-identical artifact → same verdict (`Admitted`, Steps 6/10/12); same-named modified artifact → `Refused` at `Gate::Artifacts` before any process, daemon record or completion exists (Steps 10/12); every EXEC receipt — admitted, unpinned, refused, preflight or spawn — carries `sha256` (Steps 7/10/12); strict mode = any declared admission, and an undeclared or wrong-surface artifact is refused under it (E-04, Step 6); the refusal discloses the gate and the attempted digest only; existing warrants keep their bytes and signatures (Step 8); `bound_strengths` reports the new bound and its tier is promoted only on an observed refusal on every kernel CI runs (Step 15).

### Task 2.5: Generic HTTP adapter over the destination catalog (L4-27)

Anchor (plan-brief.md, L4-27): "A worker-control script exchanged commands and results through a then-public dataset acting as a pull-based command-and-control channel, polling every five seconds (First-party, OpenAI S01 §IV.B): a generic HTTP loop, not a named integration" — so the long tail of outbound HTTP becomes a governed effect whose destination is a catalog capability (L4-23), whose payload carries a data class the catalog entry must permit, and whose timing lands in the receipt graph (L7-09).

**What this task builds, in one paragraph.** A fifth staged effect, `http.call`, next to the four GitHub effects. Its published MCP schema has no `url`, `host`, `endpoint` or any other destination-shaped parameter: the only way to say *where* is `capability`, an enum populated from the warrant's egress catalog, so an uncataloged destination is unexpressible rather than denied. The proxy decides the capability through the existing `EgressBroker` at call time (so a smuggled raw address is refused and receipted), the effect is staged like any other Write, and at settle time a new `HttpAdapter` — holding whatever bearer token the operator configured, which the agent never sees — re-decides through `warrantor_egress::decide`, checks method and payload data class against the catalog entry, performs the call, and records `warrantor.http-call/1` timing records. The response body never re-enters an agent context: only its digest and size are kept (the L5-11 admission of a body into memory is a later task; here the body is quarantined by not being returned at all).

**What it does not change.** `bound_strengths()["egress_hosts"]` stays `Mediated`; the adapter runs in the settling process and the proxy is still a chokepoint the agent could decline to use. No new trust root, no DNS resolution, no network namespace. `Verdict::Deny { gate }` in the notary is untouched.

Task 1.2 names capabilities as `host:<H>` sugar or a declared name, resolved through its `Vocabulary::names(&self) -> Vec<String>` and `Vocabulary::resolve(&self, value: &str) -> Result<String, DenyReason>` (Task 1.2 Produces); this section names them with the broker's own `net.egress:<host>` string from `capability_for`, which exists today. The seam is two calls: `tool_spec` takes its enum from `broker.capabilities()` and `capability_refusal` decides through `broker.decide_capability`. After Task 1.2 lands, `tool_spec` takes the enum from `proxy.vocabulary().names()` and `capability_refusal` calls `resolve` first, then `broker.decide` on the resolved host; nothing else in this section moves. Until then a bare `--egress H` is the only catalog, and this section makes those sugar entries read-only (`GET`, `public`): a webhook `POST` with a non-public payload needs a declared capability. Absent means none, throughout.
- *Task 2.1* (`effects.rs`) refuses an unclassified tool in strict mode. Its `DecompositionRegistry::builtin()` (Task 2.1 Produces) holds the four GitHub tools; if it has merged, Step 3 also inserts `http.call` there as `net`, or strict mode refuses the tool this section publishes.

The adapter itself is unchanged: it is an `EffectPerformer`, and Task 2.3 wraps performers, it does not replace them.

```rust
/// string exactly as it decides the host the capability was derived from.
```

```rust
    /// The derived catalog itself, for an adapter that must decide against the same object the
    /// proxy decided against. `None` when the warrant permits no egress.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn catalog(&self) -> Option<&broker::DestinationCatalog> {
        self.catalog.as_ref()
    }

    /// Every capability this warrant grants, in bound order. This is the closed vocabulary the
    /// HTTP tool's schema publishes: there is no other way to say where a call goes.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn capabilities(&self) -> &[String] {
        &self.chain
    }

    /// Decide a capability *name* rather than a host.
    ///
    /// A string without the [`EGRESS_CAPABILITY_PREFIX`] is a raw address however it is spelled,
    /// and is refused as [`DenyReason::NotACapability`] before the catalog is consulted.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn decide_capability(&self, capability: &str) -> broker::EgressVerdict {
        match capability.strip_prefix(EGRESS_CAPABILITY_PREFIX) {
            Some(logical_endpoint) if !logical_endpoint.is_empty() => {
                self.decide(logical_endpoint)
            }
            _ => broker::EgressVerdict::Deny {
                reason: DenyReason::NotACapability,
            },
        }
    }
```

```rust
//! L4-27: the governed HTTP call. The agent names a capability, never a destination; the
//! payload's data class is bounded by the catalog entry; every call's timing is recorded.

use serde_json::Value;
use warrantor_warrant::adapters::http::{
    tool_spec, ARG_BODY, ARG_CAPABILITY, ARG_DATA_CLASS, ARG_METHOD, ARG_PATH, TOOL,
};
use warrantor_warrant::egress::{capability_for, EgressBroker, DESTINATION_KEYS};
use warrantor_warrant::{SideEffectClass, WarrantBounds};

const NOW: u64 = 1_786_000_000;

fn bounds(hosts: &[&str]) -> WarrantBounds {
    WarrantBounds {
        tools: ["git", TOOL].into_iter().map(str::to_string).collect(),
        write_paths: ["src/**".to_string()].into_iter().collect(),
        egress_hosts: hosts.iter().map(|h| (*h).to_string()).collect(),
        staged_classes: [SideEffectClass::Write].into_iter().collect(),
        expires_at: NOW + 3600,
        budget_cents_observed: None,
        delegation_depth: 2,
    }
}

/// The L4-23 static gate: no destination-shaped parameter exists on the published schema, and
/// the schema is closed, so a destination is unexpressible rather than refused.
#[test]
fn the_http_schema_has_no_destination_parameter_and_is_closed() {
    let broker = EgressBroker::for_bounds(&bounds(&["api.github.com"]));
    let spec = tool_spec(&broker);
    assert_eq!(spec.name, TOOL);
    let schema = spec.input_schema;
    assert_eq!(schema["additionalProperties"], Value::Bool(false));
    let properties = schema["properties"].as_object().expect("properties");
    for key in DESTINATION_KEYS {
        assert!(!properties.contains_key(*key), "schema publishes destination key {key}");
    }
    let capabilities: Vec<&str> = schema["properties"][ARG_CAPABILITY]["enum"]
        .as_array()
        .expect("capability enum")
        .iter()
        .filter_map(Value::as_str)
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(capabilities, vec![capability_for("api.github.com").as_str()]);
    let required: Vec<&str> = schema["required"].as_array().expect("required").iter().filter_map(Value::as_str).collect();
    for key in [ARG_CAPABILITY, ARG_METHOD, ARG_PATH, ARG_DATA_CLASS] {
        assert!(required.contains(&key), "{key} must be required");
    }
    assert!(!required.contains(&ARG_BODY));
}

/// A warrant with no egress publishes a capability enum that is EMPTY, not absent: the tool is
/// still described, and nothing can be put in it.
#[test]
fn a_warrant_with_no_egress_publishes_an_empty_capability_enum() {
    let broker = EgressBroker::for_bounds(&bounds(&[]));
    let schema = tool_spec(&broker).input_schema;
    assert_eq!(schema["properties"][ARG_CAPABILITY]["enum"], Value::Array(vec![]));
}
```
