Implement the types and `tool_spec` in `rust/warrant/src/adapters/http.rs` (replacing the stub from Step 3):

```rust
//! L4-27 — the governed HTTP call.
//!
//! Outbound HTTP for the long tail nobody writes an adapter for. Three properties, in order of
//! how much they matter:
//!
//! 1. **The agent never names a destination.** The tool takes a `capability`, an enum over the
//!    warrant's egress catalog; there is no `url`, `host` or `endpoint` parameter and the
//!    schema is closed. An uncataloged destination is not refused, it is unexpressible. A raw
//!    address smuggled into the `capability` field is refused by the proxy at call time.
//! 2. **The payload declares a data class**, and the catalog entry carries the highest class
//!    it may carry. Absent means `public`.
//! 3. **The response never re-enters an agent context.** The adapter runs at settle, when the
//!    agent is gone; it keeps the status, a digest and a byte count, never the body.
//!
//! Where this holds: the proxy chokepoint and the settling process. `bound_strengths()` still
//! says `egress_hosts` is `Mediated`, and nothing here changes that.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::json;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use warrantor_egress as broker;

use crate::egress::{EgressBroker, EgressRefusal, EGRESS_CAPABILITY_PREFIX};
use crate::mcp::ToolSpec;
use crate::proxy::ToolCall;
use crate::settle::EffectPerformer;
use crate::staging::StagedEffect;

/// The tool name the agent calls.
pub const TOOL: &str = "http.call";
/// Format of each timing record the adapter emits.
pub const HTTP_CALL_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.http-call/1";
pub const ARG_CAPABILITY: &str = "capability";
pub const ARG_METHOD: &str = "method";
pub const ARG_PATH: &str = "path";
pub const ARG_BODY: &str = "body";
pub const ARG_DATA_CLASS: &str = "data_class";

/// Methods a capability may permit. `CONNECT`, `OPTIONS` and `TRACE` are not expressible.
pub const METHODS: &[&str] = &["GET", "HEAD", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"];

/// Payload data classes, ordered: a request may carry at most the entry's ceiling.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum DataClass {
    Public,
    Internal,
    Confidential,
    Restricted,
}

impl DataClass {
    /// The lower-case words the schema publishes, in order.
    pub const WORDS: &'static [&'static str] = &["public", "internal", "confidential", "restricted"];

    /// Parse the lower-case word. Anything else is not a class.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn parse(word: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match word {
            "public" => Some(Self::Public),
            "internal" => Some(Self::Internal),
            "confidential" => Some(Self::Confidential),
            "restricted" => Some(Self::Restricted),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The ceiling an entry declares. `None` reads as `Public`: absent means the least.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn ceiling_of(entry: &broker::CatalogEntry) -> Result<Self, String> {
        match entry.max_data_class.as_deref() {
            None => Ok(Self::Public),
            Some(word) => Self::parse(word).ok_or_else(|| {
                format!(
                    "the catalog entry for {} declares max_data_class {word:?}, which is not a \
                     data class; refusing rather than guessing",
                    entry.logical_endpoint
                )
            }),
        }
    }
}

/// What the adapter hands the transport. `url` is built by the adapter from the catalog entry;
/// the agent contributed only `method`, `path` and `body`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct HttpRequest {
    pub url: String,
    pub method: String,
    pub body: Option<String>,
    /// The bearer token for this endpoint, held by the settling process. Never logged.
    pub bearer: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct HttpResponse {
    pub status: u16,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
}

/// A minimal transport, injected so the adapter is testable without a network — the same shape
/// and the same reason as [`crate::adapters::github::GitHubTransport`].
pub trait HttpTransport {
    /// Send one request. Errors are human-readable; the settle engine stops on the first.
    fn send(&mut self, request: &HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, String>;
}

/// One performed call, for the receipt graph (L7-09). Carries digests, never bodies.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct HttpCallRecord {
    pub format: String,
    pub handle: String,
    pub capability: String,
    pub logical_endpoint: String,
    pub method: String,
    pub path: String,
    pub data_class: DataClass,
    pub catalog_digest: String,
    pub request_digest: String,
    pub status: u16,
    pub response_digest: String,
    pub response_bytes: u64,
    pub started_at_ms: u64,
    pub finished_at_ms: u64,
}

fn sha256_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    hasher.update(bytes);
    format!("sha256:{}", hex::encode(hasher.finalize()))
}

/// The tool as the agent sees it. Closed schema; the only destination vocabulary is the
/// capability enum, taken from the broker the proxy will decide against.
#[must_use]
pub fn tool_spec(broker: &EgressBroker) -> ToolSpec {
    ToolSpec {
        name: TOOL.to_string(),
        description: "Make one outbound HTTP request to a destination this warrant grants as a \
                      capability. There is no URL parameter: choose a capability, a method, a \
                      path under that destination, and declare the payload's data class. The \
                      request is staged and performed only if a human settles the warrant; you \
                      receive a handle, never the response body."
            .to_string(),
        input_schema: json!({
            "type": "object",
            "additionalProperties": false,
            "required": [ARG_CAPABILITY, ARG_METHOD, ARG_PATH, ARG_DATA_CLASS],
            "properties": {
                ARG_CAPABILITY: { "type": "string", "enum": broker.capabilities() },
```

```rust
/// The proxy's check for this tool: decide the named capability through the broker.
///
/// Returns the refusal to record, or `None` for any other tool and for a permitted capability.
/// A missing `capability` argument is a raw (empty) destination and is refused, never skipped —
/// the same fail-closed reading [`crate::egress::destinations_of`] gives an unresolvable
/// destination argument.
#[must_use]
pub fn capability_refusal(call: &ToolCall, broker: &EgressBroker) -> Option<EgressRefusal> {
    if call.tool != TOOL {
        return None;
    }
    let named = call.arguments.get(ARG_CAPABILITY).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    match broker.decide_capability(&named) {
        broker::EgressVerdict::Allow { .. } => None,
        broker::EgressVerdict::Deny { reason } => Some(EgressRefusal {
            tool: TOOL.to_string(),
            argument: ARG_CAPABILITY.to_string(),
            destination: named
                .strip_prefix(EGRESS_CAPABILITY_PREFIX)
                .unwrap_or(&named)
                .to_string(),
            capability: named,
            reason,
            count: 1,
        }),
    }
}
```

```rust
fn tempdir(tag: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
    let mut path = std::env::temp_dir();
    path.push(format!(
        "warrantor-http-{tag}-{}",
        std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
            .unwrap_or(0)
    ));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&path).expect("tempdir");
    path
}

/// A catalog with one declared capability: POST + GET, confidential ceiling.
fn declared_catalog() -> DestinationCatalog {
    let mut catalog = DestinationCatalog {
        version: "warrantor.destination-catalog/test".to_string(),
        entries: vec![CatalogEntry {
            logical_endpoint: "hooks.example.com".to_string(),
            addresses: vec!["hooks.example.com".to_string()],
            tls_identity: None,
            permitted_methods: vec!["GET".to_string(), "POST".to_string()],
            expires_at: NOW + 3600,
            max_data_class: Some("confidential".to_string()),
        }],
        digest: String::new(),
        signature: None,
    };
    catalog.digest = catalog.compute_digest();
    catalog
}

struct FakeHttp {
    sent: Vec<HttpRequest>,
    status: u16,
}

impl HttpTransport for FakeHttp {
    fn send(&mut self, request: &HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, String> {
        self.sent.push(request.clone());
        Ok(HttpResponse { status: self.status, body: b"{\"ok\":true}".to_vec() })
    }
}

fn ticking_clock() -> Box<dyn FnMut() -> u64> {
    let mut t = 1_000u64;
    Box::new(move || {
        t += 7;
        t
    })
}

fn warrant(hosts: &[&str]) -> (Warrant, SigningKey) {
    let issuer = SigningKey::from_bytes(&[1; 32]);
    let settle_key = SigningKey::from_bytes(&[2; 32]);
    let w = Warrant::grant("wrt_http", "notify", "spiffe://muveraai.com/agent/alpha", bounds(hosts), NOW, &settle_key.verifying_key(), &issuer).expect("grant");
    (w, settle_key)
}

fn staged(dir: &std::path::Path, pairs: &[(&str, &str)]) -> StagingQueue {
    let mut q = StagingQueue::open(dir.join("q.jsonl"), "wrt_http", EffectRegistry::builtin()).expect("open");
    q.stage(TOOL, args(pairs), NOW).expect("stage");
    q
}

fn adapter(catalog: DestinationCatalog, status: u16) -> HttpAdapter<FakeHttp> {
    HttpAdapter::new(FakeHttp { sent: Vec::new(), status }, catalog, ticking_clock())
}

/// The happy path: a POST inside the declared capability is performed, the real id is the
/// status and the response digest, and one timing record exists.
#[test]
fn a_call_inside_the_capability_is_performed_and_recorded() {
    let dir = tempdir("perform");
    let (mut w, key) = warrant(&["hooks.example.com"]);
    let q = staged(&dir, &[
        (ARG_CAPABILITY, &capability_for("hooks.example.com")),
        (ARG_METHOD, "POST"),
        (ARG_PATH, "/notify?run=1"),
        (ARG_BODY, "{\"text\":\"done\"}"),
        (ARG_DATA_CLASS, "internal"),
    ]);
    let mut adapter = adapter(declared_catalog(), 202).with_bearer("hooks.example.com", "s3cret");

    let report = settle(&mut w, &q, None, &key.verifying_key(), &mut adapter).expect("settle");

    assert!(report.complete, "{:?}", report.boundary);
    assert_eq!(w.state, WarrantState::Settled);
    let records: &[HttpCallRecord] = adapter.records();
    assert_eq!(records.len(), 1);
    let r = &records[0];
    assert_eq!(r.format, HTTP_CALL_FORMAT);
    assert_eq!(r.method, "POST");
    assert_eq!(r.logical_endpoint, "hooks.example.com");
    assert_eq!(r.data_class, DataClass::Internal);
    assert_eq!(r.status, 202);
    assert!(r.finished_at_ms > r.started_at_ms, "timing lands in the record");
    assert!(r.response_digest.starts_with("sha256:"));
    assert_eq!(r.response_bytes, 11);
    let sent = &adapter.transport().sent[0];
    assert_eq!(sent.url, "https://hooks.example.com/notify?run=1");
    assert_eq!(sent.bearer.as_deref(), Some("s3cret"));
}
```

```rust
/// Refuse a path that could move the request off the cataloged destination.
///
/// # Errors
/// The reason, in terms the operator can act on.
pub fn validate_path(path: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    if !path.starts_with('/') {
        return Err(format!("path {path:?} must start with '/'"));
    }
    if path.starts_with("//") {
        return Err(format!("path {path:?} is protocol-relative and would name a host"));
    }
    if path.contains("://") || path.contains('@') {
        return Err(format!("path {path:?} carries a scheme or credentials; the destination is the capability's"));
    }
    if path.chars().any(|c| c.is_whitespace() || c.is_control()) {
        return Err(format!("path {path:?} contains whitespace or a control character"));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Performs governed HTTP calls against the catalog the proxy decided against.
pub struct HttpAdapter<T: HttpTransport> {
    transport: T,
    catalog: broker::DestinationCatalog,
    bearers: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    clock: Box<dyn FnMut() -> u64>,
    records: Vec<HttpCallRecord>,
}

impl<T: HttpTransport> HttpAdapter<T> {
    /// Build an adapter over `catalog`. `clock` returns milliseconds and is called twice per call.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new(transport: T, catalog: broker::DestinationCatalog, clock: Box<dyn FnMut() -> u64>) -> Self {
        Self { transport, catalog, bearers: BTreeMap::new(), clock, records: Vec::new() }
    }

    /// Hold a bearer token for one logical endpoint. The agent never sees it: this runs at settle.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn with_bearer(mut self, logical_endpoint: &str, token: &str) -> Self {
        self.bearers.insert(logical_endpoint.to_string(), token.to_string());
        self
    }

    /// Every call performed, in order, for the receipt graph.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn records(&self) -> &[HttpCallRecord] {
        &self.records
    }

    /// The transport, so a test can read what was sent.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn transport(&self) -> &T {
        &self.transport
    }

    fn argument<'a>(effect: &'a StagedEffect, name: &str) -> Result<&'a str, String> {
        effect.arguments.get(name).map(String::as_str).ok_or_else(|| format!("{TOOL} requires {name}"))
    }

    fn perform_call(&mut self, effect: &StagedEffect) -> Result<String, String> {
        let capability = Self::argument(effect, ARG_CAPABILITY)?.to_string();
        let method = Self::argument(effect, ARG_METHOD)?.to_string();
        let path = Self::argument(effect, ARG_PATH)?.to_string();
        let class_word = Self::argument(effect, ARG_DATA_CLASS)?;
        let data_class = DataClass::parse(class_word)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("{class_word:?} is not a data class; one of {:?}", DataClass::WORDS))?;
        let body = effect.arguments.get(ARG_BODY).cloned();

        if !METHODS.contains(&method.as_str()) {
            return Err(format!("{method:?} is not a method this adapter can express; one of {METHODS:?}"));
        }
        if matches!(method.as_str(), "GET" | "HEAD") && body.is_some() {
            return Err(format!("{method} carries no body"));
        }
        validate_path(&path)?;

        // Decide again, here, against the catalog: the settle process trusts the proxy's
        // decision no more than the proxy trusted the agent's.
        let logical_endpoint = capability
            .strip_prefix(EGRESS_CAPABILITY_PREFIX)
            .filter(|e| !e.is_empty())
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("{capability:?} is not a capability"))?
            .to_string();
        let request = broker::EgressRequest {
            capability: capability.clone(),
            logical_endpoint: logical_endpoint.clone(),
            chain_capabilities: vec![capability.clone()],
            enforcement_mode: "advisory".to_string(),
            is_discovery: false,
            has_approval: false,
        };
        let (pinned, catalog_digest) = match broker::decide(&request, Some(&self.catalog)) {
            broker::EgressVerdict::Allow { pinned_addresses, catalog_digest, .. } => (pinned_addresses, catalog_digest),
            broker::EgressVerdict::Deny { reason } => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "egress to {logical_endpoint} is refused at settle: {}",
                    crate::egress::reason_phrase(reason)
                ))
            }
        };
        let entry = self.catalog.find(&logical_endpoint).ok_or_else(|| format!("{logical_endpoint} left the catalog"))?.clone();
        if !entry.permitted_methods.iter().any(|m| m == &method) {
            return Err(format!(
                "the capability for {logical_endpoint} permits {:?}, not {method}; a bare --egress host permits GET only and a write needs a declared capability",
                entry.permitted_methods
            ));
        }
        let ceiling = DataClass::ceiling_of(&entry)?;
        if data_class > ceiling {
            return Err(format!(
                "the payload is declared {class_word} and the capability for {logical_endpoint} carries at most {:?}",
                DataClass::WORDS[ceiling as usize]
            ));
        }
        let [address] = pinned.as_slice() else {
            return Err(format!(
                "the capability for {logical_endpoint} pins {} addresses; this adapter sends to exactly one and does not choose",
                pinned.len()
            ));
        };

        let http_request = HttpRequest {
            url: format!("https://{address}{path}"),
            method: method.clone(),
            body: body.clone(),
            bearer: self.bearers.get(&logical_endpoint).cloned(),
        };
        let request_digest = sha256_hex(format!("{method} {path}\n{}", body.unwrap_or_default()).as_bytes());
        let started_at_ms = (self.clock)();
        let response = self.transport.send(&http_request)?;
        let finished_at_ms = (self.clock)();
        let response_digest = sha256_hex(&response.body);
        let real_id = format!("http {} {response_digest}", response.status);
        self.records.push(HttpCallRecord {
            format: HTTP_CALL_FORMAT.to_string(),
            handle: effect.handle.clone(),
            capability,
            logical_endpoint,
            method,
            path,
            data_class,
            catalog_digest,
            request_digest,
            status: response.status,
            response_digest,
            response_bytes: response.body.len() as u64,
            started_at_ms,
            finished_at_ms,
        });
        Ok(real_id)
    }
}

impl<T: HttpTransport> EffectPerformer for HttpAdapter<T> {
    fn perform(&mut self, effect: &StagedEffect, _resolved: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<String, String> {
        if effect.tool != TOOL {
            return Err(format!("the HTTP adapter does not implement {}", effect.tool));
        }
        self.perform_call(effect)
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 8 — Wire the real transport and the routed performer into `warrantor settle`, and persist the records.**

No unit test exists for the binary's `build_performer`; this step is verified by `cargo build` and the live run in Step 9. In `rust/warrant/src/bin/warrantor.rs`, after `HttpsGitHub` (line 2210) add:

```rust
/// A real HTTPS transport for the governed HTTP call. Built exactly like [`HttpsGitHub`]: both
/// timeouts set, redirects refused (a redirect would carry the bearer somewhere the catalog did
/// not name), status reported and body digested by the adapter rather than echoed.
struct HttpsTransport {
    agent: ureq::Agent,
}

impl warrantor_warrant::adapters::http::HttpTransport for HttpsTransport {
    fn send(
        &mut self,
        request: &warrantor_warrant::adapters::http::HttpRequest,
    ) -> Result<warrantor_warrant::adapters::http::HttpResponse, String> {
        let mut req = self.agent.request(&request.method, &request.url).set("user-agent", "warrantor");
        if let Some(bearer) = &request.bearer {
            req = req.set("authorization", &format!("Bearer {bearer}"));
        }
        let sent = match &request.body {
            Some(body) => req.set("content-type", "application/json").send_string(body),
            None => req.call(),
        };
        match sent {
            Ok(response) | Err(ureq::Error::Status(_, response)) => {
                let status = response.status();
                let mut body = Vec::new();
                response
                    .into_reader()
                    .take(8 * 1024 * 1024)
                    .read_to_end(&mut body)
                    .map_err(|e| format!("read response: {e}"))?;
                Ok(warrantor_warrant::adapters::http::HttpResponse { status, body })
            }
            Err(other) => Err(format!("the request failed before a response: {other}")),
        }
    }
}

/// Routes each staged effect to the adapter that performs it.
struct RoutedPerformer {
    http: warrantor_warrant::adapters::http::HttpAdapter<HttpsTransport>,
    other: Box<dyn EffectPerformer>,
}

impl EffectPerformer for RoutedPerformer {
    fn perform(
        &mut self,
        effect: &StagedEffect,
        resolved: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
    ) -> Result<String, String> {
        if effect.tool == warrantor_warrant::adapters::http::TOOL {
            self.http.perform(effect, resolved)
        } else {
            self.other.perform(effect, resolved)
        }
    }
}

fn millis_now() -> u64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_millis() as u64)
        .unwrap_or(0)
}
```

(`Read` is imported inside function bodies in this binary — lines 4988, 5383 and 6269 — never at the top; do the same: put `use std::io::Read;` as the first line of `fn send`, for `take`/`read_to_end`.) `Ok(r) | Err(ureq::Error::Status(_, r))` is the pattern this binary already uses at lines 5410 and 6261.

Rewrite `build_performer` (lines 2786-2818) to take the bounds and return the router. Keep the existing GitHub body as `fn build_github_performer() -> Box<dyn EffectPerformer>` (rename only), then:

```rust
/// Build the performer for a settle: HTTP over the warrant's own catalog, GitHub when
/// configured, an honest refusal otherwise.
fn build_performer(bounds: &WarrantBounds) -> RoutedPerformer {
    let broker = warrantor_warrant::egress::EgressBroker::for_bounds(bounds);
    let catalog = broker.catalog().cloned().unwrap_or(warrantor_egress::DestinationCatalog {
        version: warrantor_warrant::egress::CATALOG_VERSION.to_string(),
        entries: Vec::new(),
        digest: String::new(),
        signature: None,
    });
    let agent = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
        .timeout_connect(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))
        .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30))
        .redirects(0)
        .build();
    let mut http = warrantor_warrant::adapters::http::HttpAdapter::new(
        HttpsTransport { agent },
        catalog,
        Box::new(millis_now),
    );
    // Bearer tokens per logical endpoint: WARRANTOR_HTTP_BEARER_<ENDPOINT> with '.', '-' and ':'
    // written as '_'. Read here, in the settling process; the agent never ran in it.
    for (key, value) in std::env::vars() {
        if let Some(endpoint) = key.strip_prefix("WARRANTOR_HTTP_BEARER_") {
            http = http.with_bearer(&endpoint.to_ascii_lowercase(), &value);
        }
    }
    RoutedPerformer { http, other: build_github_performer() }
}
```

The `warrantor_egress` crate is already a dependency of `warrantor-warrant` (Cargo.toml), so `warrantor_egress::DestinationCatalog` resolves in the binary without a manifest change.

### Task 2.6: Provenance labels on tool outputs and peer-proposal admission (L5-11, L5-12)

**Anchor.** L5-11: agents "received requests and assignments from other agents that they may have taken to be instructions" (S02 §Assignments, vetoes, and holds), and the blueprint's proof gate C-03 is "inject an instruction-shaped message from an unauthorized peer; assert effective authority is unchanged"; L5-12's gate adds "a peer proposal that includes a credential handle is refused at admission regardless of scope."

**What this task builds, in one paragraph.** Two things, both reachable from the CLI and both receipted. First, every response the agent endpoint hands back after a `Decision::Forward` or `Decision::Stage` carries a `warrantor.provenance/1` label — `origin`, `trust` (always `none`: nothing read through the proxy carries authority), `expiry` (the warrant's own `expires_at`), `compartment` (the warrant id) and `non_transitive: true` — placed *beside* the upstream's text in the MCP result's `_meta`, never spliced into it, because text is exactly the surface a label exists to describe. Second, a peer proposal is a signed `warrantor-agent-channel` `Message` whose payload is a `warrantor.peer-proposal/1` object naming proposer, population, task lineage, tool and arguments; `warrantor proposal admit <warrant-id> <envelope.json>` verifies the signature, refuses any payload containing a credential handle *before* looking at scope, checks population membership, binds the proposed work against the receiver's own `WarrantBounds` through the existing `Proxy::decide`, and writes a signed `warrantor.proposal-receipt/1` (`syscall: "msg"`, `decision_class: "delegate"`) whether it admitted or refused. Admission never executes anything and never changes a bound: an admitted proposal is a *proposal object* the receiver may act on through its own endpoint, where every call is decided again.

**What this task does not build, stated so the ledger cannot overstate it.** Durable-memory quarantine across a container reset (the second half of L5-11's verification) is not touched: no crate in `rust/warrant` holds agent memory, and labeling a store this crate does not own would be a label with nothing behind it. The proposer's *identity* is not established: the message signature is verified against the key embedded in the message (that is what `warrantor_agent_channel::Message::verify` does), which proves integrity and continuity, not who holds the key. There is no pinned peer directory — building one would be a new trust root, which Rule "no new trust root" forbids — so the receipt records the proposer's verifying key verbatim and the CLI says "key not pinned; identity not established". Task 3.1's principals are where that changes.

**Why `Proxy::decide` is the binding check and not a new evaluator.** L5-12 says the receiver evaluates the proposed work "against the receiver's own warrant only." The one place this crate already evaluates a tool call against a warrant is `rust/warrant/src/proxy.rs:186 pub fn decide(&mut self, call: &ToolCall) -> Decision`. A second evaluator for proposals would be a second definition of what the warrant allows, and the two would drift. So admission constructs a `ToolCall` from the proposal and asks the same engine, in `ProxyMode::Enforce`, with the receiver's bounds. A `Decision::Deny { bound, .. }` is a refusal at bind, receipted with the bound's name only — the same shape as `Decision::Deny`, and the same discipline as the notary's gate-only denial.

```rust
//           [--arg k=v ...] [--lineage <task-id> ...] [--class read|write|destructive|financial]
//           [--expires-in <seconds>] [--sequence <n>] --key-file <path> --out <envelope.json>
//        warrantor proposal admit <warrant-id> <envelope.json> [--export <path>]
//        warrantor proposal list <warrant-id>
//        warrantor verify <exported-proposal.json>
```

**Admission order, fixed.** Each gate is named by a word that lands in `ProposalVerdict::RefusedAtAdmission { gate }` and nothing else lands there — the offending value stays in `ProposalDecision::reason` for the terminal and is never in the receipt.
1. `format` — `envelope.format == PROPOSAL_ENVELOPE_FORMAT` and `envelope.message.format == MESSAGE_FORMAT`.
2. `signature` — `envelope.message.verify()` (integrity against the embedded key; identity not established, said in the CLI output).
3. `digest` — `format!("sha256:{}", sha256_hex(envelope.payload.as_bytes())) == envelope.message.payload_digest` (agent-channel prefixes its digests with `sha256:`; `report::sha256_hex` does not).
4. `replay` — `message_digest(&envelope.message)` not in `seen_message_digests`.
5. `class` — `envelope.message.class == ContentClass::TaskCoordination`; a message declared `CredentialShare`, `ExfiltrationAttempt` or `Unknown` is refused before the payload is parsed.
6. `payload` — the payload parses as `PeerProposal` with `format == PROPOSAL_FORMAT`.
7. `credential_handle` — `credential_handle_in(&payload_value)` over the **whole** payload, not only `arguments`. Three rules: any object key, case-insensitively, in `CREDENTIAL_KEYS = ["token","capability_token","credential","secret","api_key","authorization","bearer","password","private_key","settle_key"]`; any object carrying all four of `warrant_id`, `subject`, `expires_at`, `signature` (the exact field set of `crate::CapabilityToken`); any string value beginning with `Bearer ` (case-insensitive). This gate runs before scope is looked at: a proposal for a tool the warrant allows, carrying a token, is still refused here.
8. `lineage` — `proposal.proposer == envelope.message.sender.0`.
9. `population` — `AgentId(proposal.proposer.clone()).tenant() == AgentId(stored.warrant.claims.subject.clone()).tenant()` and `proposal.population` equals that segment. For `spiffe://muveraai.com/agent/a` the segment is `agent`, exactly as `AgentId::tenant` reads it.
10. `expired` — `proposal.expires_at > now` and `stored.warrant.claims.bounds.expires_at > now`.
11. Bind — `Proxy::new(stored.warrant.claims.bounds.clone(), ProxyMode::Enforce, EffectRegistry::github()).decide(&ToolCall { tool, arguments: flattened, side_effect })`. `Deny { bound, .. }` → `RefusedAtBind { bound: bound.to_string() }`; `Forward | Stage { .. }` → `Admitted`, with `label = Some(ProvenanceLabel::peer(...))` whose `expires_at` is `min(proposal.expires_at, bounds.expires_at)`. Nothing is forwarded and nothing is staged: the proxy instance is dropped.

Arguments are flattened the way `AgentEndpoint::call` flattens them at `mcp_endpoints.rs:1022–1028` (`v.as_str().map_or_else(|| v.to_string(), str::to_string)`), so the bind sees the same strings a real call would.

  ```rust
  use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
  use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

  use ed25519_dalek::{Signer, SigningKey, Verifier, VerifyingKey};
  use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  use serde_json::Value;
  use warrantor_agent_channel::{AgentId, ContentClass, Message, MESSAGE_FORMAT};
  use warrantor_trust_core::signing::SigningKeyWrapper;

  use crate::proxy::{Decision, Proxy, ProxyMode, ToolCall};
  use crate::report::{canonicalize, sha256_hex};
  use crate::staging::EffectRegistry;
  use crate::store::StoredWarrant;
  use crate::{SideEffectClass, WarrantError};

  /// How much authority an item may carry. There is one value.
  ///
  /// The enum exists so the label *states* it and so a second value would be a visible format
  /// change rather than a silent one. Authority comes from the warrant and from nowhere an agent
  /// reads.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
  pub enum Trust {
      /// Carries no authority. A peer's message is data with a source, never an instruction.
      None,
  }

  /// Who produced an item.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "kind")]
  pub enum Origin {
      /// An attached MCP server answered a forwarded call.
      Upstream { server: String, tool: String },
      /// This process queued an effect and returned a handle.
      Staged { handle: String },
      /// A peer proposed work.
      Peer { agent: String },
  }

  /// The five labels every item entering the agent's context carries (L5-11).
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  pub struct ProvenanceLabel {
      /// [`PROVENANCE_FORMAT`].
      pub format: String,
      /// Who produced it.
      pub origin: Origin,
      /// How much authority it may carry. Always [`Trust::None`].
      pub trust: Trust,
      /// When it must be forgotten: the warrant's own deadline, epoch seconds.
      pub expires_at: u64,
      /// Which task may read it: the warrant id.
      pub compartment: String,
      /// It cannot be forwarded with more trust than it arrived with. Always true.
      pub non_transitive: bool,
      /// SHA-256 hex of the content, so a fact can be traced to the read that introduced it.
      pub lineage: String,
  }

  impl ProvenanceLabel {
      fn new(origin: Origin, content: &[u8], expires_at: u64, compartment: &str) -> Self {
          Self {
              format: PROVENANCE_FORMAT.to_string(),
              origin,
              trust: Trust::None,
              expires_at,
              compartment: compartment.to_string(),
              non_transitive: true,
              lineage: sha256_hex(content),
          }
      }

      /// A label for an upstream's answer. `published_tool` is `<server>.<tool>`; an upstream name
      /// cannot contain a dot (`UpstreamSpec::parse` refuses one), so the first dot is the split.
      #[must_use]
      pub fn upstream(published_tool: &str, response_text: &str, expires_at: u64, compartment: &str) -> Self {
          let (server, tool) = published_tool
              .split_once('.')
              .map_or((published_tool, ""), |(s, t)| (s, t));
          Self::new(
              Origin::Upstream { server: server.to_string(), tool: tool.to_string() },
              response_text.as_bytes(),
              expires_at,
              compartment,
          )
      }

      /// A label for a staging handle this process minted.
      #[must_use]
      pub fn staged(handle: &str, expires_at: u64, compartment: &str) -> Self {
          Self::new(Origin::Staged { handle: handle.to_string() }, handle.as_bytes(), expires_at, compartment)
      }

      /// A label for an admitted peer proposal.
      #[must_use]
      pub fn peer(proposer: &str, payload: &str, expires_at: u64, compartment: &str) -> Self {
          Self::new(Origin::Peer { agent: proposer.to_string() }, payload.as_bytes(), expires_at, compartment)
      }
  }
  ```

  ```rust
  //! L5-12: a peer can propose work; it cannot grant authority, and it cannot carry a credential.

  use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

  use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
  use serde_json::{json, Value};
  use warrantor_agent_channel::ContentClass;
  use warrantor_trust_core::signing::SigningKeyWrapper;
  use warrantor_warrant::provenance::{
      admit, compose, credential_handle_in, receipt_for, sign_receipt, verify_receipt,
      verify_receipt_signed_by, Origin, PeerProposal, ProposalStore, ProposalVerdict, Trust,
      DELEGATE_DECISION_CLASS, MSG_SYSCALL, PROPOSAL_FORMAT, PROPOSAL_RECEIPT_FORMAT,
  };
  use warrantor_warrant::proxy::{Decision, Proxy, ProxyMode, ToolCall};
  use warrantor_warrant::staging::EffectRegistry;
  use warrantor_warrant::store::StoredWarrant;
  use warrantor_warrant::{SideEffectClass, Warrant, WarrantBounds};

  const NOW: u64 = 1_786_000_000;
  const RECEIVER: &str = "spiffe://muveraai.com/agent/receiver";
  const PEER: &str = "spiffe://muveraai.com/agent/peer";

  fn tempdir(tag: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
      let mut path = std::env::temp_dir();
      path.push(format!(
          "warrantor-proposal-{tag}-{}",
          std::time::SystemTime::now()
              .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
              .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
              .unwrap_or(0)
      ));
      std::fs::create_dir_all(&path).expect("tempdir");
      path
  }

  fn stored_open(id: &str, tools: &[&str]) -> StoredWarrant {
      let issuer = SigningKey::from_bytes(&[1; 32]);
      let settle = SigningKey::from_bytes(&[2; 32]);
      let bounds = WarrantBounds {
          tools: tools.iter().map(|t| (*t).to_string()).collect(),
          write_paths: BTreeSet::new(),
          egress_hosts: BTreeSet::new(),
          staged_classes: [SideEffectClass::Write].into_iter().collect(),
          expires_at: NOW + 3600,
          budget_cents_observed: None,
          delegation_depth: 1,
      };
      let warrant = Warrant::grant(id, "receive proposals", RECEIVER, bounds, NOW, &settle.verifying_key(), &issuer)
          .expect("grant");
      StoredWarrant { warrant, worktree: None, repo: None, branch: None, base_commit: None, staged_chain: None }
  }

  fn peer_key() -> SigningKeyWrapper {
      SigningKeyWrapper::from_bytes(&[7; 32])
  }

  fn proposal(tool: &str, arguments: &[(&str, Value)]) -> PeerProposal {
      PeerProposal {
          format: PROPOSAL_FORMAT.to_string(),
          proposer: PEER.to_string(),
          population: "agent".to_string(),
          task_lineage: vec!["task-root".to_string(), "task-7".to_string()],
          tool: tool.to_string(),
          arguments: arguments.iter().map(|(k, v)| ((*k).to_string(), v.clone())).collect(),
          side_effect: SideEffectClass::Read,
          expires_at: NOW + 600,
      }
  }

  #[test]
  fn a_credential_handle_is_found_at_any_depth_and_in_token_shape() {
      assert_eq!(credential_handle_in(&json!({"text": "hi"})), None);
      assert_eq!(credential_handle_in(&json!({"args": {"Token": "abc"}})), Some("/args/Token".to_string()));
      assert_eq!(
          credential_handle_in(&json!({"h": {"warrant_id": "w", "subject": "s", "expires_at": 1, "signature": "ff"}})),
          Some("/h".to_string())
      );
      assert_eq!(credential_handle_in(&json!({"x": ["Bearer eyJ"]})), Some("/x/0".to_string()));
  }

  fn a_proposal_carrying_a_credential_handle_is_refused_at_admission_regardless_of_scope() {
      // `selftest.echo` IS in the receiver's warrant. The credential is what refuses it, and the
      // receipt names the gate, not the token.
      let stored = stored_open("w-cred", &["selftest.echo"]);
      let env = compose(&proposal("selftest.echo", &[("text", json!("hi")), ("api_key", json!("sk-live-1"))]), "w-cred", 0, NOW, &peer_key())
          .expect("compose");

      assert_eq!(decision.verdict, ProposalVerdict::RefusedAtAdmission { gate: "credential_handle".to_string() });
      assert!(decision.label.is_none());
      let receipt = receipt_for(&env, &stored, &decision, NOW);
      let text = serde_json::to_string(&receipt).expect("json");
      assert!(!text.contains("sk-live-1"), "the receipt must not carry the credential: {text}");
  }

  #[test]
  fn admitting_a_proposal_leaves_effective_authority_unchanged() {
      let stored = stored_open("w-admit", &["selftest.echo"]);
      let before = stored.warrant.claims.bounds.clone();
      let env = compose(&proposal("selftest.echo", &[("text", json!("do this"))]), "w-admit", 0, NOW, &peer_key()).expect("compose");
      let decision = admit(&env, &stored, &BTreeSet::new(), NOW);
      assert_eq!(decision.verdict, ProposalVerdict::Admitted);
      let label = decision.label.expect("an admitted proposal is labeled");
      assert_eq!(label.origin, Origin::Peer { agent: PEER.to_string() });
      assert_eq!(label.trust, Trust::None);
      assert!(label.non_transitive);
      assert_eq!(label.expires_at, NOW + 600, "the shorter of proposal and warrant expiry");
      // The blueprint gate C-03: effective authority is unchanged. The bounds are signed claims,
      // and the proxy built from them still refuses what it refused before the proposal.
      assert_eq!(stored.warrant.claims.bounds, before);
      let mut proxy = Proxy::new(before, ProxyMode::Enforce, EffectRegistry::github());
      let call = ToolCall { tool: "github.create_pr".to_string(), arguments: BTreeMap::new(), side_effect: SideEffectClass::Write };
      assert!(matches!(proxy.decide(&call), Decision::Deny { bound: "tools", .. }));
  ```

  ```rust
  /// Object keys that make a payload a credential carrier, matched case-insensitively at any depth.
  pub const CREDENTIAL_KEYS: [&str; 10] = [
      "token", "capability_token", "credential", "secret", "api_key",
      "authorization", "bearer", "password", "private_key", "settle_key",
  ];

  /// The exact field set of [`crate::CapabilityToken`]. An object carrying all four is a token
  /// whatever it is called.
  const TOKEN_SHAPE: [&str; 4] = ["warrant_id", "subject", "expires_at", "signature"];

  /// The work a peer proposes. Data with a source; never an instruction.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  pub struct PeerProposal {
      /// [`PROPOSAL_FORMAT`].
      pub format: String,
      /// The proposing agent's SPIFFE id. Must equal the envelope's signed sender.
      pub proposer: String,
      /// The population the proposer claims membership of: the tenant segment of its id.
      pub population: String,
      /// Task lineage, root first.
      pub task_lineage: Vec<String>,
      /// The published tool name the peer proposes the receiver call.
      pub tool: String,
      /// Proposed arguments, as JSON.
      pub arguments: BTreeMap<String, Value>,
      /// The class the peer declares. A claim, used only for the bind check; the receiver's own
      /// endpoint classifies again if it ever acts on the proposal.
      pub side_effect: SideEffectClass,
      /// When the proposal must be forgotten, epoch seconds.
      pub expires_at: u64,
  }

  /// A signed message plus the exact payload bytes it signs, as one file.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  pub struct ProposalEnvelope {
      /// [`PROPOSAL_ENVELOPE_FORMAT`].
      pub format: String,
      /// The channel message; `channel_id` is the receiver's warrant id.
      pub message: Message,
      /// The proposal, serialized. Digested by the message; parsed here.
      pub payload: String,
  }

  /// Build a signed envelope for `proposal`, addressed to `receiver_warrant_id`.
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// [`WarrantError::Encode`] if the proposal does not serialize or signing fails.
  pub fn compose(
      proposal: &PeerProposal,
      receiver_warrant_id: &str,
      sequence: u64,
      timestamp: u64,
      signer: &SigningKeyWrapper,
  ) -> Result<ProposalEnvelope, WarrantError> {
      let payload = serde_json::to_string(proposal).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(e.to_string()))?;
      let message = Message::sign(
          receiver_warrant_id,
          AgentId(proposal.proposer.clone()),
          sequence,
          ContentClass::TaskCoordination,
          payload.as_bytes(),
          timestamp,
          signer,
      )
      .map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("sign proposal: {e}")))?;
      Ok(ProposalEnvelope { format: PROPOSAL_ENVELOPE_FORMAT.to_string(), message, payload })
  }

  /// The JSON-pointer path of the first credential handle in `value`, if any.
  #[must_use]
  pub fn credential_handle_in(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
      fn walk(value: &Value, path: &mut String) -> Option<String> {
          match value {
              Value::Object(map) => {
                  if TOKEN_SHAPE.iter().all(|k| map.contains_key(*k)) {
                      return Some(if path.is_empty() { "/".to_string() } else { path.clone() });
                  }
                  for (key, child) in map {
                      let lowered = key.to_ascii_lowercase();
                      let len = path.len();
                      path.push('/');
                      path.push_str(key);
                      if CREDENTIAL_KEYS.contains(&lowered.as_str()) {
                          return Some(path.clone());
                      }
                      if let Some(hit) = walk(child, path) {
                          return Some(hit);
                      }
                      path.truncate(len);
                  }
                  None
              }
              Value::Array(items) => {
                  for (index, child) in items.iter().enumerate() {
                      let len = path.len();
                      path.push('/');
                      path.push_str(&index.to_string());
                      if let Some(hit) = walk(child, path) {
                          return Some(hit);
                      }
                      path.truncate(len);
                  }
                  None
              }
              Value::String(s) if s.get(..7).is_some_and(|p| p.eq_ignore_ascii_case("bearer ")) => {
                  Some(path.clone())
              }
              _ => None,
          }
      }
      walk(value, &mut String::new())
  }

  /// SHA-256 hex of the canonical JSON of a message: the replay key.
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// [`WarrantError::Encode`] if the message does not serialize.
  pub fn message_digest(message: &Message) -> Result<String, WarrantError> {
      let value = serde_json::to_value(message).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(e.to_string()))?;
      let text = serde_json::to_string(&canonicalize(&value)).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(e.to_string()))?;
      Ok(sha256_hex(text.as_bytes()))
  }

  /// What admission decided. A refusal carries the gate or the bound, and nothing else.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "verdict")]
  pub enum ProposalVerdict {
      /// A proposal object exists. Nothing was granted and nothing was performed.
      Admitted,
      /// Refused before the receiver's warrant was consulted.
      RefusedAtAdmission { gate: String },
      /// Refused by the receiver's own bounds, by name.
      RefusedAtBind { bound: String },
  }

  /// The admission result, for the terminal and for the receipt.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub struct ProposalDecision {
      pub verdict: ProposalVerdict,
      /// A sentence for the operator. Never written into the receipt.
      pub reason: String,
      /// Present only when admitted.
      pub label: Option<ProvenanceLabel>,
      /// The parsed proposal, when the payload parsed.
      pub proposal: Option<PeerProposal>,
      /// The replay key.
      pub message_digest: String,
  }

  fn refused(gate: &str, reason: String, proposal: Option<PeerProposal>, digest: String) -> ProposalDecision {
      ProposalDecision {
          verdict: ProposalVerdict::RefusedAtAdmission { gate: gate.to_string() },
          reason,
          label: None,
          proposal,
          message_digest: digest,
      }
  }

  /// Admit or refuse a peer proposal against the receiver's own warrant. Pure: performs nothing.
  #[must_use]
  pub fn admit(
      envelope: &ProposalEnvelope,
      stored: &StoredWarrant,
      seen_message_digests: &BTreeSet<String>,
      now: u64,
  ) -> ProposalDecision {
      let digest = message_digest(&envelope.message).unwrap_or_default();
      if envelope.format != PROPOSAL_ENVELOPE_FORMAT || envelope.message.format != MESSAGE_FORMAT {
          return refused("format", format!("envelope declares {:?} / message {:?}; this build reads {PROPOSAL_ENVELOPE_FORMAT} / {MESSAGE_FORMAT}", envelope.format, envelope.message.format), None, digest);
      }
      if let Err(e) = envelope.message.verify() {
          return refused("signature", format!("the message does not verify against its own key: {e}"), None, digest);
      }
      if format!("sha256:{}", sha256_hex(envelope.payload.as_bytes())) != envelope.message.payload_digest {
          return refused("digest", "the payload is not the bytes the message signed".to_string(), None, digest);
      }
      if seen_message_digests.contains(&digest) {
          return refused("replay", format!("message {digest} was already decided for this warrant"), None, digest);
      }
      if envelope.message.class != ContentClass::TaskCoordination {
          return refused("class", format!("a proposal is task coordination; this message declares {:?} and is refused before its payload is read", envelope.message.class), None, digest);
      }
      let payload_value: Value = match serde_json::from_str(&envelope.payload) {
          Ok(v) => v,
          Err(e) => return refused("payload", format!("payload is not JSON: {e}"), None, digest),
      };
      let proposal: PeerProposal = match serde_json::from_value(payload_value.clone()) {
          Ok(p) if p.format == PROPOSAL_FORMAT => p,
          Ok(p) => return refused("payload", format!("payload declares {:?}; this build reads {PROPOSAL_FORMAT}", p.format), None, digest),
          Err(e) => return refused("payload", format!("payload is not a peer proposal: {e}"), None, digest),
      };
      if let Some(path) = credential_handle_in(&payload_value) {
          return refused("credential_handle", format!("the proposal carries a credential handle at {path}; a proposal never transfers a credential, whatever it proposes"), Some(proposal), digest);
      }
      if proposal.proposer != envelope.message.sender.0 {
          return refused("lineage", format!("the payload names proposer {:?} but the message was signed by {:?}", proposal.proposer, envelope.message.sender.0), Some(proposal), digest);
      }
      let receiver_population = AgentId(stored.warrant.claims.subject.clone()).tenant().to_string();
      let proposer_population = AgentId(proposal.proposer.clone()).tenant().to_string();
      if proposer_population != receiver_population || proposal.population != receiver_population {
          return refused("population", format!("proposer is in population {proposer_population:?} (claims {:?}); the receiver is in {receiver_population:?}", proposal.population), Some(proposal), digest);
      }
      let bounds = &stored.warrant.claims.bounds;
      if proposal.expires_at <= now || bounds.expires_at <= now {
          return refused("expired", format!("proposal expires at {}, warrant at {}, now is {now}", proposal.expires_at, bounds.expires_at), Some(proposal), digest);
      }
      let flattened: BTreeMap<String, String> = proposal
          .arguments
          .iter()
          .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.as_str().map_or_else(|| v.to_string(), str::to_string)))
          .collect();
      let call = ToolCall { tool: proposal.tool.clone(), arguments: flattened, side_effect: proposal.side_effect };
      let mut proxy = Proxy::new(bounds.clone(), ProxyMode::Enforce, EffectRegistry::github());
      match proxy.decide(&call) {
          Decision::Deny { reason, bound } => ProposalDecision {
              verdict: ProposalVerdict::RefusedAtBind { bound: bound.to_string() },
              reason: format!("the receiver's warrant refuses {}: {reason}", proposal.tool),
              label: None,
              proposal: Some(proposal),
              message_digest: digest,
          },
          Decision::Forward | Decision::Stage { .. } => {
              let expires_at = proposal.expires_at.min(bounds.expires_at);
              let label = ProvenanceLabel::peer(&proposal.proposer, &envelope.payload, expires_at, &stored.warrant.claims.id);
              ProposalDecision {
                  verdict: ProposalVerdict::Admitted,
                  reason: format!("{} is within the receiver's warrant; admitted as a proposal object. Nothing was granted and nothing was performed.", proposal.tool),
                  label: Some(label),
                  proposal: Some(proposal),
                  message_digest: digest,
              }
          }
      }
  }
  ```

  ```rust
  const PROPOSAL_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"warrantor-proposal-receipt-v1";

  /// Domain-separated, length-prefixed signing input — the same shape the warrant's own signature
  /// uses, so a receipt signature can never be replayed as anything else.
  fn signing_input(domain: &[u8], body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
      let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(domain.len() + body.len() + 16);
      out.extend_from_slice(&(domain.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
      out.extend_from_slice(domain);
      out.extend_from_slice(&(body.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
      out.extend_from_slice(body);
      out
  }

  /// The record of one admission decision: a MSG-syscall, DELEGATE-class decision.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  pub struct ProposalReceipt {
      pub format: String,
      pub syscall: String,
      pub decision_class: String,
      pub warrant_id: String,
      pub receiver: String,
      pub proposer: String,
      /// Hex of the key the message verified against. Recorded, not trusted: nothing pins it.
      pub proposer_key: String,
      pub population: String,
      pub task_lineage: Vec<String>,
      pub proposed_tool: String,
      pub message_digest: String,
      pub verdict: ProposalVerdict,
      /// Always false. Present so a reader is told, and so a value of true fails verification.
      pub authority_widened: bool,
      pub decided_at: u64,
  }

  /// Assemble the receipt for a decision. Never carries the reason sentence or the arguments.
  #[must_use]
  pub fn receipt_for(envelope: &ProposalEnvelope, stored: &StoredWarrant, decision: &ProposalDecision, now: u64) -> ProposalReceipt {
      let (population, task_lineage, proposed_tool) = decision.proposal.as_ref().map_or_else(
          || (String::new(), Vec::new(), String::new()),
          |p| (p.population.clone(), p.task_lineage.clone(), p.tool.clone()),
      );
      ProposalReceipt {
          format: PROPOSAL_RECEIPT_FORMAT.to_string(),
          syscall: MSG_SYSCALL.to_string(),
          decision_class: DELEGATE_DECISION_CLASS.to_string(),
          warrant_id: stored.warrant.claims.id.clone(),
          receiver: stored.warrant.claims.subject.clone(),
          proposer: envelope.message.sender.0.clone(),
          proposer_key: hex::encode(&envelope.message.verifying_key),
          population,
          task_lineage,
          proposed_tool,
          message_digest: decision.message_digest.clone(),
          verdict: decision.verdict.clone(),
          authority_widened: false,
          decided_at: now,
      }
  }

  /// A receipt plus the issuer's signature over its canonical digest.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  pub struct SignedProposalReceipt {
      pub format: String,
      pub receipt_digest: String,
      pub receipt: ProposalReceipt,
      pub signature_algorithm: String,
      pub signature_public_key: String,
      pub signature_value: String,
  }

  fn receipt_digest(receipt: &ProposalReceipt) -> Result<String, WarrantError> {
      let value = serde_json::to_value(receipt).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(e.to_string()))?;
      let text = serde_json::to_string(&canonicalize(&value)).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(e.to_string()))?;
      Ok(sha256_hex(text.as_bytes()))
  }

  /// Sign with the **issuer** key: admission grants nothing, so settle authority has no business here.
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// [`WarrantError::Encode`] if the receipt does not serialize.
  pub fn sign_receipt(receipt: ProposalReceipt, key: &SigningKey) -> Result<SignedProposalReceipt, WarrantError> {
      let digest = receipt_digest(&receipt)?;
      let signature = key.sign(&signing_input(PROPOSAL_DOMAIN, digest.as_bytes()));
      Ok(SignedProposalReceipt {
          format: PROPOSAL_EXPORT_FORMAT.to_string(),
          receipt_digest: digest,
          receipt,
          signature_algorithm: "Ed25519".to_string(),
          signature_public_key: hex::encode(key.verifying_key().to_bytes()),
          signature_value: hex::encode(signature.to_bytes()),
      })
  }

  fn decode_key(hex_key: &str) -> Result<VerifyingKey, WarrantError> {
      let raw = hex::decode(hex_key).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("public key hex: {e}")))?;
      let bytes: [u8; 32] = raw.as_slice().try_into().map_err(|_| WarrantError::SignatureInvalid)?;
      VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&bytes).map_err(|_| WarrantError::SignatureInvalid)
  }

  /// Verify against the key the file carries. Says nothing about whether that key is trusted.
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// [`WarrantError::UnknownFormat`], [`WarrantError::Invalid`] (digest or over-claim) or
  /// [`WarrantError::SignatureInvalid`].
  pub fn verify_receipt(signed: &SignedProposalReceipt) -> Result<(), WarrantError> {
      let key = decode_key(&signed.signature_public_key)?;
      verify_receipt_signed_by(signed, &key)
  }

  /// Verify against a key the caller pinned out of band.
  ///
  /// # Errors
  /// As [`verify_receipt`], plus [`WarrantError::SignatureInvalid`] when `key` is not the signer.
  pub fn verify_receipt_signed_by(signed: &SignedProposalReceipt, key: &VerifyingKey) -> Result<(), WarrantError> {
      if signed.format != PROPOSAL_EXPORT_FORMAT {
          return Err(WarrantError::UnknownFormat(signed.format.clone()));
      }
      if signed.receipt.format != PROPOSAL_RECEIPT_FORMAT {
          return Err(WarrantError::UnknownFormat(signed.receipt.format.clone()));
      }
      if signed.receipt.authority_widened {
          return Err(WarrantError::Invalid("a proposal receipt claims authority was widened; admission cannot widen authority".to_string()));
      }
      if signed.receipt.syscall != MSG_SYSCALL || signed.receipt.decision_class != DELEGATE_DECISION_CLASS {
          return Err(WarrantError::Invalid(format!("receipt is {}/{}; a proposal receipt is {MSG_SYSCALL}/{DELEGATE_DECISION_CLASS}", signed.receipt.syscall, signed.receipt.decision_class)));
      }
      let actual = receipt_digest(&signed.receipt)?;
      if actual != signed.receipt_digest {
          return Err(WarrantError::Invalid(format!("receipt digest is {actual}, file says {}", signed.receipt_digest)));
      }
      if hex::encode(key.to_bytes()) != signed.signature_public_key {
          return Err(WarrantError::SignatureInvalid);
      }
      let raw = hex::decode(&signed.signature_value).map_err(|_| WarrantError::SignatureInvalid)?;
      let bytes: [u8; 64] = raw.as_slice().try_into().map_err(|_| WarrantError::SignatureInvalid)?;
      let signature = ed25519_dalek::Signature::from_bytes(&bytes);
      key.verify(&signing_input(PROPOSAL_DOMAIN, signed.receipt_digest.as_bytes()), &signature)
          .map_err(|_| WarrantError::SignatureInvalid)
  }

  /// `<root>/proposals/<warrant-id>/<n>.json`, one file per decision, n zero-padded so the
  /// directory lists in decision order.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  pub struct ProposalStore {
      root: PathBuf,
  }

  impl ProposalStore {
      /// # Errors
      /// [`WarrantError::Encode`] if the directory cannot be created.
      pub fn open(root: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self, WarrantError> {
          let root = root.as_ref().join("proposals");
          std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("create proposals dir: {e}")))?;
          Ok(Self { root })
      }

      fn dir(&self, warrant_id: &str) -> PathBuf {
          self.root.join(warrant_id)
      }

      /// # Errors
      /// [`WarrantError::Encode`] on serialization or I/O failure.
      pub fn save(&self, signed: &SignedProposalReceipt) -> Result<PathBuf, WarrantError> {
          let dir = self.dir(&signed.receipt.warrant_id);
          std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("create {}: {e}", dir.display())))?;
          let index = self.list(&signed.receipt.warrant_id)?.len();
          let path = dir.join(format!("{index:06}.json"));
          let body = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(signed).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(e.to_string()))?;
          std::fs::write(&path, body).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("write {}: {e}", path.display())))?;
          Ok(path)
      }

      /// Every receipt for a warrant, in decision order. A file that will not parse is an error,
      /// not a gap: a missing receipt is the one thing this store must never read as "nothing".
      ///
      /// # Errors
      /// [`WarrantError::Encode`] on an unreadable directory or an unparseable file.
      pub fn list(&self, warrant_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<SignedProposalReceipt>, WarrantError> {
          let dir = self.dir(warrant_id);
          if !dir.try_exists().map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(e.to_string()))? {
              return Ok(Vec::new());
          }
          let mut paths: Vec<PathBuf> = std::fs::read_dir(&dir)
              .map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("read {}: {e}", dir.display())))?
              .filter_map(Result::ok)
              .map(|entry| entry.path())
              .filter(|p| p.extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "json"))
              .collect();
          paths.sort();
          paths
              .iter()
              .map(|path| {
                  let body = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("read {}: {e}", path.display())))?;
                  serde_json::from_slice(&body).map_err(|e| WarrantError::Encode(format!("{} is not a proposal receipt: {e}", path.display())))
              })
              .collect()
      }

      /// The replay set: every message digest already decided for this warrant.
      ///
      /// # Errors
      /// As [`Self::list`].
      pub fn seen_digests(&self, warrant_id: &str) -> Result<BTreeSet<String>, WarrantError> {
          Ok(self.list(warrant_id)?.into_iter().map(|s| s.receipt.message_digest).collect())
      }
  }
  ```

  ```rust
  fn cmd_proposal(args: &Args, store: &WarrantStore, root: &Path) -> ExitCode {
      match args.positional.first().map(String::as_str) {
          Some("compose") => cmd_proposal_compose(args),
          Some("admit") => cmd_proposal_admit(args, store, root),
          Some("list") => cmd_proposal_list(args, root),
          _ => fail("usage: warrantor proposal compose ... | admit <warrant-id> <envelope.json> [--export <path>] | list <warrant-id>"),
      }
  }

  fn proposal_class(word: &str) -> Result<SideEffectClass, String> {
      match word {
          "read" => Ok(SideEffectClass::Read),
          "write" => Ok(SideEffectClass::Write),
          "destructive" => Ok(SideEffectClass::Destructive),
          "financial" => Ok(SideEffectClass::Financial),
          other => Err(format!("--class {other:?} is not one of read, write, destructive, financial")),
      }
  }

  /// The peer's signing key: a 64-hex-character file, created if absent. Not a KeyKind, on purpose:
  /// it is a PEER's key, held wherever the peer runs, and this verb exists so a test and an operator
  /// can produce an envelope without a second binary. Nothing here pins it; the admit side says so.
  fn load_or_create_peer_key(path: &Path) -> Result<warrantor_trust_core::signing::SigningKeyWrapper, String> {
      if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(path) {
          let raw = hex::decode(text.trim()).map_err(|e| format!("{}: not hex: {e}", path.display()))?;
          let bytes: [u8; 32] = raw.as_slice().try_into().map_err(|_| format!("{}: a peer key is 32 bytes", path.display()))?;
          return Ok(warrantor_trust_core::signing::SigningKeyWrapper::from_bytes(&bytes));
      }
      let mut csprng = ed25519_dalek::rand_core::UnwrapErr(getrandom::SysRng);
      let generated = SigningKey::generate(&mut csprng);
      if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
          std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| format!("create {}: {e}", parent.display()))?;
      }
      std::fs::write(path, hex::encode(generated.to_bytes())).map_err(|e| format!("write {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
      eprintln!("warrantor: generated a new peer signing key at {}. Protect it: whoever holds it signs as this peer.", path.display());
      Ok(warrantor_trust_core::signing::SigningKeyWrapper::from_bytes(&generated.to_bytes()))
  }

  fn cmd_proposal_compose(args: &Args) -> ExitCode {
      let Some(receiver) = args.positional.get(1) else {
          return fail("usage: warrantor proposal compose <receiver-warrant-id> --from <spiffe-id> --population <p> --tool <t> --key-file <path> --out <file>");
      };
      let required = |name: &str| -> Result<String, String> {
          match args.flags.get(name) {
              Some(v) if v != "true" => Ok(v.clone()),
              _ => Err(format!("--{name} is required")),
          }
      };
      let (from, population, tool, key_file, out) = match (required("from"), required("population"), required("tool"), required("key-file"), required("out")) {
          (Ok(a), Ok(b), Ok(c), Ok(d), Ok(e)) => (a, b, c, d, e),
          (Err(e), ..) | (_, Err(e), ..) | (_, _, Err(e), ..) | (_, _, _, Err(e), _) | (_, _, _, _, Err(e)) => return fail(&e),
      };
      let mut arguments = BTreeMap::new();
      for raw in args.all("arg") {
          let Some((k, v)) = raw.split_once('=') else {
              return fail(&format!("--arg takes k=v, got {raw:?}"));
          };
          arguments.insert(k.to_string(), serde_json::Value::String(v.to_string()));
      }
      let side_effect = match args.flags.get("class").map(String::as_str).map_or(Ok(SideEffectClass::Read), proposal_class) {
          Ok(c) => c,
          Err(e) => return fail(&e),
      };
      let expires_in = match args.flags.get("expires-in").map(|v| v.parse::<u64>()) {
          None => 600,
          Some(Ok(n)) if n > 0 => n,
          Some(_) => return fail("--expires-in takes a positive number of seconds"),
      };
      let sequence = match args.flags.get("sequence").map(|v| v.parse::<u64>()) {
          None => 0,
          Some(Ok(n)) => n,
          Some(Err(_)) => return fail("--sequence takes a whole number"),
      };
      let signer = match load_or_create_peer_key(Path::new(&key_file)) {
          Ok(k) => k,
          Err(e) => return fail(&e),
      };
      let at = now();
      let proposal = provenance::PeerProposal {
          format: provenance::PROPOSAL_FORMAT.to_string(),
          proposer: from,
          population,
          task_lineage: args.all("lineage").to_vec(),
          tool,
          arguments,
          side_effect,
          expires_at: at + expires_in,
      };
      let envelope = match provenance::compose(&proposal, receiver, sequence, at, &signer) {
          Ok(e) => e,
          Err(e) => return fail(&e.to_string()),
      };
      let body = match serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&envelope) {
          Ok(b) => b,
          Err(e) => return fail(&e.to_string()),
      };
      if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(&out, body) {
          return fail(&format!("write {out}: {e}"));
      }
      println!("composed  {out}\n  proposer    {}\n  to warrant  {receiver}\n  proposes    {}", proposal.proposer, proposal.tool);
      ExitCode::SUCCESS
  }

  fn cmd_proposal_admit(args: &Args, store: &WarrantStore, root: &Path) -> ExitCode {
      let (Some(id), Some(path)) = (args.positional.get(1), args.positional.get(2)) else {
          return fail("usage: warrantor proposal admit <warrant-id> <envelope.json> [--export <path>]");
      };
      let stored = match store.load(id) {
          Ok(s) => s,
          Err(e) => return fail(&e.to_string()),
      };
      let body = match std::fs::read(path) {
          Ok(b) => b,
          Err(e) => return fail(&format!("read {path}: {e}")),
      };
      let envelope: provenance::ProposalEnvelope = match serde_json::from_slice(&body) {
          Ok(e) => e,
          Err(e) => return fail(&format!("{path} is not a proposal envelope: {e}")),
      };
      let proposals = match provenance::ProposalStore::open(root) {
          Ok(p) => p,
          Err(e) => return fail(&e.to_string()),
      };
      let seen = match proposals.seen_digests(id) {
          Ok(s) => s,
          Err(e) => return fail(&format!("cannot read earlier decisions, so replay is unknown: {e}")),
      };
      let issuer = match load_or_create_key(&root.join("keys/issuer.key"), KeyKind::Issuer) {
          Ok(k) => k,
          Err(e) => return fail(&e),
      };
      let at = now();
      let decision = provenance::admit(&envelope, &stored, &seen, at);
      let signed = match provenance::sign_receipt(provenance::receipt_for(&envelope, &stored, &decision, at), &issuer) {
          Ok(s) => s,
          Err(e) => return fail(&format!("decided, but the receipt could not be signed: {e}")),
      };
      let kept = match proposals.save(&signed) {
          Ok(p) => p,
          Err(e) => return fail(&format!("decided, but the receipt was not kept: {e}")),
      };
      let verdict = match &signed.receipt.verdict {
          provenance::ProposalVerdict::Admitted => "admitted".to_string(),
          provenance::ProposalVerdict::RefusedAtAdmission { gate } => format!("refused at admission ({gate})"),
          provenance::ProposalVerdict::RefusedAtBind { bound } => format!("refused at bind ({bound})"),
      };
      println!("{verdict}  {}", signed.receipt_digest);
      println!("  warrant     {id}");
      println!("  proposer    {}  (key {}; NOT pinned -- integrity verified, identity not established)", signed.receipt.proposer, &signed.receipt.proposer_key[..16]);
      println!("  proposes    {}", if signed.receipt.proposed_tool.is_empty() { "(payload not read)" } else { signed.receipt.proposed_tool.as_str() });
      println!("  {}", decision.reason);
      println!("  authority   unchanged. Admission grants nothing and performs nothing; the receiver decides each call against its own warrant when it acts.");
      println!("  kept at     {}", kept.display());
      if let Some(export) = args.flags.get("export") {
          if export == "true" {
              return fail("--export needs a file path");
          }
          if let Err(e) = write_export_anchored(&signed, Path::new(export), root, id, anchor::Anchored::Proposal) {
              return fail(&e);
          }
          println!("\nexported  {export}");
      }
      if matches!(signed.receipt.verdict, provenance::ProposalVerdict::Admitted) { ExitCode::SUCCESS } else { ExitCode::FAILURE }
  }

  fn cmd_proposal_list(args: &Args, root: &Path) -> ExitCode {
      let Some(id) = args.positional.get(1) else {
          return fail("usage: warrantor proposal list <warrant-id>");
      };
      let proposals = match provenance::ProposalStore::open(root).and_then(|p| p.list(id)) {
          Ok(list) => list,
          Err(e) => return fail(&e.to_string()),
      };
      if proposals.is_empty() {
          println!("No proposals decided for {id}.");
          return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
      }
      for signed in proposals {
          println!("{:<10} {:<14} {:<40} {}", signed.receipt.decided_at, match &signed.receipt.verdict {
              provenance::ProposalVerdict::Admitted => "admitted".to_string(),
              provenance::ProposalVerdict::RefusedAtAdmission { gate } => format!("refused:{gate}"),
              provenance::ProposalVerdict::RefusedAtBind { bound } => format!("bind:{bound}"),
          }, signed.receipt.proposer, signed.receipt.proposed_tool);
      }
      ExitCode::SUCCESS
  }

  fn verify_proposal_export(path: &str, body: &[u8], anchor: Option<&Anchor>) -> ExitCode {
      let signed: provenance::SignedProposalReceipt = match serde_json::from_slice(body) {
          Ok(s) => s,
          Err(e) => return fail(&format!("{path} is not an exported warrantor proposal receipt: {e}")),
      };
      let checked = match anchor {
          Some(anchor) => provenance::verify_receipt_signed_by(&signed, &anchor.key),
          None => provenance::verify_receipt(&signed),
      };
      if let Err(e) = checked {
          return fail(&format!("{path} does NOT verify: {e}"));
      }
      println!("verified  {}", signed.receipt_digest);
      println!("  warrant       {}", signed.receipt.warrant_id);
      println!("  syscall       {} ({}-class decision)", signed.receipt.syscall, signed.receipt.decision_class);
      println!("  proposer      {}", signed.receipt.proposer);
      println!("  proposed      {}", signed.receipt.proposed_tool);
      println!("  verdict       {:?}", signed.receipt.verdict);
      println!("  authority     {}", if signed.receipt.authority_widened { "WIDENED (this cannot verify)" } else { "unchanged" });
      println!("  signed by     {}", signed.signature_public_key);
      println!("  anchor        {}", anchor_line(anchor));
      println!("  - the proposer's key is recorded, not pinned: integrity is verified, identity is not established");
      if anchor.is_none() {
          println!("  - {NO_ANCHOR_LIMITATION}");
      }
      ExitCode::SUCCESS
  }
  ```

  ```rust
  #[test]
  fn the_cli_round_trip_composes_admits_exports_and_verifies_offline() {
      use std::process::Command;
      use warrantor_warrant::store::WarrantStore;
      let root = tempdir("cli");
      let store = WarrantStore::open(&root).expect("store");
      store.create(&stored_open("w-cli", &["selftest.echo"])).expect("create");
      let bin = env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_warrantor");
      let envelope = root.join("envelope.json");
      let composed = Command::new(bin)
          .args(["proposal", "compose", "w-cli", "--from", PEER, "--population", "agent", "--tool", "selftest.echo", "--arg", "text=hi", "--lineage", "task-root", "--key-file"])
          .arg(root.join("peer.key"))
          .arg("--out")
          .arg(&envelope)
          .arg("--root")
          .arg(&root)
          .output()
          .expect("run compose");
      assert!(composed.status.success(), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&composed.stderr));
      let export = root.join("receipt.json");
      let admitted = Command::new(bin)
          .args(["proposal", "admit", "w-cli"])
          .arg(&envelope)
          .arg("--export")
          .arg(&export)
          .arg("--root")
          .arg(&root)
          .output()
          .expect("run admit");
      let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&admitted.stdout);
      assert!(admitted.status.success(), "{stdout}{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&admitted.stderr));
      assert!(stdout.starts_with("admitted"), "{stdout}");
      assert!(stdout.contains("NOT pinned"), "the CLI must say identity is not established: {stdout}");
      let verified = Command::new(bin).args(["verify"]).arg(&export).arg("--root").arg(&root).output().expect("run verify");
      let out = String::from_utf8_lossy(&verified.stdout);
      assert!(verified.status.success(), "{out}{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&verified.stderr));
      assert!(out.contains("syscall       msg (delegate-class decision)"), "{out}");
      assert!(out.contains("authority     unchanged"), "{out}");
      // A second admit of the same envelope is a replay, and exits non-zero.
      let replay = Command::new(bin).args(["proposal", "admit", "w-cli"]).arg(&envelope).arg("--root").arg(&root).output().expect("run admit again");
      assert!(!replay.status.success());
      assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&replay.stdout).contains("refused at admission (replay)"));
  }
  ```

**Sequencing notes.** Task 2.1's effect registry spells the message syscall `msg` and the delegation syscall `delegate`; the two string constants here are those words, so when that registry lands the receipt's `syscall` and `decision_class` fields need no format change — a later task may replace the constants with the registry's own spelling function in one line. Task 2.3's staged receipts and this task's proposal receipts are independent: both sign with the issuer key and both verify through `warrantor verify`'s format dispatch, and neither reads the other's files. Task 3.1's principals are the only thing that can turn "key recorded" into "identity established"; nothing here should be promoted before that.

## Phase 3 — Identity, custody, recorder, machine-speed response

> **Status of this phase.** Expanded 2026-09-02 from the spine's task stubs to task-structural form: anchor,
> verified crate provenance, files, interfaces, ordered test-first Steps, exit gate and hazards. It is one level
> less granular than Phases 0-2 in exactly one respect — **it does not quote verbatim error strings, rustfmt hunks
> or line ranges**, because those must be captured by running the commands against the tree and inventing them
> would be the precise failure this repository has a doctrine against. Capturing them is Step 0 of each task and is
> mechanical. Do not skip it.

> **Provenance finding, verified 2026-09-02 against `origin/main` (`git ls-tree --name-only origin/main rust/`).**
> `origin/main` declares **40** workspace members. Of the crates this phase wires, `credential-vault`,
> `flight-recorder` and `containment-conformance` **are** on `origin/main`; `agent-identity-graph`, `tenancy`,
> `capability-tokens`, `revocation-verbs` and `harness-floor` **are not** — they exist only in the dirty
> `docs/content-program-p9-fold` working tree, untracked. Every task below that names an absent crate inherits
> Task 0.1's full shape: carry the crate in, add the member line, regenerate the lock with `cargo metadata` (never
> by hand), expect `cargo fmt --check` to fail on first contact, and only then wire it. A task that assumes the
> crate is already buildable will fail at its first cargo invocation.

**Phase entry condition.** Phase 2 complete. The effect decomposition registry (L4-01) exists, so `MUTATE` and
`EXEC` are addressable syscalls rather than adapter-specific special cases; Task 3.6 depends on that.

**Phase exit gate (from the phase map).** A red-team agent with root inside its own workload cannot forge a
verifying chain (this is the L0-05 seed; the full adversary is Task 5.3), and a seeded trigger fires its mapped
containment verb within a stated bound with no operator in the path.
